LLqzdeta7Y.one_liner: Proper learner for normalized bias-free narrow ReLU networks under Gaussian inputs using a nonlinear label-distance statistic and rotation.
LLqzdeta7Y.problem: Cancellation among signed neurons complicates uniform learning guarantees for narrow ReLU networks.
LLqzdeta7Y.method: A proper learner for width-k normalized, bias-free networks under Gaussian inputs without separation assumptions. First-moment control and a scaled nonlinear label-distance statistic lower-bound a second-moment signal using residual variance, and a norm-preserving rotation ensures approximation by at most k units in the original class.
LLqzdeta7Y.key_idea: Combine first-moment control with a scaled nonlinear label-distance statistic to lower-bound a second-moment signal by residual variance, then apply a norm-preserving rotation to keep the output proper.
LLqzdeta7Y.evidence: Theoretical proof only: sample and time bounds for width k and squared L2 error epsilon from noiseless Gaussian examples; no experiments are mentioned.
LLqzdeta7Y.claimed_gains: Uses g(k) eps^(-O(k^2)) O~(d) noiseless examples and g(k) eps^(-O(k^2)) O~(d^2) real-arithmetic operations, so at fixed width sample complexity is nearly linear and running time nearly quadratic in dimension.
LLqzdeta7Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result answers an open question posed by Chen et al. with a technically coherent proof that handles signed-neuron cancellation.
LLqzdeta7Y.main_concern: The guarantees say little about dependence on width k (k stays in the exponent of 1/epsilon with an unspecified g(k)), and the proof is hard to follow with the algorithm described only in Section 6.

4pw2hIrq0U.one_liner: Pretrained set-transformer and conditional-flow model for in-context Bayesian GLMM inference, refined by Independence Metropolis-Hastings or used to warm-start NUTS.
4pw2hIrq0U.problem: Bayesian inference for GLMMs needs MCMC, and the No-U-Turn Sampler is slow and must restart from scratch for every new dataset, model, and prior specification.
4pw2hIrq0U.method: MetaBeta takes the full prior and model specification as context at test time, using two set transformers and two conditional neural spline flows that mirror the GLMM hierarchy (global parameters shared across groups, local parameters per group), trained jointly on millions of simulated datasets. The flow posterior is refined by Independence Metropolis-Hastings against the unnormalized posterior, or used to warm-start NUTS.
4pw2hIrq0U.key_idea: Amortize GLMM posteriors with prior-conditioned set-transformer encoders and spline flows, then correct the flow with Independence Metropolis-Hastings to retain asymptotic exactness.
4pw2hIrq0U.evidence: Training on millions of simulated datasets with continuous, binary, and count outcomes, and controlled benchmarks with ground-truth parameters comparing against NUTS on parameter recovery and calibration.
4pw2hIrq0U.claimed_gains: Warm-starting NUTS gives nearly identical inference 3.5-13x faster than cold-started NUTS and removes over 98% of NUTS' divergent transitions.
4pw2hIrq0U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining a prior-amortized pretrained model with MCMC-based exactness, scaled to a well-specified GLMM class, is a significant step for amortized Bayesian inference, with a clear description of task and method.
4pw2hIrq0U.main_concern: One reviewer finds that related work understates prior art for the two core ideas (prior amortization and MCMC-exactness correction), and another says the practical need for a pretrained model is not sufficiently justified.

kbXAX8Ig9G.one_liner: Audio restoration model combining per-domain headroom-anchored RL post-training with Condition-Swap Guidance to curb hallucination
kbXAX8Ig9G.problem: Generative universal audio restoration can hallucinate content unsupported by the degraded input, and uniform reward post-training and classifier-free guidance each have a specific weakness.
kbXAX8Ig9G.method: Headroom-Anchored RL tracks each audio domain separately and shifts a domain back toward a supervised target once its reward signals become unreliable, while Condition-Swap Guidance replaces the CFG null reference with a permuted copy of the input's own conditioning segments (same content, wrong timing).
kbXAX8Ig9G.key_idea: Gate RL updates per domain by reward headroom with a supervised fallback, and use a time-permuted copy of the input's own conditioning as the negative reference in guidance.
kbXAX8Ig9G.evidence: One model across speech, singing and music, a listening study against AnyEnhance, a comparison of CSG with Self-Swap Guidance (Table 3), and transfer of CSG to other restoration models including image restoration.
kbXAX8Ig9G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the complementary training-time and inference-time mechanisms are useful, CSG needs no retraining and transfers to other models, and the listening study favors it over AnyEnhance.
kbXAX8Ig9G.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited relative to prior work (CSG modifies Self-Swap Guidance, Headroom-Anchored RL resembles supervised-anchored RL), and content-fidelity validation is thin, with speech WER above the noisy input.

KegWkHURAG.one_liner: Exact sampling from p_i^k using only samples, via collision maps composed backward in time with coupling from the past.
KegWkHURAG.problem: Sampling at temperature 1/k from samples alone is either exact but slow (rejection sampling needs Theta(n^(k-1)) samples) or fast but biased (first-collision shortcut, Theta(n^(1-1/k))).
KegWkHURAG.method: Defines a collision map, a random update built from one k-fold collision and earlier outcomes, proves it preserves the target distribution, and composes these maps backward in time (Collision-map CFTP) without knowing the probabilities or the support. It returns an exact output after a bounded expected number of collisions.
KegWkHURAG.key_idea: A collision map that provably preserves the target p^k distribution is composed backward in time with coupling from the past, needing no knowledge of probabilities or support.
KegWkHURAG.evidence: Proofs of instance-optimal sample complexity with a matching lower bound up to a constant depending on k, all theorems verified in Lean 4 per the TL;DR, and synthetic experiments (k=2 on uniform supports and one four-label distribution per a review).
KegWkHURAG.claimed_gains: Exact output needing only a constant factor more samples than the biased collision shortcut, at collision scale Theta(n^(1-1/k)) versus Theta(n^(k-1)) for rejection sampling.
KegWkHURAG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical result is strong: exact sampling at the collision scale without knowing the probabilities or support, with a matching lower bound showing instance-optimality up to a constant.
KegWkHURAG.main_concern: The empirical evaluation is narrow (synthetic, mostly k=2, little on the LLM-reasoning motivation) and novelty relative to prior exact-sampling frameworks such as Dice Enterprise is not clearly positioned.

cmznEFc4Wo.one_liner: Active Taskless Distillation transfers a private update's capability through single-word teacher responses at prompts where the public model is near-tied.
cmznEFc4Wo.problem: Private post-training updates can leak capability-relevant information through behavior on unrelated inputs, but prior subliminal-learning methods are computationally heavy and mostly transfer superficial traits or preferences.
cmznEFc4Wo.method: ATD uses the public ancestor model to find prompts where it assigns nearly equal probability to two ordinary words, where a small private update may flip the preferred word. It collects one greedy word per prompt from the private teacher and trains the student only on these prompt-word pairs.
cmznEFc4Wo.key_idea: Select prompts where the public model is near-tied between two words, so one greedy teacher word reveals the direction of the private update's gradient.
cmznEFc4Wo.evidence: Primary coding experiment on Qwen2.5-1.5B evaluated on HumanEval+ against control arms, plus tests on Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.2-1B; reviews cite 4 seeds and 164 test items.
cmznEFc4Wo.claimed_gains: A student trained on 5,664 single-word teacher responses gains 5.34 pp on HumanEval+ over a control trained on the same responses with disrupted (text cut off in the abstract).
cmznEFc4Wo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and clearly motivated, and credit extending subliminal transfer from traits to a code-verified capability using only black-box single-token teacher access.
cmznEFc4Wo.main_concern: Gains are modest and statistically thin (confidence intervals include zero on the other three model families, 164 test items), and the setting requires teacher and student to share the same public ancestor.

GCJ61TFZDZ.one_liner: Proves alternating gradient descent-ascent has O(1/T) ergodic duality-gap convergence in every finite two-player zero-sum matrix game.
GCJ61TFZDZ.problem: Prior AltGDA theory applies only to unconstrained settings or requires restrictive equilibrium assumptions in constrained settings.
GCJ61TFZDZ.method: A Lyapunov-based proof inspired by numerical results from a performance estimation programming (PEP) framework for Lyapunov function search over compact convex sets, with counterexamples for last-iterate convergence and a Lean 4 formalization.
GCJ61TFZDZ.key_idea: Find a Lyapunov function via PEP over compact convex sets and control simplex-boundary projection effects, giving uniform-average O(1/T) duality-gap bounds for every initialization and horizon.
GCJ61TFZDZ.evidence: Theoretical proof of the global ergodic rate, simple counterexamples showing the last-iterate duality gap does not converge to zero, and a machine-checked Lean 4 formalization.
GCJ61TFZDZ.claimed_gains: AltGDA converges at an O(1/T) ergodic rate in every finite two-player zero-sum matrix game, for every initialization and every horizon T.
GCJ61TFZDZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the result is a significant theoretical contribution that removes the restrictive equilibrium assumptions of prior work.
GCJ61TFZDZ.main_concern: The stepsize condition depends on the Goldman-Tucker separation constant delta, which may be unknown, limiting practical applicability, and the PEP-based Lyapunov section is hard to follow.

WVDtPAWKQk.one_liner: UnderRTL is a benchmark testing whether RTL representations capture functional equivalence and implementation quality using verified equivalent designs.
WVDtPAWKQk.problem: Existing evaluations of RTL representations assess functional behavior and implementation quality separately and on different designs, leaving their interaction unclear.
WVDtPAWKQk.method: UnderRTL builds on 7,075 curated RTL designs with verified functional variants, synthesis-based PPA labels across multiple PDKs and constraints, and natural-language queries for six linked tasks. Functionally equivalent implementations link the two axes, and 24 engineered-feature, text, graph, and multimodal methods are evaluated under standardized protocols.
WVDtPAWKQk.key_idea: Use formally equivalent RTL implementations with differing synthesized PPA to measure functional invariance and implementation sensitivity on the same designs.
WVDtPAWKQk.evidence: Evaluation of 24 methods on six linked tasks over 7,075 designs; the abstract reports task-dependent limitations in both capabilities and weak transfer to unseen designs.
WVDtPAWKQk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the curated 7k+ design dataset, the equivalence-controlled PPA comparisons, and data controls such as source-level splits, deduplication, formal checks, and distance matching.
WVDtPAWKQk.main_concern: Reproducibility details are missing, notably reset and initial-state assumptions for sequential equivalence checking, power switching-activity assumptions, and training and feature-extraction settings.

065FIfNFMS.one_liner: Attention-based selection of a reference IPM iterate plus neural primal-dual adjustment warm-starts interior-point solvers for parametric nonlinear programs.
065FIfNFMS.problem: Warm-starting interior-point methods needs a start that is not only near-optimal but also strictly interior and sufficiently central, which primal-only learned warm starts do not guarantee.
065FIfNFMS.method: WSNet reuses the IPM trajectory of a solved reference instance: an attention-based stage selects a promising iterate, and an adjustment stage refines its primal-dual variables for the new instance with a learned dual correction, finite-step residual minimization, and complementarity-based losses that promote centrality.
065FIfNFMS.key_idea: Select an intermediate iterate from a reference IPM trajectory by attention, then train a primal-dual correction with complementarity losses so the start is interior and central.
065FIfNFMS.evidence: Experiments on synthetic and public datasets accelerating IPOPT, plus a theoretical result that mini-batch training yields strictly interior primal-dual points for training instances with high probability under stated assumptions.
065FIfNFMS.claimed_gains: Reduces IPOPT iteration count by up to 77.8%; the rest of the sentence is cut off in the input.
065FIfNFMS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see IPM warm-starting as an important practical problem and value building a full primal-dual start trained for interiority and centrality, with improvements on some problem types.
065FIfNFMS.main_concern: Benchmarks are small, synthetic, and narrow (random data, nonconvexity only through a sin term), so transfer to real application problems is untested, and the theory is seen as existential.

hmN5cCDcfT.one_liner: Chooses synthetic price-path generator settings by their measured utility gap over replaced real windows, for financial foundation-model adaptation.
hmN5cCDcfT.problem: Under a fixed adaptation budget each synthetic window displaces a real one, so a realistic synthetic path can still hurt the adapted model, and realism-based generator evaluation ignores this trade-off.
hmN5cCDcfT.method: UGapSyn defines the utility gap as the reduction in forecasting risk relative to the same adaptation without replacement, measured by continuing adaptation from a shared state with synthetic or real windows at the replaced positions. It selects the configuration of a controllable GARCH-jump generator by the gap on validation data, with an optional safeguard that adjusts synthetic data during adaptation when repeated historical measurements agree.
hmN5cCDcfT.key_idea: Score each synthetic configuration by paired continuations from a shared model state with and without replacing real windows, and keep the setting with the largest forecasting-risk reduction.
hmN5cCDcfT.evidence: Three foundation models on two US equity panels and one Chinese panel (nine settings), compared with real-data adaptation and five synthesis and condensation baselines.
hmN5cCDcfT.claimed_gains: Lower mean test MSE than real-data adaptation in all nine settings and than all five synthesis and condensation baselines on both US panels for every model; the Chronos-Bolt-Base figure is cut off in the input.
hmN5cCDcfT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the utility-gap framing well motivated, since it compares a synthetic window with the real window it displaces, and the paired-continuation protocol controls unrelated training variation.
hmN5cCDcfT.main_concern: The runtime revision safeguard adds little over the fixed configuration and historical utility transfers poorly across periods; reviewers also question baseline fairness (fixed 50% replacement) and per-asset replacement.

MgCKbUEueu.one_liner: Learns per-view edge weights under a cross-domain alignment loss, boosting edges carrying shared information and suppressing domain-specific ones.
MgCKbUEueu.problem: Message passing over fixed edge weights aggregates domain- and view-specific information layer after layer into node representations that alignment must later reconcile.
MgCKbUEueu.method: CARE updates the edge weights of each relation view under the cross-domain alignment objective, with gradients flowing through graph propagation, strengthening edges that propagate shared information and suppressing domain- or view-specific ones; weights are bounded within [1-rho, 1+rho] per a review.
MgCKbUEueu.key_idea: Backpropagate the alignment loss through message passing to learn bounded edge weights per relation view for both source and target graphs.
MgCKbUEueu.evidence: Benchmark cross-network node classification tasks against baseline methods, with ablations including blocking alignment gradients to the edge-weighting module.
MgCKbUEueu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that guiding message-passing edge weights with the alignment objective is a reasonable, adaptive idea with consistent improvements and a useful ablation.
MgCKbUEueu.main_concern: The alignment objective has no negative pairs or class-conditional term and can collapse, and there is no direct evidence that learned edge weights favor shared over domain-specific information.

qufHfNKM6s.one_liner: Tests whether near-tied LLM rankings reverse under low-family-DIF item selection, compared with matched random subtests, using spectral MIRT and DIF.
qufHfNKM6s.problem: Small leaderboard gaps are read as model superiority, but the advantage may depend on items that favor particular model families after capability adjustment.
qufHfNKM6s.method: A family-label-free spectral approximation to MIRT plus residual DIF analysis: one uploader-disjoint half identifies low-DIF items that score models in the other half with frozen weights preserving group and easiness composition, against equally short matched-random subtests.
qufHfNKM6s.key_idea: Select items with low residual family DIF using a label-free spectral MIRT, then compare near-tie reversals against matched random subsampling baselines.
qufHfNKM6s.evidence: Five benchmarks with uploader-disjoint halves, matched-random baselines, and ablations over IRT models and model samples.
qufHfNKM6s.claimed_gains: Full-benchmark and low-DIF rankings stay strongly correlated (tau_b .900 to .948), yet in four of five benchmarks 30.9-47.1% of cross-family pairs within one point reverse, exceeding matched-random medians by 16.9-28.6 points (all p=.001).
qufHfNKM6s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is careful and goes beyond showing near-ties can flip, by measuring excess reversal over matched random subsets with extensive ablations.
qufHfNKM6s.main_concern: One reviewer found the paper hard to follow with unclear motivation and novelty, and effect sizes depend on the estimator (e.g., MMLU excess drops from about 24.4 to 9.2 points under direct logistic MIRT).

jbpfiDdn6c.one_liner: Coordinate-conditioned upsampler queries continuous coordinates to upsample frozen foundation-model features without materializing dense high-resolution grids
jbpfiDdn6c.problem: Vision foundation model features are spatially coarse, and existing feature upsamplers are tied to specific backbones or materialize dense feature grids, making high-resolution inference costly.
jbpfiDdn6c.method: CoordUp formulates feature upsampling as a coordinate-conditioned operator: a lightweight, feature-agnostic network answers queries at continuous output coordinates, so features can be streamed pointwise through a prediction head without storing the full-resolution map.
jbpfiDdn6c.key_idea: Upsampling is posed as pointwise queries at continuous output coordinates, so memory scales with the query batch rather than the output feature grid.
jbpfiDdn6c.evidence: Five frozen backbones and three high-resolution datasets for semantic segmentation and depth estimation, plus zero-shot transfer to the final activations of DA3 and SAM3.
jbpfiDdn6c.claimed_gains: CoordUp consistently improves boundary-sensitive metrics over previous encoder-agnostic upsamplers, and an 80 Mpx output uses only 8.6 GB of GPU memory.
jbpfiDdn6c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the coordinate-query design scales to very high resolutions with low memory and a small parameter count.
jbpfiDdn6c.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited because the design choices appear in prior upsamplers (NAF, LoftUp), gains on DA3 and SAM3 are small, and no VAE backbones are tested.

9fMtruZwWM.one_liner: Aligns a pocket-conditioned generator's denoiser features to a machine-learned interatomic potential through an equivariant projector to improve molecule validity
9fMtruZwWM.problem: Structure-based generative models trained on crystal and docked structures receive only geometric supervision and lack information about the energy landscape and atomic forces, so they struggle with fine-grained physical constraints.
9fMtruZwWM.method: An equivariant projector matches features of a denoiser layer to latent features of a pretrained machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) during training, giving the generator a dense, physically grounded signal. The approach is applied to two pocket-conditioned generators, DrugFlow and FLOWR.
9fMtruZwWM.key_idea: Representation alignment between a denoiser layer, via an equivariant projector, and atom-wise MLIP latent features supplies physics-aware supervision beyond geometry.
9fMtruZwWM.evidence: Two pocket-conditioned generators (DrugFlow and FLOWR) on CrossDocked2020 and SPINDR test sets, with three-seed averages and ablations over MLIP teachers, encoder types, layers, and loss weights.
9fMtruZwWM.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract reports significantly improved structural validity and, across two generators, greater substructure overlap with native ligands and improved protein-ligand interaction.
9fMtruZwWM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the physics-aware supervision is well defined and timely, representation alignment is under-explored for molecular generators, and results hold across two architectures with useful ablations.
9fMtruZwWM.main_concern: Reviewers say the cross-architecture physical-quality claims exceed the evidence, since FLOWR raw strain rises from 92.4 to 101.1 kcal/mol and improvements are not consistently significant.

FYP80cTIdc.one_liner: Drafter injects each predecessor's predicted feature into its successor at every layer, conditioning parallel speculative drafts through depth.
FYP80cTIdc.problem: Parallel speculative drafting selects tokens independently, producing inconsistent continuations that shorten the accepted prefix, and existing methods apply conditional decoding only in a lightweight module after the backbone.
FYP80cTIdc.method: DSpine adds gated adjacent injection at every backbone layer so each position's predicted feature is written into its successor while all positions update in parallel. A unified transfer space from the target model's output embeddings ties layer-wise injection to final conditional decoding, with layer-wise output-embedding supervision and fused kernels plus a transition cache in SGLang.
FYP80cTIdc.key_idea: Gated adjacent injection at every layer propagates each predecessor's predicted feature to its successor, unfolding the causal conditioning chain over network depth while positions update in parallel.
FYP80cTIdc.evidence: Mathematics, coding, and conversation benchmarks on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B under greedy and sampled decoding, SGLang serving throughput, and diagnostic analyses of shallow-layer predictions with ablations.
FYP80cTIdc.claimed_gains: Mean acceptance length of Qwen3-8B under greedy decoding rises from 3.77 with DFlash to 4.82 (+27.8%), and the abstract also reports 23.3% higher SGLang performance (text cut off).
FYP80cTIdc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is well motivated by diagnostics and consistently beats strong parallel-drafting baselines on acceptance length and, under greedy decoding, throughput.
FYP80cTIdc.main_concern: Ablations are thin: they do not isolate all-layer injection from final-layer-only conditioning or from the block-causal attention change, and evaluation covers only Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B.

AU3xgZmeHw.one_liner: Latent RL policy learns a non-negative muscle-synergy basis end-to-end from reward, with a Gram-determinant entropy correction keeping it well conditioned.
AU3xgZmeHw.problem: Musculoskeletal control has far more muscles than degrees of freedom, and existing synergy-based RL methods obtain their basis from a separate discovery phase, a dynamics model, or physiology rather than the task reward.
AU3xgZmeHw.method: Plexus constrains actions to non-negative combinations of synergy vectors and makes the basis a free parameter of the actor, learned jointly from reward. Entropy is measured on the induced action manifold through a Gram determinant correction to the log-density, which flows through the decoder.
AU3xgZmeHw.key_idea: Add a Gram-determinant correction to the log-density so entropy is measured on the induced action manifold, which keeps the jointly learned decoder basis from losing rank.
AU3xgZmeHw.evidence: Six MyoSuite tasks on two musculoskeletal models, compared with full-dimensional baselines and, per reviews, with Latent SAC without the correction across latent widths.
AU3xgZmeHw.claimed_gains: Across six MyoSuite tasks on two musculoskeletal models, Plexus matches or exceeds full-dimensional baselines on every task (the abstract is cut off after this).
AU3xgZmeHw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mismatch between latent and action entropy is a meaningful insight and that the correction, learned jointly with the decoder, improves over SAC baselines without it on nearly all tasks and latent widths.
AU3xgZmeHw.main_concern: Plexus's best results occur when the latent size equals the action size (K=A), so the evaluation does not show where compressed control with the correction is practically preferable.

nWHzHZ6NTw.one_liner: Derives minimax risk laws when k of n labels get nonlinear processing and the rest pass a fixed affine readout.
nWHzHZ6NTw.problem: Low-dimensional structure improves prediction from noisy observations but requires adaptation, and it is unclear how much benefit remains when adaptation is confined to an initial pilot sample.
nWHzHZ6NTw.method: For Gaussian observations of a known compact smooth manifold, the paper proves matching minimax bounds over the full pilot-then-affine class, attained by projection, mean correction, and normal shrinkage. It then extends to quadratic readouts, learned geometry, and conditional-moment low-rank readouts with a gain guarantee.
nWHzHZ6NTw.key_idea: Compare the geometric uncertainty left by the pilot sample with the noise in the remaining observations, yielding a staircase of risk constants set by derivative-space dimensions.
nWHzHZ6NTw.evidence: Minimax upper and lower bounds, simulations of the geometric laws, and captured-view image experiments evaluating configured low-rank readouts at matched capacity.
nWHzHZ6NTw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching upper and lower bounds are a substantial theoretical contribution and that the risk staircase explains why intrinsic dimension alone does not determine prediction risk.
nWHzHZ6NTw.main_concern: The practical connection is weak: the nonlinear label budget is hard to interpret from the introduction, results assume Gaussian observations of a known manifold while experiments use sparse pixels, and real-data results compare only against variants of the method.

Gw5ySwdrU1.one_liner: SMD distills few-step diffusion by regressing student interval velocities onto teacher velocities along student rollouts.
Gw5ySwdrU1.problem: Few-step distillation methods often need auxiliary score models, adversarial training, or specialized architectures, and the high-curvature teacher velocity field makes simple on-policy regression unstable.
Gw5ySwdrU1.method: The student's velocity is held constant within each sampling interval and matched to teacher velocities along student rollouts. A lightweight residual Pivot proxy, used only in training, models local velocity variation separately from the interval-mean prediction, and weaker teacher predictions act as negative references in a repulsive regularizer.
Gw5ySwdrU1.key_idea: On-policy velocity regression with a training-only Pivot residual network absorbing local curvature, plus a repulsive term pushing away from weaker teacher predictions.
Gw5ySwdrU1.evidence: Image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio-video generation, with models of up to 33 billion parameters, at 4 NFE.
Gw5ySwdrU1.claimed_gains: Using only 4 NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step methods, with no numeric gains visible in the truncated abstract.
Gw5ySwdrU1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the approach is simple, needs no online score model or adversarial training, and is validated broadly across image, video, and 3D generation.
Gw5ySwdrU1.main_concern: The contribution of the repulsive term is unclear (it reduces to an extrapolated teacher target, similar to a higher guidance scale), novelty over methods like PDD is incremental, and diversity and training stability relative to the teacher are not verified.

q3ecauFvlI.one_liner: Trajectory replay matches an updated velocity field to a frozen historical velocity on partial trajectories and to new-task velocities.
q3ecauFvlI.problem: Generative replay for continual learning needs full trajectory simulation at every step, and the resulting synthetic-sample errors are fit as training data and degrade the historical distribution.
q3ecauFvlI.method: The updated velocity field is trained to match both the frozen historical velocity along partially simulated trajectories and the incoming task's velocity, weighted by a stability-plasticity coefficient. The optimum averages the two velocities by density and generates the mixture of their probability paths, and mean velocity distillation lets historical trajectories be reached with few network evaluations.
q3ecauFvlI.key_idea: Regress velocities along partial historical trajectories so the optimum is the density-weighted average of old and new velocities, yielding the mixture of their probability paths.
q3ecauFvlI.evidence: Class-incremental image generation against generative replay and distillation baselines, and two biological case studies extending generative perturbation models to new contexts and experimental batches across two data modalities.
q3ecauFvlI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is intuitive and well motivated, with a clean optimality characterization, an extensive evaluation, and a well-motivated adaptive weighting schedule.
q3ecauFvlI.main_concern: Novelty over prior work (the cited Masip et al. 2025 baseline) is unclear, and comparisons do not isolate whether gains come from how replay states are obtained, the student's learning rule, or the batch allocation between old and new tasks.

yNOIjER6jB.one_liner: Provably secure LLM steganography for receivers lacking the sender's model or prompt, using coupling and an e-process for certified recovery.
yNOIjER6jB.problem: High-capacity provably secure steganography usually needs the receiver to reproduce the sender's token distribution with the same model and prompt, while token-only alternatives have low embedding rates or limited recovery reliability.
yNOIjER6jB.method: PACER separates the sender's token distribution from receiver-side recovery information. With a receiver-side distribution it combines maximal coupling with token-class coupling; otherwise token-class coupling alone gives token-only recovery, and an e-process accumulates evidence to certify payload blocks under a prescribed error bound.
yNOIjER6jB.key_idea: Couple the sender's sampling to receiver-side evidence (maximal and token-class coupling) while preserving the sender distribution, and certify payload blocks by accumulating an e-process.
yNOIjER6jB.evidence: Proofs of computational security and a bound on incorrect recovery, plus experiments on four datasets across receiver access modes against steganography and watermarking baselines per reviews.
yNOIjER6jB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the asymmetric receiver access problem is valuable and that separating distribution preservation from recovery evidence is a well-motivated, unified design covering four receiver modes.
yNOIjER6jB.main_concern: The full-recovery evaluation is under-specified: BER excludes unrecovered suffixes and PACER's payload length and success criterion are unclear versus fixed-payload baselines, and block synchronization under retokenization is also underspecified.

lkgZmGsuS8.one_liner: Interprets catastrophic forgetting through solution density, deriving chance-level risk floors and an inverse-factorial bound under a volume-based selection hypothesis.
lkgZmGsuS8.problem: Standard ERM in continual learning degrades earlier-task performance, and it is unclear what follows when current-task learning stops favoring low-risk solutions for earlier data.
lkgZmGsuS8.method: A measure-theoretic risk decomposition with a proximal/distal split relative to the current task, plus a solution-density selection hypothesis that bounds the probability ERM selects low-risk distal solutions by their normalized parameter volume. With label-permutation symmetry this gives a chance-level lower bound on expected distal risk and a 1/r! upper bound on optimal solution density.
lkgZmGsuS8.key_idea: Assume ERM selects low-risk distal solutions with probability at most their normalized parameter volume, then use label-permutation symmetry to lower-bound risk at chance level.
lkgZmGsuS8.evidence: Theorems under the selection hypothesis and CIFAR-100 proof-of-concept experiments (ResNet-32 per reviews) in class-disjoint, blurry, and generalized class-incremental settings using risk-CDF comparisons and plug-in risk bounds.
lkgZmGsuS8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing forgetting as a selection problem (existence of low-risk solutions versus the probability ERM finds them) is a clear, appealing perspective, developed with careful measure-theoretic assumptions.
lkgZmGsuS8.main_concern: Nearly all results hinge on Hypothesis 2, which is postulated rather than derived from ERM, and the experiments are limited to CIFAR-100 and ResNet-32 with bounds on final risk rather than measured forgetting.

GAZ9M6IWIX.one_liner: Deep RL actor emitting compact coefficients over a fixed temporal basis to generate action weights across a fine scheduling grid.
GAZ9M6IWIX.problem: When scheduling periodic messages in deterministic networks, a per-time-grid-position actor output makes the actor output dimension grow with scheduling precision.
GAZ9M6IWIX.method: ActBasis predicts compact coefficients over a fixed temporal basis (fixed sine/cosine harmonics) to generate action-selection weights across the full scheduling grid, instead of one weight per position per link.
GAZ9M6IWIX.key_idea: Represent per-link time-grid action-selection weights as a low-dimensional combination of fixed harmonic basis functions, decoupling actor output size from timing resolution.
GAZ9M6IWIX.evidence: A single-resource task and network topologies including an A380 scenario, compared with a direct per-position (Dense) parameterization under a matched encoder, TD3 learner, critic interface, and decoder, plus initialization controls.
GAZ9M6IWIX.claimed_gains: Reaches scheduling success rates close to a direct per-position parameterization while reducing timing outputs per link by a factor of 125.
GAZ9M6IWIX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ActBasis cleanly decouples scheduling precision from actor output dimension and stays close to dense-parameterization performance with far fewer outputs.
GAZ9M6IWIX.main_concern: The choice of a fixed sinusoidal basis is not justified against other compact representations, and the evidence is limited to one scenario with much of the advantage already present before training.

xanjAjimtr.one_liner: Feed-forward street-scene Gaussian splatting that jointly predicts intrinsic properties, sunlight, and environment radiance in a physically based pipeline.
xanjAjimtr.problem: Feed-forward reconstruction models predict color radiance fields without intrinsic properties or lighting, while editable alternatives need hours of per-scene iterative inverse rendering.
xanjAjimtr.method: In one forward pass, Lumen-GS predicts intrinsic primitives, sunlight, and global environment radiance from sparse-view images at a single timestamp, aggregating multi-view features with a Hybrid Ring representation and taking sunlight direction from GPS/IMU metadata. A Physically-Aligned Decoder (PAD) has intrinsic heads supervised by teacher pseudo-labels and physically based rendering.
xanjAjimtr.key_idea: Jointly supervise intrinsic prediction heads with teacher pseudo-labels and a physically based rendering loss inside a sunlight-integrated feed-forward representation.
xanjAjimtr.evidence: Results on nuScenes for reconstruction, relighting, and harmonization, compared with feed-forward baselines and iterative inverse-rendering methods (abstract is truncated).
xanjAjimtr.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that it stays competitive with the strongest feed-forward baselines in novel-view synthesis, with no numbers visible.
xanjAjimtr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree relightable feed-forward reconstruction for outdoor scenes is a valuable direction and that the method gives competitive rendering quality against sparse-view feed-forward baselines without per-scene optimization.
xanjAjimtr.main_concern: Evaluation is concentrated on nuScenes with a close baseline (XYZCylinder) missing, unclear baseline training protocols, and PBR metrics that do not verify physically consistent relighting under novel illumination.

FIZ3JfMEN4.one_liner: BTGA weights each source-target view pair's alignment by Barlow Twins consistency and redundancy scores for multi-view graph domain adaptation.
FIZ3JfMEN4.problem: Domain shift differs across views, but existing multi-view graph domain adaptation methods weight all view pairs uniformly and ignore how each source view relates to its target view.
FIZ3JfMEN4.method: Barlow Twins invariance and redundancy-reduction terms are applied to each source-target view pair, and the resulting consistency and redundancy scores set the alignment weight of that pair.
FIZ3JfMEN4.key_idea: Measure each view pair by consistency and redundancy (Barlow Twins terms), which correlate with domain discrepancy, and use both as training signals and as per-pair alignment weights.
FIZ3JfMEN4.evidence: Empirical correlation of consistency and redundancy with domain discrepancy, plus experiments on benchmark datasets; reviews cite twelve transfer tasks on ACM and MAG with component ablations.
FIZ3JfMEN4.claimed_gains: Experiments on a variety of benchmark datasets verify effectiveness; no numbers stated.
FIZ3JfMEN4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that view pairs have different domain shifts and that weighting them by consistency and redundancy is a reasonable, interpretable idea with consistent gains.
FIZ3JfMEN4.main_concern: Ablations lack a uniform-weighting variant, so adaptive weighting is not isolated, and the link between the scores and discrepancy rests on limited empirical evidence.

6mI1yWABeZ.one_liner: Proves max of up to 12 inputs needs only two hidden ReLU layers, via exact computer-assisted linear-algebra search.
6mI1yWABeZ.problem: The number of hidden layers needed to exactly represent piecewise-linear functions, such as the maximum function, is only partly known.
6mI1yWABeZ.method: After symmetry reduction, an exact search over candidate solutions becomes a finite linear system over the rationals, and structured first-layer solutions are substituted recursively into deeper networks.
6mI1yWABeZ.key_idea: Reduce the search for exact ReLU constructions of max_n to a symmetry-reduced rational linear system, and reuse the structured first layer recursively to cut depth.
6mI1yWABeZ.evidence: Computer-assisted exact certificates for max_n up to n=12, with proofs and separate verification programs described by reviewers.
6mI1yWABeZ.claimed_gains: max_n is exactly representable with two hidden layers for every n<=12 (previously n=5), and any CPWL function on R^d needs at most ceil(log_6((d+1)/2))+1 hidden layers, versus base three before.
6mI1yWABeZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the constructions are sound and verifiable and extend the known range from 5 to 12 inputs, improving the depth bound from base three to base six.
6mI1yWABeZ.main_concern: The results leave the asymptotic depth bound and the general two-hidden-layer question unchanged and offer little practical guidance, with the lower bound still open.

iWgKeFsVtF.one_liner: Replaces nonlinearities with Gaussian-process activations whose posterior mean equals the original activation, giving post-hoc single-pass uncertainty for frozen networks.
iWgKeFsVtF.problem: Strong uncertainty methods require retraining, Monte Carlo sampling, or expensive second-order computations and may alter a frozen backbone's predictions.
iWgKeFsVtF.method: GAPA models uncertainty over activation outputs rather than weights, using GP activations with closed-form activation-space variances. It scales through a sparse inducing-point approximation over cached reference pre-activations and local k-nearest-neighbor subset conditioning for deterministic single-pass propagation.
iWgKeFsVtF.key_idea: Use a GP over each activation whose posterior mean exactly matches the original nonlinearity and whose variance reflects coverage by cached reference pre-activations.
iWgKeFsVtF.evidence: Regression, classification, image segmentation, and language modeling, including tabular regression, ResNet classification, U-Net segmentation, and LLaMA-3.2-3B OOD detection (per reviews), with ablations on cache coverage and layer placement.
iWgKeFsVtF.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says GAPA is competitive with strong post-hoc baselines and often improves calibration or out-of-distribution detection while remaining efficient at test time.
iWgKeFsVtF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is retraining-free, preserves the backbone's predictions exactly, and is evaluated broadly across tasks and architectures.
iWgKeFsVtF.main_concern: It is unclear why activation-space support reflects predictive epistemic uncertainty, and one reviewer notes overlap with an earlier activation-level GP paper (Bergna et al., AABI 2025) that is not cited.

qkRTCwPCZu.one_liner: SCOPE-Fuzzer fuzzes LLM-based paper reviewers with feedback-driven strategy selection and adaptive content mutation to expose failures static templates miss.
qkRTCwPCZu.problem: Prior evaluations of LLM-based scientific reviewers use a narrow set of static perturbation templates, giving limited evidence of real reliability.
qkRTCwPCZu.method: The authors build a three-level perturbation framework (surface presentation, argumentative logic, value judgment) and then propose SCOPE-Fuzzer. It selects perturbation strategies from reviewer feedback and adaptively mutates paper content over repeated probes.
qkRTCwPCZu.key_idea: Treat reviewer robustness as an iterative fuzzing problem: choose perturbation strategies by observed score feedback and mutate paper content adaptively instead of applying one fixed template.
qkRTCwPCZu.evidence: Experiments on representative LLM-based reviewers (seven reviewer systems per reviews) show stratified vulnerability and perturbation undercoverage; multi-probe and fuzzing tests use 93 ICLR 2024 papers.
qkRTCwPCZu.claimed_gains: Abstract states SCOPE-Fuzzer consistently uncovers vulnerabilities overlooked by static evaluation and other baselines; no numbers stated.
qkRTCwPCZu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that broader perturbation coverage and adaptive fuzzing reveal reviewer weaknesses that single-template static evaluation understates, under a realistic author-edit threat model.
qkRTCwPCZu.main_concern: Gains may come from best-of-k selection and regression to the mean, since there is no content-neutral rewriting baseline and human validation covers only six abstract pairs.

hVQ2ezBTWz.one_liner: ThinkWAM routes each decision state to direct action prediction or future-prediction reasoning at a chosen intensity.
hVQ2ezBTWz.problem: World action models that drop test-time future prediction cut cost but can degrade control, and the benefit of prediction varies across decision states.
hVQ2ezBTWz.method: A multi-intensity reasoning training scheme lets one WAM do both direct action prediction and predictive reasoning at different intensities. A router is trained in two stages to learn the benefit of reasoning and then a cost-aware allocation over intensities.
hVQ2ezBTWz.key_idea: Train a router that decides per decision state whether to run future prediction and at what intensity, balancing predicted control quality against computation cost.
hVQ2ezBTWz.evidence: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa GR1 and real-world tasks, with reasoning-ratio experiments comparing learned gating with random routing.
hVQ2ezBTWz.claimed_gains: Success rates of 98.8%, 80.5% and 77.7% on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and RoboCasa GR1 and 73.8% on real-world tasks, with predictive reasoning applied to a limited share of states (abstract cuts off at 28%).
hVQ2ezBTWz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that test-time future prediction is neither always necessary nor safely removable is valuable, and the router is validated on several benchmarks.
hVQ2ezBTWz.main_concern: Efficiency is reported as reasoning frequency and FLOPs per forward rather than end-to-end latency, and novelty over prior adaptive world-action-model work is seen as incremental.

RAEvAORlmQ.one_liner: Norm-preserving relative camera encoding using rotation blocks for ray orientation, multi-frequency phases for metric translation, and a disparity-anchored epipolar prior.
RAEvAORlmQ.problem: Homogeneous projective camera encodings can let attention logits and feature norms grow unbounded with physical translation baselines on real-world metric trajectories.
RAEvAORlmQ.method: MeRoPE encodes relative orientation between calibrated viewing rays with orthogonal rotation blocks, maps raw metric displacements into multi-frequency rotary phases, and adds a disparity-anchored correspondence prior along the epipolar arc. This preserves feature norms, bounds pre-softmax logits regardless of translation scale, and is invariant to global rigid coordinate changes.
RAEvAORlmQ.key_idea: Build the camera positional operator entirely from orthogonal rotations, feeding raw metric displacement in as rotary phases so feature norms stay fixed at any translation scale.
RAEvAORlmQ.evidence: A multi-dataset driving benchmark with large-baseline trajectories and PanShot with diverse camera optics, compared with prior camera encodings on a matched backbone.
RAEvAORlmQ.claimed_gains: Stronger camera control than prior encodings, with the lowest reported mean joint rotation-translation error among the compared encodings; no numeric values are given in the abstract.
RAEvAORlmQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the operator is clean and norm-preserving, with comparisons against recent camera encodings on one backbone and ablations that mostly support each component.
RAEvAORlmQ.main_concern: The claimed scale-dependent failure is not directly measured, and the driving-benchmark CamMC advantage over RayNova is within run-to-run variation, with PanShot translation known only up to scale.

cCbVsSE2Eb.one_liner: Instruction-conditioned rectified flow trained on one-to-eight-step degradation chains, refined by one preference-optimization round, for music mastering.
cCbVsSE2Eb.problem: SonicMaster is trained mostly on single degradations (never more than three), so it can succeed by correcting each artifact in isolation, unlike real music that accumulates several ordered degradations.
cCbVsSE2Eb.method: Trains Prism, an instruction-conditioned rectified flow from degraded to reference-master latents, on degradation chains of one to eight degradations from 24 types, plus pass-through pairs for already-mastered music. A single offline preference-optimization round ranks the model's own samples by predicted production quality (PQ) and mel-SSIM to the reference.
cCbVsSE2Eb.key_idea: Train on ordered multi-degradation chains with pass-through pairs, then run offline preference optimization that ranks own samples by predicted production quality and mel-SSIM.
cCbVsSE2Eb.evidence: Held-out synthetic chains and 574 real low-production-quality releases, with ablations against the prior corpus and a same-architecture model trained further on the original corpus.
cCbVsSE2Eb.claimed_gains: On held-out chains mel-SSIM improves by +0.112 versus +0.002 and preservation of already-mastered inputs is 0.98 vs. 0.82; across 574 real releases predicted PQ rises from 5.36 to 5.87, improving 79.3% of tracks, against +0.09 for SonicMaster and +0.32 for the same architecture trained further.
cCbVsSE2Eb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the carefully built compound-degradation corpus, the pass-through preservation, and ablations showing the gains are not explained by continued training on the old corpus.
cCbVsSE2Eb.main_concern: Evidence on real music is weak and not independent: Audiobox is used for selection, ranking, and evaluation, and the small real-audio listening study shows no advantage over SonicMaster and omits Prism without preference optimization.

LWEB5QhYci.one_liner: Discrete entropy estimator that computes missing mass through a self-consistent fixed point, aimed at small-sample settings.
LWEB5QhYci.problem: Plugin entropy estimates underestimate entropy in small samples because they ignore the probability mass of unobserved support elements.
LWEB5QhYci.method: SENECA estimates the missing mass with a self-consistent calculation, solved as a fixed point with Steffensen iteration per reviews, and uses it in a coverage-adjusted entropy estimate that gives unseen categories equal probability.
LWEB5QhYci.key_idea: Solve a self-consistent fixed-point equation for the missing mass, spread it equally over estimated unseen categories, and plug it into the entropy estimate.
LWEB5QhYci.evidence: Numerical experiments over eight distribution families, a biodiversity estimation application, and detection of incorrect LLM responses; a consistency proof is also given.
LWEB5QhYci.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the small-sample problem is well motivated and that SENECA is competitive in simulations and applications, including LLM uncertainty without internal probabilities.
LWEB5QhYci.main_concern: The consistency proof relies on an unestablished bound on the estimated number of unseen categories, and uniqueness and convergence of the fixed point are not shown.

0PMR7eHERh.one_liner: Typed graph linking multimodal patient observations to a biomedical knowledge graph through explicit alignment edges for clinical LLM retrieval.
0PMR7eHERh.problem: Existing predictive systems rarely represent links between patient multimodal evidence and biomedical knowledge, so the links cannot be traced to sources or removed to measure their contribution.
0PMR7eHERh.method: MM-KG keeps patient observations and biomedical concepts as separate graph layers joined by alignment edges. Modality-specific harmonizers map EHR text, imaging, genomic and biospecimen data to UMLS concepts, a route-prioritized aligner links them, and candidate-conditioned retrieval selects a compact subgraph for an LLM or GNN.
0PMR7eHERh.key_idea: Keep patient evidence and knowledge in separate graph layers joined by removable alignment edges, then retrieve a candidate-conditioned subgraph.
0PMR7eHERh.evidence: MIMIC-IV and ADNI with a 2x2 design separating patient evidence, biomedical knowledge and their interaction, plus held-out five-candidate ranking compared with MindMap.
0PMR7eHERh.claimed_gains: Drug-controlled AUROC interaction of +0.194 on MIMIC and +0.299 on ADNI, and +0.131 Hits@1 over MindMap on held-out five-candidate ranking.
0PMR7eHERh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit separation of patient observations, knowledge concepts and alignment edges, which supports provenance tracing and evidence removal.
0PMR7eHERh.main_concern: The methodological contribution is limited, since entity linking, graph retrieval, RAG and GNN components are existing and largely deterministic, making this mainly systems integration.

tHkXsjjuqN.one_liner: Persistent sparse voxel feature map for online semantic occupancy mapping, with offline refinement from cached local features.
tHkXsjjuqN.problem: Embodied agents need an up-to-date global semantic occupancy map during exploration under causal constraints, and a better refined map afterward using additional computation.
tHkXsjjuqN.method: VEOcc++ keeps a persistent sparse voxel feature map that expands with newly observed regions and integrates aligned local features through reliability-guided updates, with context-aware decoding for the current map. After exploration, cached local features are consolidated and combined with the online representation for multi-scale spatial refinement.
tHkXsjjuqN.key_idea: Maintain and update persistent voxel features with reliability-guided integration instead of accumulating semantic predictions, then refine offline using cached local features.
tHkXsjjuqN.evidence: EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet online and offline evaluation, a fixed-predictor comparison against VEOcc fusion, ablations, zero-shot deployment, and Jetson robot experiments reporting latency, cache size, and memory growth per reviewers.
tHkXsjjuqN.claimed_gains: The method reaches 67.12% IoU and 58.40% mIoU online, beats VEOcc fusion by 3.70 IoU and 3.74 mIoU with the local predictor fixed, and offline refinement reaches 67.79% IoU and 59.37% mIoU.
tHkXsjjuqN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the online-plus-offline mapping design is practical, results on EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet are strong with convincing fixed-predictor gains, and real-robot or Jetson experiments show deployment feasibility.
tHkXsjjuqN.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited relative to persistent-memory Gaussian methods (EmbodiedOcc, TGSFormer) and the online update's benefit is unclear, since mean feature accumulation already reaches 57.49 mIoU versus 58.40 and offline refinement adds under one point.

wIeY6eluuv.one_liner: HT-ChainPE, a phased-elimination algorithm with a chained robust estimator, lowers the gamma_T exponent of GP bandit regret under heavy-tailed noise.
wIeY6eluuv.problem: Existing regret bounds for Gaussian process bandits with (1+epsilon)-moment noise are linear in the maximum information gain gamma_T.
wIeY6eluuv.method: HT-ChainPE combines regularized D-optimal design with a robust chained estimator in a phased elimination scheme, and the authors also prove a worst-case regret lower bound on [0,1]^d.
wIeY6eluuv.key_idea: Combine regularized D-optimal design with a robust chained estimator so regret depends on gamma_T with an exponent below one.
wIeY6eluuv.evidence: Theory: upper and lower regret bounds, plus an experimental check of a more practical variant (per reviews).
wIeY6eluuv.claimed_gains: Cumulative regret of O~(T^{1/(1+eps)} (1 v gamma_T)^{(1+3eps)/(2(1+eps))}), retaining the T^{1/(1+eps)} dependence while reducing the gamma_T exponent below one for eps<1.
wIeY6eluuv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper advances the state of the art on GP bandits under heavy-tailed noise with improved upper and lower bounds and is readable.
wIeY6eluuv.main_concern: Reviewers say originality is limited (a kernelization of prior phased-elimination work plus chaining, with a remaining gap between bounds) and the algorithm is not practical, and one reviewer questions the reported experiments.

Mj9Ligkb9X.one_liner: Two-stage tool-use framework: predict 2D keypoint trajectories from action-free data, then ground them into robot actions with few demonstrations.
Mj9Ligkb9X.problem: Robots trained on specific tools fail to transfer the same function to novel tools because perceptual functional similarity does not carry over to action space.
Mj9Ligkb9X.method: After comparing affordance images, human video prompts, functional videos and object masks, and 2D keypoint trajectories, they choose keypoint trajectories; FuncBridge learns to predict them from action-free data and grounds them into robot actions with limited demonstrations.
Mj9Ligkb9X.key_idea: Decouple functional reasoning from action execution via 2D keypoint trajectories, which balance functional expressiveness and action groundability.
Mj9Ligkb9X.evidence: A benchmark with ten tools and three functions (hitting, sweeping, hooking) in simulation and the real world, with a comparison of intermediate representations.
Mj9Ligkb9X.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on unseen tools in simulation and the real world; no numbers stated.
Mj9Ligkb9X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree functional generalization for tool use is a relevant problem, the keypoint-trajectory representation fits tool use, and results improve across hitting, sweeping and hooking in simulation and real-world tests.
Mj9Ligkb9X.main_concern: Reviewers say the unseen-tool claim is not cleanly established because action-free keypoint data appear to cover all test tools, and the components are largely adapted from prior work with incremental novelty.

hKNOcBcEpB.one_liner: LS-LoRA places LoRA adapters only in layers with low input-output cosine similarity, a forward-only proxy for Fisher sensitivity.
hKNOcBcEpB.problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs often degrades general capabilities, and existing mitigations rely on data replay or regularization rather than choosing where to adapt.
hKNOcBcEpB.method: Layers are ranked by input-output cosine similarity, a forward-only proxy for layer-wise empirical Fisher information, and LoRA adapters are trained only in the lowest-similarity layers.
hKNOcBcEpB.key_idea: Select adaptation layers by low input-output cosine similarity, which tracks high empirical Fisher scores, so only task-sensitive layers receive LoRA adapters.
hKNOcBcEpB.evidence: Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation across several models, with retention measured on commonsense benchmarks and a random layer-selection control noted by reviewers.
hKNOcBcEpB.claimed_gains: The abstract states improved average target-task performance while retaining general capabilities, with numbers cut off; reviews cite 4.2 to 14.4% lower peak memory and 10.0 to 29.6% shorter training time.
hKNOcBcEpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and cheap, needing only forward passes over unlabeled inputs, and gives consistent target-task and capability-retention gains over baselines.
hKNOcBcEpB.main_concern: Incremental contribution and missing baselines (similarity-based layer selection exists in ShortGPT and Ogawa et al.), and the retention evaluation is narrow with an unclear protocol and no variance.

ixV0cP8et2.one_liner: Open suite of from-scratch text-to-image MMDiT flow models with deterministic, traceable training and resumable checkpoints for studying learning dynamics.
ixV0cP8et2.problem: Text-to-image research lacks open, fully traceable training runs of the kind Pythia and OLMo provide for language models, so how concepts are learned cannot be studied from training history.
ixV0cP8et2.method: BlueMage trains 0.5B, 2.0B and 3.9B MMDiT flow models on 1M, 10M and 100M GPIC images with 40 to 117 resumable checkpoints per run. Data order, flow time, noise and caption dropout are deterministic, and attribute-entity annotations on every caption allow concept exposure to be tracked.
ixV0cP8et2.key_idea: Fix every stochastic training choice per slot in closed form, so any checkpoint's data stream and each concept's exposure history can be recomputed.
ixV0cP8et2.evidence: Controlled runs across three model sizes and three data scales, with exposure records and five reported findings on attribute-entity pairs, binding, retrieval and caption variation.
ixV0cP8et2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the traceable training record, with reconstructable data order, exposure histories and resumable checkpoints, is a useful community resource for studying memorization, attribution and reproducibility.
ixV0cP8et2.main_concern: Findings are associational and based on a single training run per condition, and rely on noisy annotations (about 57% attribute-entity recall) and a single VLM judge.

YoZbmlH3ZA.one_liner: Maps molecular encoder features to LLM embeddings with an injective projector that splits preservation and nonlinear adaptation into orthogonal subspaces.
YoZbmlH3ZA.problem: Existing molecular-LLM projectors do not enforce recoverability of encoder features after projection, which may limit access to fine-grained molecular features.
YoZbmlH3ZA.method: MIP2 fuses topological and geometric features through reversible coupling, then separates feature preservation and nonlinear adaptation into orthogonal subspaces to yield an injective projection with an explicit recovery map. It keeps one token per atom and uses bidirectional attention within the molecular span.
YoZbmlH3ZA.key_idea: Fused features occupy a learned subspace while the nonlinear residual is confined to its orthogonal complement, giving the projection a closed-form left inverse.
YoZbmlH3ZA.evidence: Experiments on molecular QA (MoleculeQA), description generation and retrosynthesis (Mol-Instructions), and property prediction (Mol-Instructions and eight MoleculeNet datasets), with backbone comparisons and ablations.
YoZbmlH3ZA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the projector design is clear and mathematically sound, with a verified recovery guarantee and controlled experiments across several tasks and LLM backbones.
YoZbmlH3ZA.main_concern: Gains are not shown to come from information preservation rather than architectural regularization, because the experiments vary components instead of the amount of information retained.

2cl14Etdww.one_liner: Trains an LLM agent's subgoal policy to predict next states, rewarded by state consistency, plus an inverse-dynamics-trained action policy.
2cl14Etdww.problem: RL for LLM agents couples reasoning with action and relies on sparse task rewards, producing ungrounded reasoning and poor sample efficiency in multi-round interaction.
2cl14Etdww.method: A Subgoal Reasoning Policy (SRP) predicts intended next states and an Action Reasoning Policy (ARP) generates actions to realize those transitions. The SRP is trained with separately normalized task-return and state-consistency advantages, while the ARP is trained with periodic inverse-dynamics.
2cl14Etdww.key_idea: Make reasoning verifiable by having the SRP predict the next state and scoring it against the observed transition, so failed trajectories still give a training signal.
2cl14Etdww.evidence: Experiments across multiple interactive environments; reviews cite comparisons with GiGPO on three environments and two backbones (including ALFWorld and WebShop) with three seeds.
2cl14Etdww.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding intermediate reasoning in observed state transitions gives useful feedback beyond sparse task reward and improves over GiGPO.
2cl14Etdww.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the benefit of separating the SRP and ARP from the consistency signal, grouping scheme, or extra adapter, and results use only three seeds without significance analysis.

MjIHuUCIDr.one_liner: Self-distills hindsight state-transition evaluations from a teacher-mode LLM into token-level advantage reshaping for multi-turn agent RL.
MjIHuUCIDr.problem: Multi-turn agentic RL relies on sparse outcome rewards with coarse credit assignment and ignores the task information hidden in state transitions.
MjIHuUCIDr.method: The same LLM acts as a student that interacts with the environment and as a teacher that sees the resulting state transitions to give hindsight evaluation of the student's actions. The teacher-student output-distribution difference is distilled into token-level credit signals, and an asymmetric reshaping applies different operators to positive and negative advantages.
MjIHuUCIDr.key_idea: Use the difference between teacher-mode (transition-conditioned) and student-mode output distributions as token-level credit, and reshape positive and negative advantages with different operators.
MjIHuUCIDr.evidence: Experiments on multiple long-horizon interactive benchmarks; reviews cite three-seed comparisons against GiGPO and RAGEN-2 on ALFWorld and WebShop.
MjIHuUCIDr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using state transitions as privileged information, without an external teacher, critic, or reward model, is a well-motivated way to improve credit assignment, with promising results on ALFWorld and WebShop.
MjIHuUCIDr.main_concern: The closest prior work (RLSD and other agentic self-distillation methods) is not a baseline, so it is unclear whether gains come from the transition evidence or the asymmetric reshaping.

DR0pKddxtK.one_liner: Infers a latent 3D semantic state from noisy multi-view 2D foundation-model embeddings with a pose-aware set-based variational model.
DR0pKddxtK.problem: Multi-view 2D foundation-model embeddings are noisy and view-dependent, so simple multi-view pooling gives unstable 3D semantics.
DR0pKddxtK.method: Casper3D models view-level semantic features as noisy observations of an underlying 3D semantic state and infers that state with a set-based variational model that incorporates relative pose. It is trained by predicting held-out semantic observations from unseen viewpoints while staying aligned with visual and text semantic spaces.
DR0pKddxtK.key_idea: Infer a variational latent 3D state by pose-aware set reasoning over views, trained by predicting held-out semantic features from unseen viewpoints, treating 2D embeddings as noisy observations.
DR0pKddxtK.evidence: The abstract states that it gives more stable 3D semantics than multi-view pooling in ambiguous and noisy settings; reviews note evaluation mainly on semantic segmentation with a single foundation model (TIPSv2).
DR0pKddxtK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the probabilistic formulation of multi-view 2D-to-3D feature lifting well motivated and interesting for 3D understanding.
DR0pKddxtK.main_concern: Novelty and the need for the Bayesian framing are questioned relative to feature-lifting methods and a noisy autoencoder, and evaluation is limited mainly to semantic segmentation with one foundation model.

aEr7V9GecQ.one_liner: Steers agentic-RAG rollouts with query-class contexts before rollout and retrieval-statistics contexts mid-rollout to prevent search-behavior homogenization.
aEr7V9GecQ.problem: Training one RLVR policy across diverse search patterns causes behavioral conflicts and collapse onto an average search pattern (behavioral homogenization), and existing fixes cost extra compute or memory.
aEr7V9GecQ.method: QDTS adds query-side pre-rollout steering, where a rule-based parser sorts queries into structural patterns and supplies class contexts during training and inference, and document-side mid-rollout steering, which evaluates online retrieval statistics and injects dynamic contexts across multi-turn rollouts to catch search failures. Reviews note that the contexts are optimized with GEPA.
aEr7V9GecQ.key_idea: Condition the RLVR policy on rule-parsed query-class contexts before rollout and retrieval-statistic-triggered contexts mid-rollout, separating conflicting search patterns without extra inference LLM calls.
aEr7V9GecQ.evidence: Reviews describe 6 QA benchmarks, multiple backbones and retrievers, behavioral metrics (depth slope, over-/under-search, selectivity), and component ablations; the abstract is truncated before the results.
aEr7V9GecQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the failure mode is concretely formalized with behavioral metrics beyond answer accuracy, and that QDTS improves results across backbones and retrievers without added inference-time LLM calls.
aEr7V9GecQ.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate class-specific and mid-rollout steering from GEPA prompt optimization, which alone gives most of the gain, and some strong baselines are copied from earlier papers rather than reproduced.

D8E6bb0Ioc.one_liner: Proves when unlabeled test-time adaptation is PAC-learnable and introduces PRISM, an optimization-free method built on recoverable semantic structure.
D8E6bb0Ioc.problem: It is unknown when unlabeled target data can determine a better predictor in test-time adaptation, and why entropy-based updates correct errors instead of merely sharpening predictions.
D8E6bb0Ioc.method: The authors give conditions for recoverable semantic structure (components recoverable and source-oriented, with within-semantic support dominating cross-semantic leakage), prove PAC-style component-resolution learnability with finite-sample guarantees, and show for two-layer networks that correction arises through a parameter-gradient coupling kernel. They then introduce PRISM, an optimization-free TTA method; reviews describe it as using multi-view agreement with spectral weighting and JS-based fusion.
D8E6bb0Ioc.key_idea: Target semantics are recoverable when source-oriented components dominate cross-semantic leakage, and entropy correction propagates source-oriented evidence through parameter sharing via a gradient coupling kernel.
D8E6bb0Ioc.evidence: Theorems on component-resolution learnability and early-stage target-risk reduction (finite-width two-layer networks, fixed head), plus experiments on five distribution-shift benchmarks, with structural audits on CIFAR-C and four backbones noted in reviews.
D8E6bb0Ioc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory offers useful, apparently correct perspectives on when and why TTA works and that PRISM improves over strong baselines without backpropagation.
D8E6bb0Ioc.main_concern: The theory covers two-layer networks and does not directly establish PRISM's effectiveness on the evaluated ViT/ResNet models, and the headline comparison rests mainly on short streams and CIFAR-C audits.

R96f3l8k3x.one_liner: Selects post-pruning recovery data by matching sparse-autoencoder feature distributions of the pruned model's gradient-salient hidden coordinates to the candidate corpus.
R96f3l8k3x.problem: Existing recovery-data selectors rank by difficulty, quality, or diversity, or need both original and pruned models, without characterizing the pruned model's internal representation that needs repair.
R96f3l8k3x.method: SFDA identifies response-salient hidden coordinates using loss gradients, encodes their activations with a TopK sparse autoencoder, and selects a fixed-size subset whose projected sparse-feature distribution matches that of the candidate corpus. The subset is optimized jointly and only the pruned checkpoint is required.
R96f3l8k3x.key_idea: Pick the recovery subset whose projected TopK-SAE feature distribution, over loss-gradient-salient hidden coordinates of the pruned model, matches the distribution of the candidate corpus.
R96f3l8k3x.evidence: Experiments across different pruned LLM configurations using 10% of Alpaca; reviews note several models, pruning methods, coding and math tasks, multi-seed runs, matched training budgets, and baselines such as PASER and MONA.
R96f3l8k3x.claimed_gains: Highest average reasoning accuracy using only 10% of Alpaca, outperforming the strongest competing selector by 2.36-4.36 percentage points.
R96f3l8k3x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that selecting recovery data from the pruned model's own state is well motivated and report consistent average gains across models, pruning methods, and matched training budgets.
R96f3l8k3x.main_concern: Ablations (Tables 6-7) show dense representations and simpler matching objectives reach nearly the same recovery NLL, so the need for the sparse-autoencoder and distribution-matching pipeline is unclear.

73G9xppHkI.one_liner: Unifies egocentric hand motion reconstruction, infilling and generation as conditional motion modeling over a shared two-hand motion representation and backbone.
73G9xppHkI.problem: Existing approaches treat 4D hand motion reconstruction, infilling, and generation as separate problems despite their shared need to model hand articulation and temporal dynamics.
73G9xppHkI.method: GHM formulates the three tasks as conditional hand motion modeling under varying levels of visual observability, using a shared motion representation and backbone that learn from visual and semantic supervision and jointly model both hands in a common motion space. Reviews add a cross-representation consistency loss aligning world and camera space.
73G9xppHkI.key_idea: One shared backbone and common two-hand motion space serves all three tasks by varying which visual and semantic conditions are provided, with a consistency loss tying world- and camera-space representations.
73G9xppHkI.evidence: Experiments across reconstruction, infilling and generation settings; reviews cite HOT3D, H2O, and HoloAssist comparisons against baselines such as HandFlow, MINT, and LatentAct.
73G9xppHkI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified formulation is clear and well motivated, with extensive comparisons across tasks and datasets and strong reconstruction and infilling results.
73G9xppHkI.main_concern: Novelty is limited because core components follow existing methods, and ablations are insufficient to separate the effects of large-scale joint training, unification, and text conditioning, while generation is weakly evaluated.

WiY7GTwHkb.one_liner: Evaluates LLM abductive inference by having agents probe two black-box lambda-calculus kernels to find which is mutated and why.
WiY7GTwHkb.problem: How well large language models perform abductive inference, inferring explanations for observations, remains poorly understood.
WiY7GTwHkb.method: Elenchos is an evaluation framework in controlled executable formal environments, instantiated with a dependently typed lambda-calculus kernel. Given one sound and one intentionally mutated kernel, agents interact with both through a black-box interface to decide which is sound and attribute the behavioral differences to the underlying mutations.
WiY7GTwHkb.key_idea: Abduction is tested through replayable black-box probing of executable kernels with a finite, known set of mutations, so evidence sufficiency and attribution can be checked objectively.
WiY7GTwHkb.evidence: Experiments on 13 models across difficulty levels and mutation configurations (13 predefined mutations, 10 selected mutation pairs in the main evaluation, per reviews), plus ablations on hypothesis evaluation versus prediction derivation.
WiY7GTwHkb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the executable, finite-hypothesis setup is a controlled and well-motivated way to test abductive reasoning, with rigorous experiments and ablations.
WiY7GTwHkb.main_concern: The setup is narrow (one lambda-calculus kernel, 13 predefined mutations, 10 selected pairs), so the broader claims about abductive reasoning may not generalize.

RDvoKny2dc.one_liner: Generates LiDAR scenes with triplane latent diffusion and a simulation-based coarse-to-fine ray point sampling strategy that preserves real scanning patterns.
RDvoKny2dc.problem: Existing LiDAR scene synthesis methods struggle to capture real scanning patterns, geometric structure, and semantic properties at the same time.
RDvoKny2dc.method: LiTDM is a two-stage framework: a triplane-based autoencoder predicts point-based occupancy and intensity with a ray sampling strategy, then a diffusion model trained on triplane features generates scenes. LiDAR Simulation-based Point Sampling (LSPS) enforces the characteristic scanning patterns of real sensors.
RDvoKny2dc.key_idea: Use triplane features as the diffusion latent proxy and decode points by coarse-to-fine sampling along simulated sensor rays (LSPS), so generated scenes follow real scan patterns.
RDvoKny2dc.evidence: Comparisons against baselines and ablations on LSPS and representation choice, plus conditional camera-to-LiDAR and text-to-LiDAR generation and cross-sensor experiments noted in reviews.
RDvoKny2dc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments and ablations are thorough and that the model supports conditional and cross-sensor generation.
RDvoKny2dc.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the pipeline resembles existing triplane scene generators (SemCity), NeRF-style ray sampling, and standard latent diffusion, and the benefit of triplanes over range images or sparse voxels is not clearly shown.

rCZrj7H112.one_liner: Discovers multimodal fusion operators by composing LLM-generated primitives with evolutionary search, then searches architectures over the discovered operator library.
rCZrj7H112.problem: Fusion operators in multimodal classification are largely human-designed, which limits the diversity of fusion mechanisms that can be explored.
rCZrj7H112.method: LLMDFO-NAS uses LLMs to generate executable, validated fusion primitives and evolutionary search to compose them into candidate fusion operators. Candidates are scored across several architecture contexts with an architecture-aggregated zero-cost proxy and Pareto selection, and the chosen operators form the library for downstream multimodal architecture search.
rCZrj7H112.key_idea: Represent fusion operators as executable programs composed from LLM-generated primitives by evolutionary search, ranked by an architecture-aggregated zero-cost proxy with Pareto selection.
rCZrj7H112.evidence: Experiments on five representative multimodal benchmarks across modality configurations, with ablations on the LLM backbone, evolutionary composition strategy, and proxy correlation noted in reviews.
rCZrj7H112.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that searching for the fusion operators themselves, as executable programs rather than picks from a fixed library, is an interesting expansion of the multimodal NAS search space.
rCZrj7H112.main_concern: The discovered operators are simple (max or mean aggregation, normalization) and could be hand-defined, so the benefit of LLMs is unproven, gains are small, and novelty over general LLM-driven discovery is limited.

9nqBznJ2lW.one_liner: Tokenizes continuous signals with a locality-preserving hierarchical feed-forward encoder, replacing meta-learning's inner loop for modality-agnostic neural fields.
9nqBznJ2lW.problem: Neural-field representation learning relies on memory-intensive per-sample meta-learning, while feed-forward alternatives add modality-specific assumptions that sacrifice generality.
9nqBznJ2lW.method: LH-NeF uses a locality-preserving hierarchical encoder to map raw coordinate-value observations to structured tokens, from which the field is reconstructed during training. A single forward pass replaces meta-learning's inner loop; reviews list Morton ordering, hierarchical attention, Gaussian weighting, cross-attention, and FiLM among the components.
9nqBznJ2lW.key_idea: Inject locality (spatially ordered tokens) and hierarchy priors into a feed-forward encoder so field tokens come from one forward pass without modality-specific architecture.
9nqBznJ2lW.evidence: Images, 3D shapes, and climate fields, on reconstruction and downstream tasks against modality-agnostic, modality-specific, and specialized generative neural field baselines, with ablations.
