vOYDCZRZXY.main_concern: PEAR's prompts and gating criteria are not disclosed and controls such as a text-only PEAR baseline are missing, and the audio-and-text-only scope is questioned.

yuecwWUrm1.one_liner: Hybrid layer compresses key kernel features and values into an SSM memory and reconstructs attention from memory states.
yuecwWUrm1.problem: Hybrid architectures usually stack attention and recurrent layers rather than mixing attention and recurrent memory within one layer.
yuecwWUrm1.method: Interdomain Attention compresses values and kernel features of keys into a recurrent memory parameterized by an SSM, then approximates dot-product attention by implicitly reconstructing the attention matrix and values from memory states, preserving SSM efficiency.
yuecwWUrm1.key_idea: Project key kernel features and values onto SSM memory states, then read out with queries to approximate softmax attention inside a single layer.
yuecwWUrm1.evidence: Pre-training of 125M-1.3B models on text compared with an S4D baseline at matched memory size and with a softmax Transformer, plus Caduceus-based genomic experiments and ablations.
yuecwWUrm1.claimed_gains: Across 125M-1.3B models, IA beats an S4D baseline at matched memory size and a softmax Transformer in perplexity and common-sense accuracy; a review cites 1.3B validation perplexity of 7.98 versus 8.62 for softmax.
yuecwWUrm1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is clear and motivated, compressing keys and values separately with query-conditioned readout, and that language-modeling results beat the S4D control across sizes with ablations supporting attention-like readout.
yuecwWUrm1.main_concern: There is no direct comparison with the closest recurrent-memory baselines such as Mamba-2 or Gated DeltaNet, and recall is weak (9.5% on RULER at 4K versus 89% for softmax).

jTY0LTIiES.one_liner: Paired base/tuned LLM study showing post-training worsens confidence reliability while discrimination stays stable; temperature scaling shifts with evaluation pool.
jTY0LTIiES.problem: It is unclear whether post-training's accuracy gains come with better confidence quality, and whether calibration fixes transfer across evaluation pools.
jTY0LTIiES.method: Empirical study of 16 base/tuned model pairs, 6 post-training settings, and 3 multiple-choice tasks, decomposing confidence quality into reliability and discrimination. It then evaluates calibration methods, varies the evaluation pool by difficulty, and measures how many target labels recalibration needs.
jTY0LTIiES.key_idea: Decomposes confidence quality into reliability (Brier component) and discrimination, then measures how a temperature fitted on one evaluation pool transfers to harder or easier pools.
jTY0LTIiES.evidence: 47 model-task cells (16 base/tuned pairs, 6 post-training settings, 3 multiple-choice tasks), including a 35-cell alignment cohort, using softmax confidence over answer options.
jTY0LTIiES.claimed_gains: In the 35-cell alignment cohort, post-training improves average accuracy by 1.1 percentage points while increasing the Brier reliability component by 0.047, with reliability degrading in 32 of 35 cells; median temperature for harder pools is approximately 5 times that for easier pools; only 20 target labels can substantially improve calibration.
jTY0LTIiES.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reliability-versus-discrimination decomposition, the paired base/tuned design, and the label-budget recalibration experiments across models, recipes, and tasks.
jTY0LTIiES.main_concern: Limited novelty, since post-training miscalibration with preserved ranking ability is already reported in prior work, and findings are confined to multiple-choice softmax confidence.

uZFqcUuTvw.one_liner: Streaming diffusion for world action models using a chunk-wise noise ladder, prefix rollout, and dense video-history memory.
uZFqcUuTvw.problem: Deployed World Action Models execute discontinuously and jerkily, and existing fixes address either inference efficiency or cross-chunk action continuity but not both.
uZFqcUuTvw.method: StreamingWAM combines a noise ladder for chunk-wise action prediction, a prefix rollout module for cross-chunk continuity, and dense video-history memory for temporally consistent conditioning. Reviews describe a persistent buffer that enables single-pass steady-state replanning while preserving unfinished plans.
uZFqcUuTvw.key_idea: Assign staircase-increasing noise levels across chunks in a persistent buffer so replanning needs one denoising pass, while prefix rollout and video history keep chunks continuous.
uZFqcUuTvw.evidence: Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic tasks, including static and dynamic settings.
uZFqcUuTvw.claimed_gains: Reduces steady-state replanning latency to 72.9 ms in simulation and 57.3 ms on the real robot, with smoother action transitions and lower sensitivity to the execution horizon K.
uZFqcUuTvw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining lower steady-state latency with action continuity addresses real deployment limits of large WAMs, with supportive ablations and simulation, perturbation, and real-robot tests.
uZFqcUuTvw.main_concern: Gains are confounded by unequal training budgets (extra training steps over the baseline checkpoint) and inconsistent baseline configurations across tables, and novelty over Diffusion Forcing and Streaming Diffusion Policy is limited.

3uGrJZz2hY.one_liner: Single network maps a list of typed prior and likelihood factors plus observations to a Gaussian posterior, generalizing across models.
3uGrJZz2hY.problem: Amortized inference usually targets a fixed model or restricted family, and extending it to new model families requires retraining or test-time fine-tuning.
3uGrJZz2hY.method: AFINs describe a model as a list of typed prior and likelihood factors and map it with the observations to a Gaussian posterior approximation through an encode-merge-decode network whose learned parameters do not depend on latent dimension or observation count. Optional importance sampling refines the approximation.
3uGrJZz2hY.key_idea: Encode each typed factor, merge factor encodings independently of their number, and decode a Gaussian posterior, so one set of weights covers varying priors, likelihoods, and dimensions.
3uGrJZz2hY.evidence: Synthetic and real-data benchmarks against NUTS and per-task variational inference (Bayesian GLM benchmarks with latent dimension up to 16 per reviews).
3uGrJZz2hY.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says a single trained AFIN gives competitive posteriors at substantially lower test-time cost than NUTS and per-task variational inference, without numbers)
3uGrJZz2hY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that amortizing over both data and model structure in one general network is new and interesting, with a sensible architecture and easy addition of new factor types.
3uGrJZz2hY.main_concern: The model class and benchmarks are restrictive (single global latent, conditionally independent observations, near-Gaussian GLM posteriors), a single Gaussian limits flexibility, and there is no theory.

WUsIidMZka.one_liner: Studies how Mamba in-context learns stationarity-constrained switching Markov chains, showing estimation gaps close while identification limits remain.
WUsIidMZka.problem: Laplacian smoothing, which Mamba was shown to learn for unconstrained Markov chains, is suboptimal when kernels share a stationary distribution, and hidden switching adds a separate identification problem.
WUsIidMZka.method: The paper separates estimation (a single unknown constrained kernel) from identification (known kernels and switching matrix). It proves the constrained Bayes predictor differs from Laplacian smoothing in the readout and probes trained Mamba on two- and three-state chains.
WUsIidMZka.key_idea: The constrained Bayes predictor needs a log-linear softmax readout that combines transition counts across rows, while hidden switching imposes a positive residual loss that no predictor removes.
WUsIidMZka.evidence: Theorems on strict suboptimality of Laplacian smoothing, an exact two-state readout with width linear in sequence length and a matching lower bound, plus probes of trained Mamba on two- and three-state chains and hidden-switching experiments.
WUsIidMZka.claimed_gains: Trained Mamba stores transition counts linearly and combines them across rows at the readout, closing most of the estimation gap, while even the optimal infinite-memory filter keeps a strictly positive residual loss under hidden switching; no numeric values stated.
WUsIidMZka.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory clean, correct and elegant, with a clear link between statistical estimation and architectural expressivity and careful probe design.
WUsIidMZka.main_concern: The work is essentially theoretical on a toy model: experiments do not show Mamba learns the proposed construction, and the hidden-switching analysis has rigor gaps such as ignoring an i.i.d. kernel baseline.

OXpf9jp52h.one_liner: Theory of when a mean uncertainty-score threshold certifies pass probability, and what finite verifier draws per ordering can identify.
OXpf9jp52h.problem: A service that needs the expected ordering-specific pass probability E[Q] above a threshold p* may instead average a decreasing score phi(Q), and it is unclear when that mean score certifies the target and what finite verifier observations can identify.
OXpf9jp52h.method: The paper shows the largest distribution-free safe cutoff is the lower convex envelope of phi at p*, and that n verifier draws per ordering identify exactly the polynomial score functionals of degree at most n under count-only observation. It contrasts this with identity-aware pooling and increasing-depth estimation.
OXpf9jp52h.key_idea: The distribution-free certification cutoff is the lower convex envelope of the score at p*, and n draws per ordering identify only degree-at-most-n polynomial score functionals.
OXpf9jp52h.evidence: Theorems on certification and identifiability, plus controlled experiments with homogeneous controls where every ordering has the same success probability; reviewers note bootstrap intervals sometimes under-cover the nominal 95%.
OXpf9jp52h.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers credit sharp, interpretable theory that separates target mismatch from finite-depth measurement error, including an affine-score necessary-and-sufficient condition and controls with identical orderings.
OXpf9jp52h.main_concern: Presentation and problem setup are hard to follow: one reviewer could not identify the application domain, setup and research question from the generator, retrieval and agent-systems framing.

nuzGwtxxl5.one_liner: Block exogeneity and sparse adjustment identify causal feedback components while separating their statistical recovery costs.
nuzGwtxxl5.problem: The sample requirements for recovering strongly connected components and their inter-component edges in cyclic causal models remain insufficiently understood.
nuzGwtxxl5.method: The paper derives information-theoretic lower bounds separating component membership from external-parent selection. BlockExo uses residual independence, inclusion minimality, and sparse adjustment to recover components and their direct external parents.
nuzGwtxxl5.key_idea: Identify root strongly connected components through residual independence and inclusion minimality using sparse adjustment sets.
nuzGwtxxl5.evidence: Lower bounds, population characterizations, and a conditional upper bound accompany simulations of cyclic linear non-Gaussian models.
nuzGwtxxl5.claimed_gains: Any estimator requires order s_max log(ep/s_max)+d_B log(ep/d_B) samples in the worst case, and BlockExo attains a structurally matching bound under suitable conditions.
nuzGwtxxl5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the sample-complexity analysis and the population characterization through block exogeneity and sparse adjustment.
nuzGwtxxl5.main_concern: Separation margins in the upper bound may depend on structural parameters, weakening the claimed match with the lower bound.

SIRSGsQfAj.one_liner: Hierarchical low-diameter graph decompositions maintain spectral sparsifiers under edge insertions and deletions with constant amortized recourse.
SIRSGsQfAj.problem: Dynamic graphs require sparse spectral representatives that remain efficient to maintain as edges change.
SIRSGsQfAj.method: The algorithm maintains a hierarchy of low-diameter graph clusterings and extends a static sparsification framework to dynamic updates. Its analysis bounds sparsifier size, update time, and recourse.
SIRSGsQfAj.key_idea: Maintain hierarchical low-diameter decompositions to update a spectral sparsifier with bounded changes after graph edge updates.
SIRSGsQfAj.evidence: The paper proves dynamic sparsification guarantees and evaluates the framework on real-world and synthetic graphs against natural baselines.
SIRSGsQfAj.claimed_gains: The algorithm attains size O(n log^3 n log log n/epsilon^2), amortized update time O(log^6 n log log n), and amortized recourse O(1).
SIRSGsQfAj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize simultaneous improvements in sparsifier size, update time, and recourse.
SIRSGsQfAj.main_concern: The technical contribution largely combines existing static sparsification, decremental decomposition, and bucketing techniques, leaving the methodological advance limited.

hNnDfhjmQx.one_liner: Learned cross-domain sensor transport and channel decorrelation adapt wearable time-series models to mismatched sensor channels.
hNnDfhjmQx.problem: Wearable domain adaptation often ignores channel-meaning changes across users, devices, and sensor placements.
hNnDfhjmQx.method: Inter-Domain Sensor Alignment learns a source-target correspondence matrix from domain-specific sensor embeddings and maps target channels into source sensor space. A decorrelation regularizer suppresses redundant couplings and representation collapse.
hNnDfhjmQx.key_idea: Explicitly transport target sensor channels into source sensor coordinates while regularizing cross-channel redundancy.
hNnDfhjmQx.evidence: Opportunity, WISDM, and sEMG evaluations include multiple UDA methods, controlled perturbations, transport visualizations, and component ablations.
hNnDfhjmQx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find cross-domain sensor mismatch practically relevant and the proposed alignment design well motivated.
hNnDfhjmQx.main_concern: The experiments do not establish that learned transport recovers sensor correspondence rather than compensating for other domain differences.

7mHxzwCVmF.one_liner: Synthetic edge-sketch supervision and photo-guided relation alignment train a perception MLLM to localize within sketches and from sketch prompts.
7mHxzwCVmF.problem: Photo-trained perception models lack sketch-specific representations and instance-level sketch-to-photo training pairs.
7mHxzwCVmF.method: Sketch-Omni converts labeled photos to edge sketches, constructs sketch-to-photo instance pairs, and trains multiple localization tasks. Photo-guided relation alignment teaches the sketch pass to reproduce phrase-related relations from the photograph pass.
7mHxzwCVmF.key_idea: Transfer photo-conditioned relational supervision to sketch inputs while constructing instance-matched sketch-to-photo training pairs.
7mHxzwCVmF.evidence: Quantitative and qualitative evaluations cover sketch-input and sketch-query tasks, including SketchyCOCO, FS-COCO, and same-category instance difficulty splits.
7mHxzwCVmF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the multi-task evaluation and documented synthetic-data construction, with quantitative results supported by qualitative examples.
7mHxzwCVmF.main_concern: Evaluation relies heavily on synthetic or training-like sketch inputs and limited baselines, weakening evidence for broader sketch generalization.

02puEqrhMo.one_liner: Uncertainty-aware Kalman fusion carries visual prompts across frames for temporally consistent depth completion.
02puEqrhMo.problem: Frame-wise depth completion is temporally inconsistent, while temporal video models can impose substantial computational overhead.
02puEqrhMo.method: KFTP adapts a frozen depth foundation model using a compact visual prompt state. It fuses previous and current prompts through Kalman-style updates with adaptive process noise to manage temporal uncertainty.
02puEqrhMo.key_idea: Propagate the prompt state and fuse it with the current optimized prompt according to estimated uncertainty.
02puEqrhMo.evidence: Indoor and outdoor depth benchmarks, including DDAD, DyDToF, and Sintel, evaluate spatial accuracy and temporal consistency against prior methods.
02puEqrhMo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize improved temporal stability and spatial accuracy from carrying prompt state across frames.
02puEqrhMo.main_concern: Missing warm-start and simpler temporal baselines leave the source of the accuracy gains and the need for Kalman fusion unclear.

zMRdihOkqk.one_liner: Region-level attention cutting and steering probe how open-weight language models maintain refusal during generation.
zMRdihOkqk.problem: Prompt-only robustness tests miss refusal failures caused by access to inference-time internal computation.
zMRdihOkqk.method: The study defines a white-box threat model that alters attention between semantic chat regions while keeping parameters fixed. It tests refusal at response opening and during continuation without training or prompt optimization.
zMRdihOkqk.key_idea: Alter attention pathways between semantic regions at selected generation stages to test refusal dependence.
zMRdihOkqk.evidence: Experiments span multiple open-weight model families and safety benchmarks, comparing attention interventions at opening and continuation.
zMRdihOkqk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a useful attention-level perspective on refusal and appreciate the clear experimental presentation.
zMRdihOkqk.main_concern: The practical scope is unclear because internal attention access and preidentified harmful regions differ from many deployment settings.

7iRbzeH6ia.one_liner: Candidate-conditioned interaction graphs predict other agents' responses so embodied planners can score alternative futures for risk.
7iRbzeH6ia.problem: Direct imitation-based action prediction can overlook how surrounding agents react to alternative ego actions.
7iRbzeH6ia.method: A vision-language model proposes ego trajectories, and interaction graphs plus speed/path meta-actions predict surrounding-agent futures for each candidate. Risk scoring selects a trajectory after task-module pretraining and LoRA adaptation.
7iRbzeH6ia.key_idea: Condition surrounding-agent response prediction on each candidate ego trajectory before risk-based selection.
7iRbzeH6ia.evidence: Closed-loop Bench2Drive experiments with a Qwen2-0.5B backbone compare driving outcomes and ablate interaction components.
7iRbzeH6ia.claimed_gains: The method reports a Driving Score of 87.47 and Success Rate of 72.73%, exceeding the strongest compared baseline by 9.43 points and 17.64 percentage points.
7iRbzeH6ia.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value modeling other agents' responses and the strong closed-loop driving results.
7iRbzeH6ia.main_concern: Training on factual trajectories and current ablations do not validate responses to unexecuted ego actions or establish their contribution to gains.

ZmTTIBqPD2.one_liner: A harmfulness-reweighted gradient identity connects expected-harm optimization with target-likelihood optimization for language-agent safety evaluation.
ZmTTIBqPD2.problem: Expected-harm and harmful-target likelihood objectives lack a clear connection in agent jailbreak optimization.
ZmTTIBqPD2.method: The paper derives an identity expressing the input gradient of log expected harmfulness through likelihood gradients under a harmfulness-reweighted distribution. OPUR samples harmful targets to guide likelihood-based input optimization.
ZmTTIBqPD2.key_idea: Reweight output likelihoods by harmfulness to connect expected-harm gradients with likelihood-based optimization.
ZmTTIBqPD2.evidence: A probabilistic derivation accompanies experiments on three agent benchmarks covering malicious-instruction and malicious-environment settings with ReAct agents.
ZmTTIBqPD2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the probabilistic connection between expected harmfulness and likelihood objectives.
ZmTTIBqPD2.main_concern: OPUR does not clearly approximate the theoretical harmfulness-reweighted distribution, leaving the theory-method connection unresolved.

5Y8elsVOjQ.one_liner: Shared adapted 3D foundation features support primitive identification, geometry recovery, and topology prediction for B-Rep reconstruction.
5Y8elsVOjQ.problem: Passing compressed task-specific predictions between reconstruction stages loses geometric context and amplifies ambiguity and errors.
5Y8elsVOjQ.method: BRepLift adapts pretrained 3D features into a shared B-Rep-aware representation. Clustering-guided face identification and context-conditioned geometry and topology modules reuse these features across reconstruction stages.
5Y8elsVOjQ.key_idea: Reuse rich adapted geometric features across stages instead of passing only intermediate primitive predictions.
5Y8elsVOjQ.evidence: Three test sets of differing geometric and topological complexity compare face, edge, vertex F1, and B-Rep validity against DualBrep.
5Y8elsVOjQ.claimed_gains: Reconstruction validity increases from 10.60% to 22.14% on ABC-ParseNet and from 17.34% to 29.46% on the curated test set.
5Y8elsVOjQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find shared geometric context a coherent design for connecting segmentation and structured reconstruction.
5Y8elsVOjQ.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate feature sharing from pretraining and adaptation, particularly against independently encoded stage features.

dy93ggoTav.one_liner: Estimated state-action validity gates action conditioning to reduce unsupported-action degeneration in autoregressive world-model rollouts.
dy93ggoTav.problem: Actions outside training support can destabilize world-model rollouts beyond errors caused by imperfect generated visual context.
dy93ggoTav.method: Controlled action manipulations characterize off-support drift and visually plausible but dynamically unreliable collapse. Validity-aware gating estimates state-action support and adjusts the strength of action conditioning.
dy93ggoTav.key_idea: Attenuate action conditioning according to a learned estimate of whether the state-action pair lies within training support.
dy93ggoTav.evidence: Visual-navigation and robotic-manipulation experiments test supported and unsupported actions, with controlled perturbations and ablations.
dy93ggoTav.claimed_gains: The method lowers final 16-second FID by 45.3% in visual navigation and 13.3% in robotic manipulation over the original models.
dy93ggoTav.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find unsupported-action instability well motivated and the empirical rollout-stability gains convincing.
dy93ggoTav.main_concern: Better visual stability does not establish reliable dynamics for unseen actions, particularly beyond the anticipated out-of-distribution action families.

7bsXysvipt.one_liner: Score-feedback matrices and conditional centering establish tight horizon-dependent gradient variance rates for on-policy distillation.
7bsXysvipt.problem: The tight dependence of distillation-gradient variance on sequence length and temporal credit rules remains unclear.
7bsXysvipt.method: The analysis represents credit assignment with a score-feedback matrix and uses conditional score centering to bound variance. Shared-parameter constructions establish matching lower bounds, while prefix controls characterize removable variance and approximation costs.
7bsXysvipt.key_idea: Exploit conditional score orthogonality to separate variance contributions from past, local, and future feedback links.
7bsXysvipt.evidence: Worst-case proofs accompany full-parameter Qwen and Llama variance measurements and controlled GPT-2 optimization experiments.
7bsXysvipt.claimed_gains: The paper establishes tight variance rates of Θ(T^2) for token-local and Θ(T^3) for full-return and reward-to-go updates, tightening the previous quartic full-return bound.
7bsXysvipt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the tight worst-case variance characterization and valid shared-parameter constructions as the main theoretical contribution.
7bsXysvipt.main_concern: Worst-case variance rates offer limited practical estimator guidance, especially because token-local updates target a different gradient and control benefits lack end-to-end validation.

Noeg3KceLr.one_liner: Asymmetric exponential moving-average feedback stabilizes federated LoRA by feeding back factor A while retaining FedAvg updates for B.
Noeg3KceLr.problem: Highly heterogeneous federated LoRA training can collapse to majority-class predictions in a seed-dependent manner.
Noeg3KceLr.method: Stabilized A-Feedback returns the EMA of LoRA factor A to training while keeping B on the FedAvg path. Server-side identities and a restricted rank-one analysis describe displacement shrinkage, accumulated gaps, and optimization bias.
Noeg3KceLr.key_idea: Apply cross-round EMA feedback to only one LoRA factor, using A as the empirically preferred default.
Noeg3KceLr.evidence: Exact feedback identities, rank-one single-step SGD bounds, and multi-task federated experiments with feedback ablations examine collapse and stability.
Noeg3KceLr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the simple implementation, negligible added communication, and improved stability in highly heterogeneous settings.
Noeg3KceLr.main_concern: A-only feedback does not consistently outperform B-feedback or evaluation-only EMA, leaving the asymmetric choice empirically task-dependent.

puSpGUgQtO.one_liner: Parallel Transformer position prediction and entropy-guided ordering with GRPO optimize chip macro placement.
puSpGUgQtO.problem: Sequential RL macro placers follow a fixed placement order, making early macro misplacements myopically constrain subsequent decisions and propagate layout errors.
puSpGUgQtO.method: HoliPlace encodes netlist and macro features with a Graph AutoEncoder and predicts position distributions for all macros simultaneously using an encoder-only Transformer. An entropy-guided ranker dynamically sets the sequential legalization order by prediction uncertainty, and GRPO jointly optimizes macro positions and ordering.
puSpGUgQtO.key_idea: Predict all macro position distributions in parallel with a GAE-Transformer encoder, order sequential placement by prediction entropy, and train jointly via GRPO.
puSpGUgQtO.evidence: Experiments evaluate wirelength, regularity, and PPA metrics on the ICCAD2015 macro placement benchmark with encoder and ordering ablations.
puSpGUgQtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting macro position distributions globally in parallel and ordering legalization via prediction entropy under GRPO addresses fixed-order sequential placement bias.
puSpGUgQtO.main_concern: Reviewers note that final legalization remains sequential with quadratic Transformer cost, rewards omit standard cells and post-routing PPA, and comparisons miss DREAMPlace and generative placers like ChipDiffusion and FlowPlace.

BXstVXkmh3.one_liner: Predicting masked video-segment features from surrounding frames and text descriptions improves video LLM understanding.
BXstVXkmh3.problem: Standard video LLMs train almost exclusively with language targets and treat video only as input, leaving self-supervised visual prediction underused for video understanding.
BXstVXkmh3.method: During training, the method removes a temporal segment from a video and trains the video LLM to predict that segment's visual features from the remaining video and a text description alongside standard language supervision, adding no inference overhead.
BXstVXkmh3.key_idea: Remove a video segment during training and supervise the video LLM to predict its visual features from remaining video and segment descriptions.
BXstVXkmh3.evidence: Controlled comparisons against language-only counterparts span three model scales from 0.8B to 4B across video understanding and temporal grounding benchmarks including MVBench and TempCompass.
BXstVXkmh3.claimed_gains: At 0.8B and 2B scales, learning to predict improves scores by up to 3.3 points on MVBench, 3.3 points on TempCompass, and 3.4 points in mean grounding mIoU.
BXstVXkmh3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the masked visual-feature prediction objective is simple, needs no extra annotations or inference cost, and yields consistent directional gains across model scales.
BXstVXkmh3.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains stem from visual prediction rather than generic regularization or epoch differences due to missing random-target controls, and note overlap with prior masked visual modeling in MLLMs.

NU9hl4p09R.one_liner: Testing and refining model-proposed board conditions against engine evaluations discovers reusable motifs for game-move explanations.
NU9hl4p09R.problem: Language models struggle to explain superhuman chess engine moves, relying on surface-level board observations rather than strategic motifs that generalize across positions.
NU9hl4p09R.method: The paper defines an automatic motif-generalization metric and introduces BinProp, a training-free method that turns LLM-proposed concepts into executable board conditions refined with engine evaluation feedback to explain moves in natural language.
NU9hl4p09R.key_idea: Convert LLM-proposed game concepts into executable board conditions and refine them with engine feedback to generate natural-language move explanations.
NU9hl4p09R.evidence: Evaluations measure automatic motif generalization across multiple language models on chess and extend concept discovery to Go, draughts, and shogi.
NU9hl4p09R.claimed_gains: BinProp improves motif generalization for every model tested on chess, nearly tripling the average score compared with direct prompting.
NU9hl4p09R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that turning LLM-proposed game concepts into executable, engine-tested features without training is simple, clearly motivated, and reusable across board games.
NU9hl4p09R.main_concern: All three reviewers question evaluation validity and explanatory faithfulness, noting that statistical correlation with engine evaluations is circularly tied to BinProp's objective without proving causal attribution or evaluating natural-language explanations with human players.

JGS12EpryI.one_liner: Comparing post-hoc unlearning updates against retrained oracles reveals weight-space orthogonality driven by steepness versus selectivity.
JGS12EpryI.problem: Post-hoc machine unlearning methods assume gradient-based optimization can recover a selective parameter update similar to retraining from scratch without the forget set.
JGS12EpryI.method: Using models retrained from the same base initialization without the forget set as weight-space oracles, the study measures directional cosine alignment and decomposes optimization geometry into steepness (forget loss gained per unit weight step) versus selectivity (forget loss gained per unit retain damage).
JGS12EpryI.key_idea: Contrast weight-space alignment to retrained oracles by separating gradient steepness per unit weight movement from selectivity per unit retain damage.
JGS12EpryI.evidence: Empirical analyses on Llama and Qwen models up to 1.5B parameters compare post-hoc unlearning methods, plain SGD, and curvature preconditioning against retrained oracles using reseed nulls and mirror forget sets.
JGS12EpryI.claimed_gains: Along the straight path to the retrained oracle, forget loss rises 140× while retain loss rises by at most 1.19×, whereas post-hoc unlearning updates at comparable forget levels are nearly orthogonal at cos ≈ 0.009 and retain about a quarter (Llama) to a ninth (Qwen) of a single retrain's alignment with the shared forget-specific component.
JGS12EpryI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric distinction between steepness and selectivity offers a clear, well-controlled empirical perspective on how gradient-based unlearning diverges from retraining.
JGS12EpryI.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluated checkpoints stop far short of oracle-level forgetting (retaining high forget ROUGE-L) and question whether matching a single weight-space retraining direction is necessary for effective unlearning.

8pLho1x6wI.one_liner: Anchoring personalized concepts to frozen pretrained class predictions balances subject fidelity and prompt alignment in diffusion.
8pLho1x6wI.problem: Few-shot personalized text-to-image diffusion either overfits reference images at the cost of prompt alignment or over-enforces prior preservation at the cost of distinctive subject attributes.
8pLho1x6wI.method: Semantic Anchoring Personalization (SAP) treats a user-specific subject as an underrepresented concept paired with a well-represented semantic class in the pretrained model, combining concept learning and prior preservation into a single anchored training objective without architectural changes.
8pLho1x6wI.key_idea: Formulate few-shot diffusion personalization as a single objective that anchors the learned target concept to its pretrained semantic class prediction.
8pLho1x6wI.evidence: Mathematical analysis and experiments on SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 evaluate subject fidelity, text-image alignment, and ablations across object personalization tasks.
8pLho1x6wI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semantic-anchoring formulation is simple, mathematically grounded, and easy to integrate across diffusion backbones without auxiliary networks or separate stages.
8pLho1x6wI.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited novelty and missing comparisons against closely related class-constrained and DreamBooth variants such as ClassDiffusion, PNP, AttnDreamBooth, and DreamBooth++, alongside limited pose diversity and newer backbones.

vfbavGC6T0.one_liner: A specification-guided user simulator and independent verifiers test clarification and requirement retention across dependent analytical stages.
vfbavGC6T0.problem: Existing data-agent benchmarks rarely test both acquiring missing requirements and preserving those decisions across dependent analyses.
vfbavGC6T0.method: IterAct-Bench turns Kaggle workflows into staged tasks with persistent agent state. A user simulator supplies clarification and correction, while separate executable verifiers assess correctness without exposing gold outputs to the simulator.
vfbavGC6T0.key_idea: Keep clarified requirements and actual computation state across stages while separating simulated user feedback from executable correctness checks.
vfbavGC6T0.evidence: The benchmark evaluates seven frontier LLMs and four agent harnesses on 86 tasks with 554 stages over 727 data files.
vfbavGC6T0.claimed_gains: The strongest configuration achieves an Average Pass Rate of 70.9%.
vfbavGC6T0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate persistent analytical state and the separation between user simulation and executable correctness verification.
vfbavGC6T0.main_concern: The evaluation does not directly isolate preservation of previously learned requirements from acquisition failures, formatting errors, and propagation of incorrect computations.

NwIU5HY9e8.one_liner: Executable smart-home simulation evaluates agents by resulting device states across tasks and increasingly complex homes.
NwIU5HY9e8.problem: Static instruction-to-API benchmarks miss state-dependent reasoning, interaction, and personalized multi-device behavior in smart homes.
NwIU5HY9e8.method: SMH-Bench uses HomeEnv to execute actions and verify final device states, including preservation of irrelevant states. Tasks span different home sizes and assess control, querying, scheduling, ambiguity handling, and personalized reasoning.
NwIU5HY9e8.key_idea: Evaluate goal satisfaction through executable household state changes rather than matching a reference action sequence.
NwIU5HY9e8.evidence: Frontier LLMs face 1,100 tasks across 7 categories and 22 subcategories, with home complexity extending to 135 devices.
NwIU5HY9e8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the task coverage and detailed evaluation, particularly final-state verification and analysis by home complexity.
NwIU5HY9e8.main_concern: Direct and interactive reasoning comparisons vary state visibility, feedback, output format, and interaction budget, confounding the source of performance differences.

gm5L6EAVSu.one_liner: Mean-field encoder and decoder dynamics characterize nonlinear autoencoders with a fixed finite-dimensional bottleneck.
gm5L6EAVSu.problem: Autoencoder theory largely covers linear, shallow nonlinear, or non-bottleneck settings rather than nonlinear finite-bottleneck architectures.
gm5L6EAVSu.method: The paper derives mean-field learning dynamics for the encoder and decoder while holding bottleneck dimension fixed. It bounds finite-width SGD risk tracking and optimal-risk approximation, then studies connections to early linear representations and principal curves.
gm5L6EAVSu.key_idea: Take hidden-layer widths to the mean-field limit while retaining a fixed bottleneck, then compare finite-network risk with the limiting dynamics.
gm5L6EAVSu.evidence: Theoretical results establish high-probability finite-time risk tracking and convergence of optimal finite-width risk to the mean-field optimum, with supplementary numerical studies.
gm5L6EAVSu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the extensive mean-field derivations and theoretical treatment of nonlinear bottleneck autoencoders.
gm5L6EAVSu.main_concern: The theory offers limited practical guidance for choosing finite widths or training real autoencoders.

3BarLAuA7V.one_liner: Bottleneck permutation scores turn conformal prediction sets into bipartite graphs whose perfect matchings encode accepted assignments.
3BarLAuA7V.problem: Permutation prediction sets can contain factorially many assignments, making explicit enumeration impractical despite straightforward statistical calibration.
3BarLAuA7V.method: The method scores each permutation by its worst selected edge and represents thresholded sets as perfect matchings in an admissible-edge graph. Split conformal calibration sets the threshold, and graph algorithms answer assignment and ambiguity queries.
3BarLAuA7V.key_idea: Threshold edgewise bottleneck nonconformity so that accepted permutations are exactly the perfect matchings of a calibrated bipartite graph.
3BarLAuA7V.evidence: Theory characterizes exactly graph-representable score families and marginal coverage under exchangeability, with synthetic, sorting, and frozen pretrained keypoint-matching experiments.
3BarLAuA7V.claimed_gains: In sorting, roughly 149 edges represent a median 2.99×10^12 accepted permutations.
3BarLAuA7V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of exact graph representations that preserve assignment constraints and the characterization of compatible scores.
3BarLAuA7V.main_concern: The practical advantage over implicit additive-cost prediction sets remains insufficiently established.

i0abkOeqNB.one_liner: Attributed evidence-to-state-to-answer chains select supervised search turns and allocate reinforcement-learning credit, including useful transitions from failed trajectories.
i0abkOeqNB.problem: Long-horizon search training lacks progress signals grounded in explicit state changes and the browser actions supporting them.
i0abkOeqNB.method: ClueFlow records typed research-state transitions and candidate supporting actions, then validates transitions against gold answers and traces sources after execution. Source–State–Final chains select SFT targets and augment Turn-PPO advantages, including valid transitions from unsuccessful trajectories.
i0abkOeqNB.key_idea: Trace validated state updates back to evidence-acquiring actions and forward to final answers to assign turn-level supervision and credit.
i0abkOeqNB.evidence: Experiments evaluate Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on BrowseComp and BrowseComp-Plus and include controlled SFT and reinforcement-learning ablations.
i0abkOeqNB.claimed_gains: With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, ClueFlow achieves 59.0% accuracy on BrowseComp and 72.0% on BrowseComp-Plus.
i0abkOeqNB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value attribution-based training signals and recovery of useful intermediate supervision from trajectories with incorrect final answers.
i0abkOeqNB.main_concern: Comparisons and ablations do not adequately isolate attribution-chain benefits from training data, context formatting, and credit-allocation choices.

h9F7seLC5B.one_liner: Normalization-aware margin decomposition and cross-checkpoint linear transport measure layerwise semantic evidence changes after mask-token training.
h9F7seLC5B.problem: Aggregate accuracy changes after mask prediction training do not reveal how VLMs rewrite the evidence behind semantic answers.
h9F7seLC5B.method: The framework exactly decomposes fixed-pass decision margins into input and residual-block contributions while accounting for normalization. Checkpoint-sourced readouts separate representation and readout changes, and calibrated linear transport maps evidence between checkpoints.
h9F7seLC5B.key_idea: Decompose decision margins by residual block and fit cross-checkpoint evidence transport while controlling which checkpoint supplies each readout.
h9F7seLC5B.evidence: Five model–benchmark comparisons across two backbone families include group-disjoint reanalysis, affine transport controls, and HiMTok residual-write interventions.
h9F7seLC5B.claimed_gains: Full transport reduces reconstruction error by 30.669.0% relative to uniform rescaling on the original evaluation splits, as written in the abstract.
h9F7seLC5B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the normalization-aware decomposition and controlled comparisons separating representation-side and readout-side changes.
h9F7seLC5B.main_concern: Descriptive evidence reconstruction does not sufficiently explain semantic behavior changes or establish the causal importance of the fitted layer structure.

lEBIf0ArRv.one_liner: Hierarchical beam graphs recover vegetation stiffness and driving forces from motion for simulation under unseen forces.
lEBIf0ArRv.problem: Recovering vegetation physics through inverse simulation or appearance-based learning is computationally expensive and can generalize poorly.
lEBIf0ArRv.method: DynaBeam represents plants and trees as connected beam elements and separates geometry, motion, and force for parameter identification. Geometry-derived modes support forward physical simulation under forces absent from the observed motion.
lEBIf0ArRv.key_idea: Infer physical parameters and forces from motion on a hierarchical beam graph whose vibration modes derive from geometry.
lEBIf0ArRv.evidence: Evaluations test physical-parameter recovery, response to unseen forces, runtime, and reconstruction from real-world videos.
lEBIf0ArRv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize efficient physical inference and the ability of geometry-derived modes to support simulation under new forces.
lEBIf0ArRv.main_concern: Missing matched identification and simple material baselines make the contribution of motion-based parameter recovery difficult to isolate.

tu4FFN3Yi4.one_liner: Influence-weight axioms identify graded sparse mechanisms with transport-metric Lipschitz functions and yield data-dependent generalization bounds.
tu4FFN3Yi4.problem: Systems with a few strong and many weak state-dependent interactions lack a systematic function-class analysis when interaction weights are given.
tu4FFN3Yi4.method: The paper defines permutation-invariant mechanisms through bounded influence and regular dependence on supplied weights, then proves an exact transport-metric representation. The resulting geometry yields sparsity-profile-dependent generalization rates and matching lower bounds in several cases.
tu4FFN3Yi4.key_idea: Translate graded influence constraints into an exact Lipschitz ball on weighted multisets, then derive learning bounds from its transport geometry.
tu4FFN3Yi4.evidence: The work provides representation and generalization theorems, lower bounds for several cases, and non-vacuous empirical certificates on Vicsek-type flock simulations.
tu4FFN3Yi4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the exact correspondence between the axiomatic class and transport-metric Lipschitz functions as a rigorous theoretical contribution.
tu4FFN3Yi4.main_concern: The flock experiments do not demonstrate a need for the richer mechanism class or establish practical learning benefits beyond simpler representations.

gqDRDWrSUP.one_liner: Expected correctness across interruption points trains one search policy to answer early and retain correct answers during continued search.
gqDRDWrSUP.problem: Agents optimized for fixed inference budgets or terminal accuracy can fail when interrupted at an unknown point.
gqDRDWrSUP.method: AnySearcher trains a single search policy with the AnyBudget objective, averaging task performance over possible interruption points. This encourages early correctness and discourages losing correct answers as more search occurs.
gqDRDWrSUP.key_idea: Optimize expected answer correctness over a distribution of interruption points along the same search trajectory.
gqDRDWrSUP.evidence: Experiments on four search benchmarks compare accuracy across budgets, tool interactions needed for performance, and preservation of correctness during continued search.
gqDRDWrSUP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unknown interruption points create a relevant deployment problem and that the anytime-search formulation is well motivated.
gqDRDWrSUP.main_concern: The training procedure closely overlaps with AnytimeReasoner without adequately explaining or testing the methodological distinction.

vmDqI0WmNj.one_liner: Exponential-mechanism selection over fixed public intervention candidates provides differential privacy for complete graph counterfactual explanations.
vmDqI0WmNj.problem: Privatizing graphs can corrupt counterfactual targets, while perturbing optimized explanations makes whole-output privacy difficult to certify.
vmDqI0WmNj.method: PRIVCFS selects interventions from a data-independent universe built from a public prior graph and feature schema. No-op semantics preserve common output support, while a bounded validity-gated utility enables exponential-mechanism release under fixed public context.
vmDqI0WmNj.key_idea: Fix the intervention output universe independently of private data, then sample with the exponential mechanism using bounded validity-gated utility.
vmDqI0WmNj.evidence: A pure ε-DP proof covers the complete released intervention, with recourse and general-population experiments, repeated-query analysis, and exhaustive small-graph checks.
vmDqI0WmNj.claimed_gains: On borderline nodes, retention reaches 94–97% of the support-restricted non-private optimum at ε=8 with absolute validity 0.35–0.61, while four queries sharing a total budget of 2 recover approximately 90–95%.
vmDqI0WmNj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers accept the conditional pure-DP construction based on bounded utility and a fixed data-independent output support.
vmDqI0WmNj.main_concern: The experimental public prior samples current private edges, leaving utility and privacy costs under a genuinely external public prior unestablished.

1Quy3DVlhG.one_liner: Sparse-autoencoder feature changes and prediction loss score rank-one LoRA updates under a fixed storage budget.
1Quy3DVlhG.problem: Task-specific mathematical fine-tuning can interfere with other mathematical abilities, motivating compact updates that preserve acquired capabilities.
1Quy3DVlhG.method: A shared SAE measures representation changes between base and fine-tuned models, which combine with prediction loss to select rank-one LoRA terms. Feature-removal and restoration interventions test whether selected representations support subsequent computation.
1Quy3DVlhG.key_idea: Select compact LoRA components using both fine-tuning-induced sparse feature changes and prediction loss.
1Quy3DVlhG.evidence: Experiments cover four Qwen, Gemma, and Llama model pairs, target-task and GSM8K accuracy, and interventions including supplying the correct next token after feature removal.
1Quy3DVlhG.claimed_gains: Using only 25% of rank-64 LoRA factor storage for candidate matrices, the joint criterion exceeds Full LoRA target-task accuracy on three pairs by 3.2–6.3 percentage points while preserving more GSM8K accuracy.
1Quy3DVlhG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent gains from feature-based update scoring and the usefulness of connecting parameter selection with representation analysis.
1Quy3DVlhG.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate sparse SAE features from generic hidden-state matching or focusing supervision on selected computation positions.

vwT4UuD7Xo.one_liner: Entity pages link recurring entities to source documents, giving search agents a reusable corpus navigation graph.
vwT4UuD7Xo.problem: Agents searching flat document collections repeatedly reconstruct relationships and can miss complementary evidence across documents.
vwT4UuD7Xo.method: CorpusMap resolves recurring entity mentions offline and creates Entity Pages that aggregate information and link to every referring document. Agents traverse this entity-document graph when gathering evidence across the corpus.
vwT4UuD7Xo.key_idea: Resolve entity mentions across documents offline and expose linked Entity Pages as a reusable navigation layer for agentic search.
vwT4UuD7Xo.evidence: Reported experiments compare answer quality and query-time token use across search backbones, with construction-cost reporting and entity-link ablations.
vwT4UuD7Xo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical problem of connecting evidence across documents and find the presentation clear.
vwT4UuD7Xo.main_concern: The cost and scalability of constructing and maintaining entity maps remain insufficiently established for larger or changing corpora.

jumXqRVM1L.one_liner: Capacity-constrained minimum-cost flow allocates evidence budgets across spectral aspects of long multimodal documents.
jumXqRVM1L.problem: Fixed reading budgets must cover relevant document facets without spending capacity on redundant evidence.
jumXqRVM1L.method: FlowReader derives aspect capacities from spectral decomposition of query-relevant content and solves a minimum-cost flow problem on a multimodal graph. It decomposes the flow into evidence chains for parallel vision-language reading and subsequent reconciliation.
jumXqRVM1L.key_idea: Use spectral-energy aspect quotas and query-conditioned flow costs to route a limited evidence budget into consistent multimodal chains.
jumXqRVM1L.evidence: VisDoMBench experiments use Qwen3-VL-32B and controlled ablations with fixed graph, scorer, reader, and judge.
jumXqRVM1L.claimed_gains: FlowReader reaches 68.9 macro accuracy, exceeds the strongest prior system by 2.7 points, retains its lead at 12.9 content nodes per query, and uses about three-quarters of the reader tokens of uncapped shortest-path routing.
jumXqRVM1L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the minimum-cost flow formulation for selecting evidence under a fixed budget without an LLM planning call.
jumXqRVM1L.main_concern: Spectral coverage and routing guarantees do not directly establish coverage of the semantic evidence that questions require.

Bz2hIU0k2a.one_liner: Executable promises define diverse training partners and guide agents' adaptation to unfamiliar collaborators.
Bz2hIU0k2a.problem: Behavioral diversity alone does not ensure that training partners teach behaviors useful for zero-shot coordination.
Bz2hIU0k2a.method: Promise-based Partner Coordination uses an LLM to generate executable coordination commitments and refine them through interaction feedback. It trains Promisers with varying promise enforcement and a Promisee that responds to inferred partner trustworthiness.
Bz2hIU0k2a.key_idea: Translate semantic commitments into state-dependent action constraints to train diverse partners and a history-conditioned response policy.
Bz2hIU0k2a.evidence: Evaluation includes self-play and cross-play in zero-shot coordination environments and a forty-participant study across Overcooked variants and two-player Hanabi.
Bz2hIU0k2a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value inspectable promises that specify recognizable partner behaviors through executable constraints.
Bz2hIU0k2a.main_concern: Shared promise sets and method-specific partner distributions limit what cross-play results establish about adaptation to genuinely unfamiliar conventions.

ysMKN82UUO.one_liner: Averaged pre-RoPE queries retrieve shared prefix candidates, which original queries rescore and reuse throughout block diffusion decoding.
ysMKN82UUO.problem: Sparse prefix attention still requires expensive full-prefix scoring when every masked query selects keys independently.
ysMKN82UUO.method: SPIRA constructs one routing query per head from the block's pre-RoPE query mean to retrieve shared prefix candidates. Original position-dependent queries rescore these candidates, and subsequent denoising steps reuse the selected keys.
ysMKN82UUO.key_idea: Separate block-shared candidate retrieval using averaged pre-RoPE queries from query-specific rescoring, then cache the selected keys across denoising steps.
ysMKN82UUO.evidence: LongBench evaluations compare three block diffusion language models with two sparse baselines, alongside latency measurements on SDAR-4B-Chat-b64.
ysMKN82UUO.claimed_gains: SPIRA exceeds the stronger sparse baseline by up to 10.2 points with 256 keys, comes within 0.06 points of exact attention with 1024 keys, and achieves 3.45× per-block decode speedup at a 122k-token prefix on SDAR-4B-Chat-b64.
ysMKN82UUO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the observed alignment of masked pre-RoPE queries interesting and useful for motivating shared candidate retrieval.
ysMKN82UUO.main_concern: The specific contribution of pre-RoPE routing needs stronger validation against alternative routing designs and closely related block-diffusion methods.

qSj68qrJxo.one_liner: Dual entity-relation clustering integrates knowledge graph training with cluster-wise conformal calibration and prediction-set fairness analysis.
qSj68qrJxo.problem: Knowledge graph embedding accuracy does not ensure reliable prediction-set coverage or fairness.
qSj68qrJxo.method: The framework learns low-rank entity and relation representations, clusters their labels, and uses the resulting structure in self-adversarial training and cluster-wise conformal calibration. A prediction-set size disparity analysis decomposes sources of unfairness.
qSj68qrJxo.key_idea: Use learned entity and relation label clusters to guide both negative-sampling-based training and conformal calibration.
qSj68qrJxo.evidence: Experiments compare multiple knowledge graph embedding backbones and datasets, alongside a theoretical prediction-set size disparity decomposition.
qSj68qrJxo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing predictive accuracy, uncertainty coverage, and fairness together in knowledge graph embeddings.
qSj68qrJxo.main_concern: The methodological and theoretical contributions are insufficiently distinguished from established conformal prediction, clustering, and negative-sampling methods.

z1tbUvR0Jo.one_liner: A learned action-world router progressively restricts visual context across diffusion-transformer layers for embodied control.
z1tbUvR0Jo.problem: Dense action-to-world attention can become homogenized and focus on task-irrelevant regions during action denoising.
z1tbUvR0Jo.method: Progressive Sparse Forcing combines a depth-decaying sparsity schedule with an end-to-end action-world router. The original training objective teaches noisy action tokens to select visual context relevant to denoising.
z1tbUvR0Jo.key_idea: Learn action-conditioned visual token selection while progressively restricting the available context across diffusion-transformer depth.
z1tbUvR0Jo.evidence: Experiments cover LIBERO manipulation, LIBERO-Plus spatial robustness, and long-horizon driving planning with 4K-100K PhysicalAI-AV training clips.
z1tbUvR0Jo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize a practical conditioning modification supported by results in robotic manipulation and autonomous driving.
z1tbUvR0Jo.main_concern: The ablations do not separate progressive sparsity from learned attention reweighting or token selection at matched budgets.

Y9dx4OgBsf.one_liner: Internal attention selects visual regions and text sentences for explicit evidence emphasis before multimodal answer generation.
Y9dx4OgBsf.problem: Noisy retrieved text and distracting image regions cause multimodal models to overlook evidence needed for knowledge-based visual question answering.
Y9dx4OgBsf.method: Look Twice uses internal attention to select query-relevant image regions and sentences, filters attention sinks and distracting content, and reformulates the input to emphasize selected evidence. It requires no parameter updates, auxiliary models, or architectural changes.
Y9dx4OgBsf.key_idea: Convert internal attention into visual and textual evidence selection, then explicitly mark the selected content in a second input.
Y9dx4OgBsf.evidence: Experiments span four knowledge-based VQA benchmarks and ten pretrained multimodal backbones from 2B to 38B parameters, with modality and selection ablations.
Y9dx4OgBsf.claimed_gains: LoT improves every evaluated backbone, with average gains of up to +12.5 accuracy points.
Y9dx4OgBsf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard evaluation across ten backbones and four benchmarks as substantial evidence of the procedure's usefulness.
Y9dx4OgBsf.main_concern: The contribution beyond existing attention-based evidence selection, cropping, and text-emphasis methods lacks clear distinction and direct comparisons.

2lwe43E1SI.one_liner: A method-of-types-inspired convergence score prioritizes stable token distributions to reduce uniform-state diffusion denoising steps.
2lwe43E1SI.problem: Confidence-based acceptance can leave stable but high-entropy token predictions unaccepted, causing redundant denoising.
2lwe43E1SI.method: The paper extends a method-of-types expression to consecutive soft token distributions to define Convergence Probability. Its training-free Convergence-Aware Entropy-Bounded Sampler uses this score with confidence and dependency considerations to prioritize converged positions.
2lwe43E1SI.key_idea: Compare consecutive soft token distributions with a method-of-types-inspired score and use it to accept stable positions earlier.
2lwe43E1SI.evidence: Experiments use DiffusionGemma across reasoning, coding, and instruction-following benchmarks and analyze entropy changes in neighboring positions.
2lwe43E1SI.claimed_gains: The proposed method reduces denoising steps by 9.9%--28.9%, while existing methods range from a 78.2% increase to a 7.0% reduction.
2lwe43E1SI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between convergence and confidence useful and recognize consistent training-free denoising-step reductions.
2lwe43E1SI.main_concern: The method-of-types derivation does not justify interpreting the score as a convergence probability or preserving the original dependency bound.

0IxB0J7Jp4.one_liner: Trains block-diffusion speculative decoding drafters with a sequence-level loss derived directly from the block verification acceptance rule.
0IxB0J7Jp4.problem: Block diffusion drafters propose multiple tokens in parallel for sequence-level block verification, but existing drafter training losses optimize independent token-level acceptance.
0IxB0J7Jp4.method: The authors derive Block Verification-aware loss (BV loss) directly from the block verification acceptance rule using a change-of-measure formulation and a practical annealed logarithmic surrogate. Training with BV loss maximizes the expected accepted prefix length of a drafted token block without altering the inference-time verification procedure.
0IxB0J7Jp4.key_idea: Optimizes block diffusion drafters to maximize expected accepted sequence length under the exact prefix-dependent block verification acceptance probability.
0IxB0J7Jp4.evidence: Evaluated on math, code, and chat benchmarks using DFlash and DSpark drafters with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B targets against cross-entropy, KL, TV, and LK losses.
0IxB0J7Jp4.claimed_gains: Increases the mean number of tokens accepted per verification call under block verification by 13.0-21.0% over cross-entropy loss training for DFlash and DSpark with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B.
0IxB0J7Jp4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that aligning the drafter training objective with sequence-level block verification is well motivated, introduces zero inference overhead, and consistently increases accepted token lengths.
0IxB0J7Jp4.main_concern: Reviewers view the formulation as a natural extension of prior acceptance-aware losses (such as LK loss) to block verification and note the evaluation is limited to 100K training examples on Qwen3-4B/8B.

4i1Qp323Hw.one_liner: Aligns training and deployment source distributions in flow-matching visuomotor policies by recursively initializing training flows from detached self-generated action previews.
4i1Qp323Hw.problem: Few-step flow-matching visuomotor policies suffer from a train-deployment mismatch when initialized from expert action sources during training but from the policy's own predicted action previews at deployment.
4i1Qp323Hw.method: Recursive Action-Preview Flow Matching (RAP) carries forward the unexecuted portion of the previous action forecast as the starting source for the next flow-matching generation cycle, refined by current observations. During offline training, RAP recursively constructs flow sources from detached policy-generated action previews (SG-RST) and fuses preview visual context with current observations via temporal visual fusion (TVF) without manual Gaussian noise tuning.
4i1Qp323Hw.key_idea: Constructs flow-matching initial sources during training from the policy's own detached multi-step action previews to match test-time warm-start action generation.
4i1Qp323Hw.evidence: Evaluated across 8 simulated tasks from 4 benchmarks and 2 real-world robot tasks with 1 or 3 inference steps against WarmPrior (WP-Preview), A2A, and VITA.
4i1Qp323Hw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training on recursively self-generated action previews directly addresses the train-test source mismatch in warm-started flow-matching policies without adding inference latency.
4i1Qp323Hw.main_concern: Reviewers note that training on detached model predictions closely parallels scheduled sampling, DAgger, and self-conditioning without adequate citation, and that real-world task gains over WP-Preview are small (1-2 trials out of 20).

jrZeSleifR.one_liner: Monitors cross-modal representation convergence during MLLM generation to selectively intensify activation steering when harmful visual inputs align with text safety directions.
jrZeSleifR.problem: Text-based safety representation steering often fails at the start of generation on harmful visual inputs because visual representations initially diverge from text-like safety patterns, leading to delayed refusal.
jrZeSleifR.method: Convergence-Aware Representation Steering (CARS) is a training-free inference-time defense that applies mild initial safety steering while monitoring the alignment of evolving hidden representations with text-based safety patterns via a lightweight classifier. When harmful cross-modal convergence is detected at a later token position, CARS triggers stronger representation steering and deletes unsafe prefix tokens.
jrZeSleifR.key_idea: Monitors generated hidden states with a text-safety classifier and dynamically escalates activation steering plus prefix deletion once multimodal representations converge toward text safety directions.
jrZeSleifR.evidence: Evaluated across three MLLMs on FigStep, MM-SafetyBench, ToViLaG, and Jailbreak-28K for safety, and ScienceQA and MM-Vet for utility.
jrZeSleifR.claimed_gains: Achieves 92.3% average defense success rate across FigStep, MM-SafetyBench, ToViLaG, and Jailbreak-28K with 0.1-1.3% utility degradation on ScienceQA and MM-Vet.
jrZeSleifR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that empirical characterization of the delayed refusal phenomenon in MLLMs is insightful and that the training-free inference-time defense achieves strong safety-utility trade-offs.
jrZeSleifR.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the observed representation convergence reflects genuine cross-modal alignment rather than the accumulation of generated text tokens in the prefix, and note incomplete ablations isolating prefix deletion from dynamic steering.

RQR7PKybm4.one_liner: Extracts critical specification intents and injects file-relevant intent reminders into coding agent contexts at file-creation checkpoints to prevent specification drift.
RQR7PKybm4.problem: During long-horizon repository generation, coding agents gradually lose track of fine-grained implementation intents in large task specifications, leading to conflicting conventions and incorrect implementations.
RQR7PKybm4.method: SIRA induces transferable intent-extraction guidance offline from discrepancies between task specifications and generated repositories on prior tasks, then builds a compact index of behaviorally critical intents for the current task. Whenever the agent creates a new file, SIRA retrieves file-relevant intents from this index and injects them into the agent's context for local self-correction.
RQR7PKybm4.key_idea: Builds an index of specification intents using offline-derived discrepancy rules and retrieves file-specific intents into the coding agent's context upon each new file creation.
RQR7PKybm4.evidence: Evaluated on the NL2Repo and RepoGenesis repository-generation benchmarks alongside a manual failure taxonomy of specification drift.
RQR7PKybm4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the failure-mode analysis of specification drift in repository generation and agree that injecting relevant specification intents at file-creation checkpoints is simple, low-overhead, and practical.
RQR7PKybm4.main_concern: Reviewers point out that offline rule extraction is static (making "self-improved" an overstatement and overlapping with uncited works like ExpeL) and that triggering only on new file creation misses drift during subsequent file edits.

9phg9cFsPx.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agents on 40 paper-derived Earth-science workflows requiring production of datasets validated against expert references and independent observations.
9phg9cFsPx.problem: Existing scientific LLM benchmarks focus on question answering rather than evaluating whether agents can execute long-horizon workflows that transform heterogeneous raw Earth data into research-quality datasets.
9phg9cFsPx.method: EarthDataBench provides 40 executable tasks derived from published Earth-science papers across seven topics, requiring agents to integrate raw data and domain methods to produce complete data products. Its evaluation protocol combines scientific-consistency checks, similarity comparisons against expert-reconstructed reference products, and validation against independent real-world observations.
9phg9cFsPx.key_idea: Evaluates agent-generated scientific datasets using a multi-level grading ladder combining scientific consistency checks, expert-product similarity, and independent observational validation.
9phg9cFsPx.evidence: Evaluated across 11 LLMs and 17 model-harness configurations on 40 executable tasks spanning seven Earth-science topics.
9phg9cFsPx.claimed_gains: Across 11 LLMs and 17 model-harness configurations, 59.2% of outcomes pass scientific-consistency checks, 15.0% reach expert-reference quality or higher, and 0.7% outperform expert references on independent validation.
9phg9cFsPx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating complete scientific data-product generation against expert artifacts and independent observations is a valuable step beyond QA-style Earth-science benchmarks.
9phg9cFsPx.main_concern: Reviewers note inconsistencies between the main text's claimed cumulative scoring ladder and the task-specific grading rules in the appendix, alongside a small sample size of 40 tasks and single-run evaluations.

MQ7WVNjG4t.one_liner: Relaxes sparsest-permutation causal discovery by restricting Cholesky factorization and fill-in to a precision-support mask for high-dimensional linear SEMs.
MQ7WVNjG4t.problem: Sparsest-permutation causal discovery requires exact all-entry Cholesky evaluations across candidate variable orderings, making it computationally prohibitive for high-dimensional datasets.
MQ7WVNjG4t.method: Relaxed Sparsest-Permutation (ReSP) constrains the Cholesky factorization of the covariance matrix in linear structural equation models to hold only within a screened precision-support mask while forcing the lower-triangular factor to be zero outside the mask. The authors prove population-level Markov equivalence recovery under sparsest Markov representation assumptions and instantiate ReSP using an approximate minimum degree ordering with local refinement.
MQ7WVNjG4t.key_idea: Restricts ordering-dependent Cholesky factorization equality and non-zero fill-in to a pre-screened precision-matrix support mask during permutation-based DAG search.
MQ7WVNjG4t.evidence: Supported by population-level theoretical guarantees for Gaussian linear SEMs and empirical evaluations scaling up to 10^4 variables (and TCGA with p ≈ 16k) and sample sizes up to 10^6.
MQ7WVNjG4t.claimed_gains: Scales to 10^4 variables with n < p and improves structural recovery as sample size increases to 10^6.
MQ7WVNjG4t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that precision-support masking during Cholesky evaluation provides a clean, practical speedup and accuracy gain for high-dimensional linear causal discovery.
MQ7WVNjG4t.main_concern: Reviewers note that restricting DAG search to the precision support (moral graph) closely follows prior frameworks like ARGES, and that theoretical exact-recovery guarantees require an admissibility condition that collapses the relaxation back to exact factorization.

5VKK6p9F7b.one_liner: Combines null-space-constrained orthogonal matrix parameterization with gradient-guided block permutation for multimodal continual instruction tuning.
5VKK6p9F7b.problem: In multimodal continual instruction tuning, standard orthogonal fine-tuning does not prevent interference with previous tasks, while naively imposing a null-space constraint breaks orthogonality and limits plasticity under a fixed block-diagonal structure.
5VKK6p9F7b.method: Null-space Orthogonal Fine-Tuning (NOFT) parameterizes task-specific weight transformations to jointly satisfy orthogonal and previous-task null-space constraints for continual stability. To improve plasticity without adding parameters, it introduces a plasticity-aware permutation that rearranges trainable block-diagonal positions based on current-task gradient magnitudes.
5VKK6p9F7b.key_idea: Parameterizes block-diagonal orthogonal transformations within the null space of previous-task features while permuting block rows/columns by current-task gradient information.
5VKK6p9F7b.evidence: Evaluated with LLaVA-v1.5-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B on two multimodal continual instruction tuning benchmarks (UCIT and TriGap) against continual learning baselines including SICO, KeepLoRA, SAME, and CL-MoE.
5VKK6p9F7b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the joint null-space and orthogonal parameterization is clearly formulated and achieves consistent performance improvements across two MLLM backbones and two continual instruction tuning benchmarks.
5VKK6p9F7b.main_concern: Reviewers note that null-space projection for continual learning and block-permuted orthogonal fine-tuning have been separately explored in prior works (e.g., Adam-NSCL, NESS, PSOFT, BOFT, GSOFT), and that the permutation module adds modest gains relative to its complexity.

WM9GcZjHxl.one_liner: Establishes finite-probe identifiability and universality for neural functionals and learns network properties from intermediate hidden-layer probe responses.
WM9GcZjHxl.problem: Probing methods that predict properties of trained neural networks from input-output queries lack theoretical guarantees on when finite probes suffice and underutilize intermediate hidden states.
WM9GcZjHxl.method: The authors prove theoretical identification and universal approximation results showing that finite probe sets suffice to identify neural networks and approximate neural functionals, and that intermediate hidden representations are more informative than final outputs alone. Motivated by this theory, they propose HIDDENPROBE, an architecture that aggregates intermediate hidden-layer responses to learned probe inputs to predict network properties.
WM9GcZjHxl.key_idea: Sends a finite set of learned synthetic probe inputs through a target network and extracts intermediate hidden-layer activations to predict network functional properties.
WM9GcZjHxl.evidence: Supported by theoretical identifiability and universality theorems for MLPs and Transformers, and evaluated across eleven neural functional benchmark settings covering MLPs, CNNs, INRs, and Transformers.
WM9GcZjHxl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that establishing theoretical identifiability and universality for finite hidden-layer probing is valuable and that HiddenProbe shows consistent empirical gains across diverse network architectures.
WM9GcZjHxl.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between the theoretical assumptions (e.g., injective activations) and experimental settings (e.g., sine-activated INRs), unclear architectural details in the main text, and missing layer-wise ablations isolating which hidden layers drive the gains.

J2AocPT9RY.one_liner: Combines coarse learned pose correction, D-optimal frame scheduling, and a learned weighted Levenberg-Marquardt solver for surgical robot-camera extrinsic calibration.
J2AocPT9RY.problem: Camera-robot extrinsic calibration in surgical videos degrades under specular reflections, articulated tool motion, occlusion, and poor initialization when using either pure analytical fitting or direct black-box pose regression.
J2AocPT9RY.method: SurgURDF-Calib uses a two-stage geometry-structured optimization pipeline that retains an analytical SE(3) solver: first, a learned module predicts a coarse sequence-level extrinsic correction from a motion- and visibility-filtered candidate pool; second, observability-aware D-optimal frame scheduling and a learned sparse Levenberg-Marquardt solver adaptively estimate geometric factor weights and anisotropic damping. The authors also introduce the SurgURDF-100K synthetic benchmark with 1,000 sequences and 100K annotated observations.
J2AocPT9RY.key_idea: Predicts coarse SE(3) initialization, D-optimal frame subsets, and per-factor weights and anisotropic damping around an analytical sparse Levenberg-Marquardt solver using URDF kinematics.
J2AocPT9RY.evidence: Evaluated on the newly created SurgURDF-100K benchmark (1,000 surgical sequences, 100K annotated observations) and real surgical videos.
J2AocPT9RY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning optimizer controls (frame selection, factor weights, and damping) around an analytical SE(3) solver is well motivated and that the SurgURDF-100K dataset is a useful contribution.
J2AocPT9RY.main_concern: Reviewers point out that real-world evaluation lacks ground-truth extrinsics and reuses fitting masks for IoU scoring, while baseline comparisons may be unfair due to ground-truth mask inputs and lack of strong classical robust-LM baselines.

ZaIfvnOm0n.one_liner: Analyzes puzzle-to-math RL reasoning transfer with a 9-class primitive classifier and preserves backtracking via a reference-perplexity novelty bonus.
ZaIfvnOm0n.problem: Post-training language models on constraint-satisfaction puzzles with vanilla reinforcement learning improves chain-of-thought length and math performance but systematically suppresses exploratory backtracking behavior.
ZaIfvnOm0n.method: The authors analyze cross-domain reasoning transfer from puzzle-only SFT and RL to hard mathematics using a 9-class span classifier that tracks reasoning primitives across training stages. To counteract the suppression of backtracking by vanilla GSPO, they add a novelty reward bonus for correct rollouts based on perplexity under the frozen reference model.
ZaIfvnOm0n.key_idea: Rewards correct RL rollouts that have higher perplexity under the frozen reference policy to preserve SFT-induced backtracking behaviors during puzzle-to-math transfer.
ZaIfvnOm0n.evidence: Evaluated across two model families (including OLMo3-7B) trained solely on constraint-satisfaction puzzles via SFT and GSPO and tested out-of-domain on hard math benchmarks including OlymMATH-Hard.
ZaIfvnOm0n.claimed_gains: The end-to-end puzzle-only recipe raises hard-math pass@32 by 20 points on OlymMATH-Hard for OLMo3-7B.
ZaIfvnOm0n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean out-of-domain puzzle-to-math experimental setup, the controlled A/B comparison between vanilla and novelty-bonus GSPO, and the fine-grained primitive behavioral analysis.
ZaIfvnOm0n.main_concern: Reviewers note that the causal link between restored backtracking and math accuracy gains is correlational rather than isolated from other behavioral shifts caused by the perplexity bonus, and experiments focus primarily on 7B models and a single puzzle setup.

4tLmF1Ubxf.one_liner: Uses a recurrent relational proposer to generate complementary joint sensing action groups evaluated under a small physics-forecast budget.
4tLmF1Ubxf.problem: Under shared receiver uncertainty, greedy or individual action scoring fails to capture complementary sensing synergies—such as pairing a calibration action with a target observation—when a physics-based evaluator can afford only a few forecasts.
4tLmF1Ubxf.method: The authors show via a two-slot Gaussian construction that individual or greedy action screening can recover an arbitrarily small fraction of optimal variance reduction, and introduce a recurrent relational proposer. Conditioned on a joint target-receiver belief, the proposer generates candidate groups of sensing actions and continuous controls while predicting their post-projection cost so a budgeted physics-based evaluator can select the best group.
4tLmF1Ubxf.key_idea: Generates candidate multi-action sensing groups and continuous controls from a joint target-receiver belief using a recurrent relational network for budgeted physics-based forecast selection.
4tLmF1Ubxf.evidence: Supported by a theoretical two-slot Gaussian suboptimality proposition and evaluated on 192 simulated cognitive-radar multi-target tracking test episodes across eight scenarios against numerical search and exhaustive pairwise forecasting.
4tLmF1Ubxf.claimed_gains: On 192 simulated test episodes across eight scenarios, it reduces mean GOSPA by 15.0% and RF energy by 7.0% relative to numerical search under matched budgets, achieves 1.22 m lower mean GOSPA than search with four times the forecasts, and reaches a median 99% of the best action pair's gain with twelve forecasts.
4tLmF1Ubxf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the two-slot Gaussian example and theoretical motivation clearly illustrate why joint sensing actions must be evaluated together under shared receiver uncertainty.
