4tLmF1Ubxf.main_concern: Reviewers find the manuscript poorly organized and difficult to follow—with undefined notation, delayed references, and missing related work comparisons on correlated sensor selection—and note that evaluation is limited to simulation.

h0ONXA8IFt.one_liner: Identifies recurring gene-wise prediction error fingerprints in virtual-cell perturbation models and reuses them post-hoc to correct unseen-perturbation predictions.
h0ONXA8IFt.problem: Prediction errors in single-cell transcriptional perturbation models are typically discarded as random residual noise rather than exploited as systematic, recurring failure patterns.
h0ONXA8IFt.method: The authors systematically analyze prediction residuals across ten virtual-cell predictors and genetic, combinatorial, and chemical perturbation datasets, showing that gene-wise over- and under-estimation fingerprints recur across held-out perturbations within the same cell line. They introduce Gap Transferability Correction (GTC), a post-hoc correction method that estimates historical error structure from training perturbations to adjust predictions on unseen interventions without retraining.
h0ONXA8IFt.key_idea: Extracts persistent gene-wise residual error fingerprints from training perturbations and applies a post-hoc correction to predictions on unseen perturbations within the same cell line.
h0ONXA8IFt.evidence: Evaluated across ten single-cell perturbation prediction models on genetic, combinatorial, and drug perturbation datasets across multiple cell lines.
h0ONXA8IFt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating virtual-cell prediction residuals as structured, transferable fingerprints is an interesting and practical perspective supported by broad evaluation across ten models.
h0ONXA8IFt.main_concern: Reviewers note that the analysis is restricted to pseudobulk averages rather than single-cell distributions, provides limited biological explanation for why specific genes are mispredicted, and shows weak transfer across different cell types.

MfNPixduM2.one_liner: Benchmarks coding agents on 450 functionality-prompted tasks across seven languages and three granularities using hidden behavioral security tests.
MfNPixduM2.problem: AI coding agents are widely used for functionality-driven "vibe coding," but existing evaluations rarely test whether code generated without explicit security prompts is vulnerable to real-world exploits across function, file, and repository scales.
MfNPixduM2.method: The Last Secure Code Benchmark (LSCBench) constructs 450 tasks from 150 real historical vulnerabilities across seven programming languages and 24 CWEs at function, file, and repository-from-scratch granularities. Agents receive only functional specifications with no mention of security, and outputs are graded in isolated environments using hidden functional test suites and executable proof-of-concept security attacks.
MfNPixduM2.key_idea: Grades functionality-only coding prompts across function, file, and repository levels using hidden executable proof-of-concept exploit tests derived from 150 real vulnerabilities.
MfNPixduM2.evidence: Evaluated across six frontier coding agents (including Claude Fable 5) on 450 tasks spanning Java, C, C++, JavaScript, Python, PHP, and Go across 24 CWEs.
MfNPixduM2.claimed_gains: Across six frontier agents, 73.6% to 91.3% of tasks pass functionally, but Claude Fable 5 produces code that is both functional and secure on only 25.1% of tasks (and 12% across all three vibe-coding settings), while other agents achieve 16.4% to 24.7%.
MfNPixduM2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the executable behavioral security tests, the anti-gaming controls (such as narrated comment-only checks), and the coverage across seven languages and three task granularities.
MfNPixduM2.main_concern: Reviewers point out that omitting security requirements creates construct-validity ambiguity for policy-dependent vulnerabilities like SSRF or authorization where secure behavior is not uniquely inferable from functional prompts alone.

C6kMhoBEeW.one_liner: Predicts composite scene depth via encoder-feature-supervised corrections to a frozen depth estimator to condition reference-based RGB object compositing.
C6kMhoBEeW.problem: Reference-based image compositing from a background, reference object, and 2D mask leaves 3D scene geometry implicit, often causing structural distortion or implausible object placement.
C6kMhoBEeW.method: Depth-to-RGB (D2R) trains reference-conditioned corrective layers on top of a frozen depth estimator using encoder features of completed ground-truth scenes as supervision targets, then decodes the predicted composite depth via the frozen depth decoder. A second-stage RGB synthesis model renders the final composite image conditioned on the fixed predicted composite depth map.
C6kMhoBEeW.key_idea: Adapts a frozen depth estimator with encoder-feature supervision to predict completed-scene depth from background, mask, and reference inputs before depth-conditioned RGB rendering.
C6kMhoBEeW.evidence: Evaluated on the newly introduced AnyInsertion++ benchmark (with paired in-distribution and category-disjoint splits) and three unpaired benchmarks against 12 open-source and 3 closed-source baselines.
C6kMhoBEeW.claimed_gains: Encoder-feature supervision reduces OOD Stage-1 AbsRel by 31.4% over decoded-depth supervision; on category-disjoint data, D2R reduces AbsRel by 43.7% and improves PSNR by 2.4 dB over the matched RGB baseline, and reduces mean CLIP reference cosine distance by 55% across three unpaired benchmarks.
C6kMhoBEeW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly predicting completed-scene depth prior to RGB synthesis is a well-motivated factorization that yields clear geometric and photometric improvements over the matched RGB baseline.
C6kMhoBEeW.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the two-stage depth pipeline remains advantageous against stronger modern image-editing backbones (such as FLUX or Qwen) or under coarse user masks, and note missing architectural details and related work in the main text.

ug2ONLMU65.one_liner: Pairs moderate weight decay with a large learning rate during dense INR fitting to reverse spectral drift and improve post-compression video quality.
ug2ONLMU65.problem: In implicit neural representation (INR) video compression, training the dense network longer improves dense reconstruction quality but eventually degrades quality after pruning and quantization due to spectral drift of weight energy toward weakly excited input directions.
ug2ONLMU65.method: The authors analyze local spectral dynamics of the optimizer during dense INR fitting, showing that weight energy drifts toward low-eigenvalue input directions without weight decay, increasing sensitivity to pruning and quantization. They propose SpecFit (Spectrally-Guided Dense Fitting), a drop-in training recipe that combines moderate weight decay with a large learning rate during dense fitting to reverse this spectral drift without changing the network, pruning rule, or quantizer.
ug2ONLMU65.key_idea: Combines moderate weight decay with a high learning rate during dense INR fitting to prevent weight energy from drifting into weakly excited spectral directions.
ug2ONLMU65.evidence: Supported by local spectral analysis of simplified optimizer dynamics and evaluated across three NeRV-based video compression backbones under standard three-stage and post-training quantization pipelines.
ug2ONLMU65.claimed_gains: Reduces PSNR BD-rate by 23-28% on average across three NeRV backbones relative to standard training.
ug2ONLMU65.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying why better dense INR fitting can hurt post-pruning and post-quantization quality is an insightful observation and that the drop-in hyperparameter adjustment achieves substantial BD-rate gains.
ug2ONLMU65.main_concern: Reviewers note that the method itself simply tunes AdamW weight decay and learning rate (similar to schedules in prior work like NVRC) and that the theoretical spectral analysis relies on simplified linear, scalar-preconditioned assumptions.

KgmvD7jG7R.one_liner: Benchmarks dense egocentric atomic action captioning with temporal boundaries and hand assignments across 1,407 episodes and 41,132 human-refined annotations.
KgmvD7jG7R.problem: Existing egocentric video benchmarks lack fine-grained atomic action decomposition, precise sub-second temporal boundaries, and explicit left/right/bimanual hand-action associations needed for embodied learning.
KgmvD7jG7R.method: EgoActionBench provides 1,407 egocentric manipulation episodes containing 41,132 human-refined atomic action annotations labeled with start/end timestamps and acting hand (left, right, or both). It pairs the dataset with a ground-truth-anchored evaluation protocol (EgoActionScore) that matches temporally eligible predictions by content agreement to jointly score semantic fidelity, temporal overlap, hand accuracy, precision, and recall.
KgmvD7jG7R.key_idea: Evaluates continuous egocentric video understanding via dense atomic action annotations with per-hand tracks and a ground-truth-anchored matching protocol scoring semantics, timing, and hand assignment.
KgmvD7jG7R.evidence: Evaluated across 20 baseline models and two backbones (Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B) adapted via SFT and RL on automatically annotated training episodes from Ego4D, EPIC-KITCHENS, and EgoLife.
KgmvD7jG7R.claimed_gains: Adapting Qwen3-VL-4B and LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B via SFT and RL improves EgoActionScore by 15.9 and 23.2 points, respectively.
KgmvD7jG7R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint recovery of atomic manipulation actions, fine temporal intervals, and left/right hand assignments is a well-motivated and challenging benchmark task for egocentric video understanding.
KgmvD7jG7R.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the matching metric allows one prediction to match multiple ground-truth actions without penalizing extra predictions, relies on a single unvalidated LLM judge, and lacks transparency on automatic training-data generation and split disjointness.

m9HLPIXnjR.one_liner: Serializes sender-refined entropy scale decisions into packet-local side information so neural video codecs remain entropy-decodable under packet loss.
m9HLPIXnjR.problem: In context-adaptive neural video codecs, packet loss causes the receiver's inferred entropy coding distribution to diverge from the sender's, corrupting symbol decoding even for intact residual payloads.
m9HLPIXnjR.method: The authors formalize entropy-condition locality—requiring that the coding distribution for an intact payload not depend on erased packets—and introduce SEAL (Sender-decided Entropy with Assured Locality). SEAL performs rich conditional context modeling solely at the sender and compresses the final entropy scale parameter into packet-local side information bound to each residual payload, ensuring identical sender and receiver decoding distributions regardless of losses elsewhere.
m9HLPIXnjR.key_idea: Binds sender-computed conditional entropy scale parameters as packet-local side information to each residual payload so receiver arithmetic decoding never depends on lost packets.
m9HLPIXnjR.evidence: Evaluated on a DCVC-RT backbone using causal CDF-substitution interventions and end-to-end 1500-byte MTU IPv4/UDP network emulation with Reed-Solomon FEC comparisons.
m9HLPIXnjR.claimed_gains: Holding retained payloads byte-identical and correcting only the entropy condition recovers +5.64 dB at 2% target packet loss.
m9HLPIXnjR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean isolation of receiver entropy-distribution desynchronization under packet loss, the concept of entropy-condition locality, and the realistic MTU packet-level transport evaluation.
m9HLPIXnjR.main_concern: Reviewers note that transmitting packet-local entropy side information incurs a substantial clean rate-distortion penalty compared to the original DCVC-RT backbone and that clean RD curves against standard non-FEC anchors are not thoroughly reported.

2m3JuNgARS.one_liner: Accelerates text-to-layer RGBA diffusion via online alpha-support prediction, layer-wise flow-endpoint skipping, and sparse DiT token evaluation.
2m3JuNgARS.problem: Text-to-layer diffusion models suffer from high inference latency when denoising multi-layer RGBA stacks because standard diffusion accelerators ignore inter-layer convergence differences and intra-layer transparent-region sparsity.
2m3JuNgARS.method: HASTE uses a lightweight token-level regressor to predict each layer's non-transparent alpha support online during denoising and schedules computation hierarchically. Converged layers bypass DiT execution entirely via flow-matching endpoint extrapolation, while active layers evaluate only tokens inside their predicted alpha support using persistent KV caches.
2m3JuNgARS.key_idea: Predicts per-layer non-transparent alpha support online to bypass converged RGBA layers via flow extrapolation and restrict active DiT computation to opaque tokens.
2m3JuNgARS.evidence: Evaluated on the Crello benchmark across Qwen-Image-Layered and three additional text-to-layer diffusion backbones.
2m3JuNgARS.claimed_gains: On the Crello benchmark, HASTE accelerates Qwen-Image-Layered sampling by 3.22x with negligible quality loss.
2m3JuNgARS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting layer-level temporal convergence and intra-layer alpha-channel spatial sparsity is well tailored to multi-layer RGBA diffusion and achieves strong training-free speedups across backbones.
2m3JuNgARS.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations show layer-level temporal skipping alone achieves 3.07x speedup while adding spatial alpha-support sparsity yields only a marginal further gain to 3.19x, and criticize cluttered figures and missing reduced-step baselines.

rKJnKaoI8z.one_liner: Generates lost ancient Chinese character forms using a diffusion model with cross-script component pre-training, U-Net bottleneck conditioning, and unified patch sampling.
rKJnKaoI8z.problem: Existing generative methods for reconstructing lost ancient Chinese character forms underutilize cross-script component evolution priors and provide weak structural guidance during generation.
rKJnKaoI8z.method: The authors propose a diffusion model (Anc-Diff) that first pre-trains on paired cross-script character components to learn evolutionary component priors. During character generation, it injects conditional features into the U-Net bottleneck and applies a unified patch sampling strategy across stages to preserve local component correspondences.
rKJnKaoI8z.key_idea: Pre-trains a U-Net diffusion model on paired cross-script character components with unified patch sampling and injects target conditional features at the U-Net bottleneck.
rKJnKaoI8z.evidence: Evaluated on the Font-607 dataset across ancient Chinese script generation tasks (including Seal Script and Clerical Script from Regular Script inputs) against eight baselines.
rKJnKaoI8z.claimed_gains: On the Font-607 Seal Script generation task, the method reduces LPIPS from 0.2517 to 0.2346 and increases cosine similarity from 0.7841 to 0.8094.
rKJnKaoI8z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating cross-script component priors for ancient Chinese character restoration is well motivated and achieves quantitative and expert-rated improvements on Font-607.
rKJnKaoI8z.main_concern: Reviewers find the architectural novelty limited relative to standard U-Net diffusion conditioning and prior work like OBSD, and note that component pre-training uses extra training epochs and data without a compute-matched comparison.

oWZdVPezj4.one_liner: Decouples patch-level domain alignment from slide-level MIL aggregation via a two-stage training procedure for cross-hospital digital pathology.
oWZdVPezj4.problem: Directly applying domain adaptation objectives during end-to-end multiple instance learning on whole-slide images interferes with MIL attention aggregation and degrades cross-hospital classification performance.
oWZdVPezj4.method: AdaptMIL separates domain adaptation from MIL aggregation using a two-stage training strategy on frozen pathology foundation model patch features. Stage 1 trains a projection layer with a domain alignment objective (using simple pooling) to learn domain-invariant patch representations, and Stage 2 freezes or transfers these aligned features to train the MIL aggregation head.
oWZdVPezj4.key_idea: Decouples representation-level domain alignment from MIL attention-head training in two sequential stages so alignment gradients do not distort instance aggregation weights.
oWZdVPezj4.evidence: Evaluated across multiple WSI datasets, clinical tasks, frozen pathology foundation models, MIL architectures, and domain adaptation objectives.
oWZdVPezj4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-hospital domain shift on frozen foundation model features is a practical digital pathology problem and that the two-stage decoupling strategy is simple, easy to integrate, and empirically effective.
oWZdVPezj4.main_concern: Reviewers note that the two-stage training split is methodologically incremental and that the mechanistic explanation linking single-stage UDA failure to sparser attention concentration remains largely correlational.

kcoh6Fi3Pf.one_liner: Benchmarks scientific research agents on 184 evidence-graph-derived tasks using report rubrics and executable artifact tests, paired with an evidence-checking multi-agent harness.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.problem: Evaluating AI research agents is difficult because plausible written reports may not reflect valid underlying computations or faithful synthesis of scientific evidence.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.method: SciProdBench provides 184 research tasks across Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, and Physics derived from scientific evidence graphs that jointly define report rubrics and hidden executable tests for computational artifacts. The authors also introduce EulerFlow, a multi-agent harness that cross-checks reported claims against computational artifacts and execution logs to revise unsupported findings.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.key_idea: Constructs paired report rubrics and hidden executable artifact verifiers from a shared scientific evidence graph and uses a verification harness to cross-check claims against execution records.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.evidence: Evaluated across nine models and four agent harnesses (including Codex, Claude Code, and EulerFlow) on 184 tasks spanning Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, and Physics.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.claimed_gains: Agents meet 90-97% of instruction-following criteria but only 49-57% of evidence-synthesis criteria, while Codex and Claude Code raise reasoning scores by 10-23 points but lower execution scores by 6-9 points.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the joint evaluation of written scientific reports and underlying computational artifacts traced to shared evidence graphs across multiple scientific disciplines.
kcoh6Fi3Pf.main_concern: Reviewers point out that only 31 of the 184 tasks include executable tests, brittle file-format expectations can cause false execution zeros, and pretraining data contamination from published source papers is not systematically controlled.

7SLjO0NUzB.one_liner: Alternates cluster-based semantic compression with probe-loss-guided data expansion for closed-loop multimodal LLM mid-training curation.
7SLjO0NUzB.problem: Static data selection for multimodal LLM mid-training fails to both remove redundant image-text supervision and adapt the training mixture to the model's evolving learning needs.
7SLjO0NUzB.method: The authors propose a closed-loop mid-training data curation framework that first constructs an initial coverage-preserving dataset via cluster-level budget allocation based on image-text specificity and local semantic diversity. During training, it periodically evaluates reference-relative prediction loss gaps on a fixed probe set across semantic clusters to diagnose high-potential regions and acquire additional training samples.
7SLjO0NUzB.key_idea: Combines initial cluster-level semantic deduplication with periodic probe-set loss-gap diagnosis against a reference model to dynamically reallocate data acquisition across semantic clusters during mid-training.
7SLjO0NUzB.evidence: Evaluated under a matched sample budget on multimodal image-text understanding benchmarks across mid-training and subsequent SFT stages.
7SLjO0NUzB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining static semantic coverage compression with dynamic model-guided data expansion during mid-training is well motivated and clearly presented.
7SLjO0NUzB.main_concern: Reviewers note that the end-to-end curation pipeline incurs high computational overhead (embedding millions of pairs, training LoRA reference models, and evaluating a 500K probe set) for a modest average benchmark gain (64.7 vs 64.0 for static compression and 63.2 for random).

kOwCddSt9A.one_liner: Exponential residual flows augment discrete diffusion states with deterministic continuous residuals whose zero crossings trigger token transitions.
kOwCddSt9A.problem: Discrete diffusion lacks a direct analogue of the probability-flow ODE used for deterministic sampling and consistency distillation.
kOwCddSt9A.method: The framework adds a continuous residual for every token and position, evolving it under piecewise ODEs determined by diffusion rate matrices. Zero crossings change discrete states, and practical discretizations support masked and uniform diffusion plus consistency distillation.
kOwCddSt9A.key_idea: Evolve auxiliary exponential residuals deterministically and trigger discrete-state transitions when residuals reach zero.
kOwCddSt9A.evidence: A marginal-preservation proof and code and text generation experiments support the construction, with distillation and residual-conditioning ablations.
kOwCddSt9A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the deterministic augmented-flow construction technically interesting and useful as a basis for trajectory-based distillation.
kOwCddSt9A.main_concern: The practical distillation gains are not clearly attributable to learning the deterministic residual-conditioned endpoint map justified by the theory.

mgr1u4his9.one_liner: MoB3R predicts intra-exposure camera trajectories and uses motion-guided cross-attention to reconstruct sharp 3D Gaussians from blurred images.
mgr1u4his9.problem: Single-pose feed-forward reconstruction mismatches trajectory-based blur formation and exhibits motion-aligned pose bias even after fine-tuning.
mgr1u4his9.method: MoB3R adds motion tokens to recover exposure trajectories in the geometry stage. The appearance stage derives per-pixel motion fields for cross-attention-guided sharp reconstruction supervised by a cycle reblur loss.
mgr1u4his9.key_idea: Recover exposure trajectories from blur patterns and use their per-pixel motion fields to guide sharp Gaussian reconstruction.
mgr1u4his9.evidence: Synthetic and real blurred-scene experiments, including DL3DV and ExBluRF in the reviews, assess pose estimation, rendering, and component ablations.
mgr1u4his9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the motion-blur diagnosis and coherent motion-aware design, with consistent improvements in pose estimation and rendering.
mgr1u4his9.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not sufficiently control deblurring frontend strength, sharp-image supervision, and training budget to isolate the architectural contribution.

PPaHgSOHbd.one_liner: CMRE resamples companion queries around each fixed EEG retrieval query to measure context-dependent accuracy and prediction consistency.
PPaHgSOHbd.problem: Full-query evaluation hides whether structure-aware EEG-to-image retrieval gains and method rankings survive changes in query-set composition.
PPaHgSOHbd.method: CMRE repeatedly applies inference rules to sampled rows of a fixed query-gallery similarity matrix. It separates accuracy gains over independent retrieval from same-query Top-1 consistency across contexts.
PPaHgSOHbd.key_idea: Hold representations fixed while resampling each query's companion set to measure structural gains and context consistency separately.
PPaHgSOHbd.evidence: Leave-one-subject-out experiments on THINGS-EEG2 compare six frozen representations and six structure-aware inference rules.
PPaHgSOHbd.claimed_gains: Full-context Top-1 gains reach 20.40 percentage points, but the winning rule changes in 17 of 24 conditions (70.8%), with an average loss of 2.70 percentage points and a maximum loss of 8.29 percentage points when retaining it under reduced contexts.
PPaHgSOHbd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled comparison using fixed similarities and multiple representations and inference rules.
PPaHgSOHbd.main_concern: The incremental insight beyond existing query-set sensitivity studies is limited and remains largely descriptive.

a1Om8ScQkB.one_liner: Derives recovery ceilings and phase transitions for zero-filled spectral PLS with missing design and response entries.
a1Om8ScQkB.problem: Missingness can distort shared-direction estimates in ways that stronger signals cannot eliminate.
a1Om8ScQkB.method: The analysis studies rank-one regression with MCAR masking, zero filling, and a column-orthogonal design before masking. It derives high-signal overlaps and finite-signal recovery curves under explicit design conditions.
a1Om8ScQkB.key_idea: Analyze how masking attenuates response signals but also tilts design-side singular directions according to leverage and signal placement.
a1Om8ScQkB.evidence: Random-matrix proofs, a replica derivation, and simulations support the results, including nested Hadamard and random orthogonal designs.
a1Om8ScQkB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value precise theoretical characterizations of asymmetric missingness effects and supporting numerical results.
a1Om8ScQkB.main_concern: The rank-one, MCAR, pre-whitened setting limits practical applicability to naturally incomplete multivariate data.

ZlMVD0tngB.one_liner: Combines verified self-distillation and correctness-conditioned state editing to reduce review-induced persistence in wrong answers.
ZlMVD0tngB.problem: Telling LLMs their outputs are under review can bias self-judgments toward retaining incorrect initial answers.
ZlMVD0tngB.method: ReSET trains models with correctness-verified teacher responses and answer-distribution distillation to re-solve questions before judging answers. Correctness-conditioned state editing targets the internal shift associated with review framing.
ZlMVD0tngB.key_idea: Combine verified reassessment supervision with editing of review-induced internal-state shifts.
ZlMVD0tngB.evidence: Paired review-framing comparisons across 14 models accompany state interventions, ReSET ablations, and cross-task evaluations.
ZlMVD0tngB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled comparison of review framing and self-judgment an interesting behavioral investigation.
ZlMVD0tngB.main_concern: The evidence does not clearly connect changes in judgment to better answer correction or downstream agent reliability.

cRhOWQjkWS.one_liner: Retrieves and releases experience by functional stage so later tasks can reuse it before the source task finishes.
cRhOWQjkWS.problem: Task-level memory mismatches stage-specific needs and delays reuse until entire long-horizon tasks finish.
cRhOWQjkWS.method: EvoRelay organizes retrieval, extraction, and cross-task propagation around functional stages. Completed stages release experience asynchronously while their source tasks continue.
cRhOWQjkWS.key_idea: Make stage-aligned experience visible to subsequent tasks immediately after that stage completes.
cRhOWQjkWS.evidence: Evaluation covers SWE-bench Verified and AppWorld with four backbones, memory baselines, runtime measurements, and stage/retrieval/release ablations.
cRhOWQjkWS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear diagnosis of experience-matching and propagation delays and the breadth of evaluation.
cRhOWQjkWS.main_concern: Stage-level memory overlaps with prior work, leaving asynchronous scheduling as the main distinguishing contribution.

PbpjeNXYQM.one_liner: Uses handedness-signed rotary attention across atom pairs with parity-specific outputs to represent central and axial molecular chirality.
PbpjeNXYQM.problem: Molecular encoders must distinguish enantiomers while respecting atom relabeling and proper rotations.
PbpjeNXYQM.method: GSF-chi lets each stereogenic unit modulate all pairwise interactions through phase fields and handedness-signed query-key rotations. A C2 projection separates reflection-even ECD peak counts and positions from reflection-odd signs.
PbpjeNXYQM.key_idea: Apply stereogenic-unit handedness to global rotary attention interactions and separate output components by reflection parity.
PbpjeNXYQM.evidence: Symmetry proofs, property tests, coordinate-reflection audits, and central/axial chirality benchmarks accompany parameter-matched rotary-attention controls.
PbpjeNXYQM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit symmetry treatment and output-dependent parity construction.
PbpjeNXYQM.main_concern: Dense terminology and incomplete definitions of features, losses, and design choices make the method difficult to understand and reproduce.

6gaH0bS32a.one_liner: Synthesizes and filters web-agent trajectories with modular frontier-model annotators, then distills them into smaller local agents through supervised fine-tuning.
6gaH0bS32a.problem: Locally deployable small web agents lag behind costly proprietary frontier-model agents.
6gaH0bS32a.method: AGENT-AS-ANNOTATORS automates trajectory collection using modular LLM components for web tasks. Gemini 3 Pro generates 3000 trajectories across six WebArena environments, which are filtered for Qwen-3.5-9B supervised fine-tuning.
6gaH0bS32a.key_idea: Use modular frontier-model task generation, execution, and evaluation to produce filtered demonstrations for small web agents.
6gaH0bS32a.evidence: Evaluations include WebArena, WorkArena L1, Online-Mind2Web, additional transfer benchmarks, multiple student sizes, and pipeline ablations.
6gaH0bS32a.claimed_gains: WorkArena L1 success rises from 33.3% to 51.5%, while WebArena success reaches 41.5% versus Go-Browse's 21.7%.
6gaH0bS32a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a modest synthetic trajectory collection produces useful small-agent improvements and cross-environment transfer.
6gaH0bS32a.main_concern: The comparisons do not isolate the pipeline's specific contribution from teacher strength, trajectory quality, and generation budget.

h96lGxQY3q.one_liner: Encodes protein pairs into residue-pair maps with coordinate-aligned positional encoding to generate free-text interaction descriptions.
h96lGxQY3q.problem: Binary and fixed-label PPI models cannot express detailed interactions between protein pairs in free text.
h96lGxQY3q.method: PPI2Text encodes amino acid sequences with ESM3, constructs a map over residue pairs, and generates captions with Qwen3. PaCo-RoPE aligns each map axis with its protein's residue positions.
h96lGxQY3q.key_idea: Align the two axes of a residue-pair representation with protein sequence coordinates before language decoding.
h96lGxQY3q.evidence: A 351k-pair corpus synthesized from ten biological databases supports baseline comparisons, architectural ablations, and multiple evaluation protocols.
h96lGxQY3q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value free-form PPI captioning and the substantial, documented interaction-description corpus.
h96lGxQY3q.main_concern: The evaluation does not adequately establish independent biological factuality or prospective generalization beyond synthesized source evidence.

TBH2srystZ.one_liner: Estimates modality channel states and gates iterative cross-modal information exchange under noise and missingness.
TBH2srystZ.problem: Multimodal fusion often treats missing and noisy modalities separately while ignoring input reliability during attention.
TBH2srystZ.method: CAT-MF estimates existence, spectral noise proxies, and damage types for each modality. Shared iterative decoding accumulates cross-modal information while channel-modulated attention suppresses missing, noisy, or similarly damaged transfers.
TBH2srystZ.key_idea: Use estimated channel quality and damage type to gate repeated cross-modal messages accumulated in persistent state.
TBH2srystZ.evidence: Conditional convergence and information-gain analyses accompany multi-task noise/missingness experiments and parameter-matched iterative-fusion comparisons.
TBH2srystZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reliability-aware iterative fusion a coherent practical approach with useful controlled empirical support.
TBH2srystZ.main_concern: The inverse-SNR proxy lacks convincing mathematical justification and direct validation, especially after vector normalization.

xGhO1vLpyq.one_liner: Compares anonymized speech performances through human preferences across scene instructions, emotional transitions, and vocal reactions.
xGhO1vLpyq.problem: Speech naturalness and transcript accuracy do not adequately measure convincing performance of complex acting directions.
xGhO1vLpyq.method: Voice Acting Arena uses an LLM director to translate acting challenges into system-specific controls, then collects listener comparisons on several performance dimensions. It also releases an open-weight baseline and automatic scorers for authenticity and vocal-burst integration.
xGhO1vLpyq.key_idea: Evaluate fixed-script scene performances with separate listener judgments for acting quality, instruction fit, authenticity, and requested reactions.
xGhO1vLpyq.evidence: The first evaluation gathers 560 listener votes on eleven model entries, with challenges spanning 40 emotion targets and ten acting domains.
xGhO1vLpyq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate scene-level expressive-speech evaluation and the accompanying baseline and data resources.
xGhO1vLpyq.main_concern: Most reported votes lack a documented connection to the archived task registry, limiting reproducibility and confidence in the rankings.

N5YcFyoZhr.one_liner: Uses LoRA-ensemble probability intervals and dominance tests to choose between committing to an answer and returning candidate sets.
N5YcFyoZhr.problem: Single predictive distributions conflate uncertainty from ignorance with ambiguity and can support unwarrantedly confident LLM answers.
N5YcFyoZhr.method: CLLMs interpret a LoRA ensemble as a credal set and commit only when one answer's lower probability exceeds every alternative's upper probability. The rule operates on constrained answer tokens or semantic clusters of credal-decoded completions.
N5YcFyoZhr.key_idea: Apply interval dominance to lower and upper probabilities across plausible predictors at token and semantic levels.
N5YcFyoZhr.evidence: Experiments use Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B on OpenBookQA, CoQA, TriviaQA, and ARC-Challenge.
N5YcFyoZhr.claimed_gains: On multiple-choice questions, CTC commits on 73-91% of questions.
N5YcFyoZhr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find interval dominance an interpretable adaptation of imprecise-probability methods to LLM commitment.
N5YcFyoZhr.main_concern: Main evaluations emphasize scalar confidence scores rather than directly comparing the proposed interval-dominance commitment decisions.

J17cCOyqiG.one_liner: Analyzes early autoencoder training to derive intervals where inlier reconstructions separate from outliers.
J17cCOyqiG.problem: The empirical tendency to learn inliers before outliers lacks a sufficiently precise theoretical explanation.
J17cCOyqiG.method: The theory compares actual training with a cluster-center reference trajectory for a fixed-decoder autoencoder trained by full-batch gradient descent. It derives separation intervals and studies compact representations and EMA-based initialization as practical extensions.
J17cCOyqiG.key_idea: Track contraction of cluster-shared reconstruction residuals relative to sample-specific residuals to certify temporary inlier-outlier separation.
J17cCOyqiG.evidence: Theoretical separation guarantees accompany matched-setting simulations and a four-way practical ablation on eleven tabular datasets.
J17cCOyqiG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a concrete training-dynamics account of when inlier memorization and outlier separation occur.
J17cCOyqiG.main_concern: The feasibility of the theoretical assumptions and their quantitative connection to observed memorization intervals remain unverified.

vUrKrGbqhx.one_liner: Bounds GNN generalization using message-passing structural complexity and adds structural entropy regularization to control cross-class propagation.
vUrKrGbqhx.problem: GNN generalization analyses underexplore the contribution of message-passing structure relative to parameter complexity.
vUrKrGbqhx.method: The paper defines structural complexity and derives a transductive Rademacher generalization bound. It introduces structural entropy regularization as a differentiable surrogate for cross-class information-propagation complexity.
vUrKrGbqhx.key_idea: Penalize structural entropy associated with cross-class message passing using a surrogate motivated by structure-aware generalization analysis.
vUrKrGbqhx.evidence: Generalization and surrogate bounds accompany experiments incorporating the regularizer into multiple GNN architectures and datasets.
vUrKrGbqhx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers consider message-passing structure a relevant generalization factor and appreciate evaluation across models and datasets.
vUrKrGbqhx.main_concern: The regularizer controls weighted cross-class propagation, which is not clearly connected to the total structural complexity in the generalization bound.

1zTEKK69fE.one_liner: Mines likely student mistakes at expert states and trains action preferences without executing sampled actions.
1zTEKK69fE.problem: Supervised imitation reinforces expert actions without explicitly correcting the student's likely mistakes at those states.
1zTEKK69fE.method: Agentic-DPO samples one-step student actions at expert states and selects the most probable decision that differs from the expert's. A length-scaled DPO loss, SFT anchor, and action-schema augmentation train preference for the expert action.
1zTEKK69fE.key_idea: Construct expert-versus-student preference pairs from likely decision errors without environment rollouts.
1zTEKK69fE.evidence: Five closed-loop tasks cover tau-bench retail/airline, ALFWorld, WebShop, and StableToolBench with repeated seeds, matched controls, and tuning comparisons.
1zTEKK69fE.claimed_gains: At 9B, gains over equally augmented SFT are 5.9–15.2 points, recovering 93% (95% CI 77–111) of GRPO's tau-bench gain with 6.7× fewer GPU-hours; continued SFT and random negatives recover 21% and 69% of the gain.
1zTEKK69fE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value rollout-free correction of student errors and the extensive controls studying negative selection.
1zTEKK69fE.main_concern: The method combines established preference-training and hard-negative techniques, leaving decision-aware negative selection as its main methodological contribution.

gXjJXQ7MuB.one_liner: Coarsens graphs by clustering propagated features to preserve polynomial-filter outputs, with multilevel merging and degree-budgeted edge pruning.
gXjJXQ7MuB.problem: Existing graph-coarsening objectives do not preserve all learned combinations of propagated features and may create dense coarse graphs.
gXjJXQ7MuB.method: The method bounds polynomial-filter transfer error using a k-means objective on block Krylov features and minimizes it through multilevel Ward merging. Edge pruning after each level limits average degree.
gXjJXQ7MuB.key_idea: Cluster the block Krylov representation of node features to preserve the span of possible polynomial-filter outputs.
gXjJXQ7MuB.evidence: Two-sided transfer-error bounds accompany nine homophilic/heterophilic node-classification benchmarks and evaluations across five GNN backbones.
gXjJXQ7MuB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the quantitative preservation objective and broad evidence of training speedups.
gXjJXQ7MuB.main_concern: The theoretical guarantee covers node merging but excludes edge pruning used by the final algorithm.

Eczg2d48Lf.one_liner: Predicts a facing anchor and coarse bearing before localizing targets described through egocentric text in point-cloud maps.
Eczg2d48Lf.problem: Egocentric directional descriptions do not define unique map-space constraints even when referenced objects are correctly grounded.
Eczg2d48Lf.method: EgoT2P pairs map-frame and egocentric queries over matched maps and target locations. FoRLoc predicts a target-centered facing anchor, coarse target-to-anchor bearing, and auxiliary object correspondences before target-position estimation.
Eczg2d48Lf.key_idea: Estimate an intermediate target-centered reference state to interpret egocentric relations in map coordinates.
Eczg2d48Lf.evidence: Paired EgoT2P experiments compare five retrained T2P methods and include ablations of the intermediate reference-state signals.
Eczg2d48Lf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reference-frame mismatch is meaningful and that paired queries support useful controlled comparisons.
Eczg2d48Lf.main_concern: The query protocols also change directional partitions and information content, so the measured gap does not isolate reference-frame uncertainty.

XDYHGwnjyO.one_liner: Separates weighted prediction error into learning and drift terms to characterize nonstationary risk-minimization trade-offs.
XDYHGwnjyO.problem: Prediction under temporal dependence and distribution drift requires understanding how weighting balances estimation error against outdated data.
XDYHGwnjyO.method: The analysis derives oracle inequalities uniform over weight classes under mixing conditions, accounting for effective sample size and class complexity. Square-loss drift bounds cover structural breaks and smooth change in regression settings.
XDYHGwnjyO.key_idea: Decompose excess risk into weight-dependent learning and distribution-drift errors to expose a bias-variance trade-off.
XDYHGwnjyO.evidence: Theoretical analyses cover linear models, basis approximations, and neural networks, recovering minimax-optimal rates up to logarithmic factors in stationary unweighted cases.
XDYHGwnjyO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the learning-drift decomposition and theoretical treatment of weighted ERM beyond independent stationary data.
XDYHGwnjyO.main_concern: The full learning-plus-drift characterization has narrower scope than the general framework, relying on squared loss and structural drift assumptions.

adJGQ0mfBN.one_liner: Supervises discrete motion plans with persistent homology and routes them anatomically before continuous text-conditioned motion synthesis.
adJGQ0mfBN.problem: Composite text-to-motion generation needs global action organization while preserving diverse valid realizations.
adJGQ0mfBN.method: QuanTopo uses persistent homology of pose, root motion, and local change to supervise a discrete plan. The plan establishes anatomical context for continuous synthesis, with a text-and-duration-conditioned predictor providing the trajectory target at inference.
adJGQ0mfBN.key_idea: Give a discrete motion plan a topology-based information target and an anatomical conditioning role in continuous synthesis.
adJGQ0mfBN.evidence: HumanML3D and KIT-ML evaluations include composite-caption sequence scoring, human evaluation, capacity controls, plan interventions, and representation probes.
adJGQ0mfBN.claimed_gains: QuanTopo reports FID scores of 0.027/0.122 on HumanML3D/KIT-ML and composite-action sequence satisfaction of 0.804 versus 0.782 for the strongest baseline.
adJGQ0mfBN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motivated hierarchical design, extensive ablations, and competitive motion-generation results.
adJGQ0mfBN.main_concern: The evidence does not sufficiently isolate how topology supervision improves semantic action order beyond language and sequential generation.

kNN0EGDWI3.one_liner: Routes time series to specialist anomaly detectors using pretrained representations and competence labels learned from simulated tasks.
kNN0EGDWI3.problem: Different temporal dynamics favor different anomaly criteria, limiting fixed scoring mechanisms attached to foundation models.
kNN0EGDWI3.method: TS-Router estimates detector competence from frozen temporal representations using soft supervision from labeled simulations. At deployment it selects specialists without target anomaly labels and fits only those detectors unsupervisedly.
kNN0EGDWI3.key_idea: Learn relative detector competence on simulated tasks and predict suitable specialists from target-series representations before fitting.
kNN0EGDWI3.evidence: Experiments cover 16 real-world benchmarks and four metrics with foundation-model, unsupervised-detector, and routing-ablation comparisons.
kNN0EGDWI3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see practical value in selecting detectors before fitting and appreciate the broad benchmark evaluation.
kNN0EGDWI3.main_concern: It remains unclear when synthetic competence rankings transfer reliably to real-world temporal dynamics and anomalies.

ETM5cVneOg.one_liner: Traces LLM massive activations to function-token alignment with right-singular directions of MLP down-projections via SVD and interventions.
ETM5cVneOg.problem: Prior studies link massive activations in Transformer LLMs to attention sinks or numerical outliers without establishing the weight-space mechanism and token-level triggers that generate them.
ETM5cVneOg.method: Across 26 pretrained LLMs, the authors combine MLP and attention ablations, frequency-controlled token regression, singular value decomposition of MLP down-projection matrices, and causal singular-vector interventions (such as Haar randomization and projection). They test how alignment between function-token representations and dominant right-singular directions of W_down writes extreme residual-stream coordinates.
ETM5cVneOg.key_idea: Identify alignment between function-token representations and top right-singular vectors of MLP down-projection matrices as the causal generator of massive activations.
ETM5cVneOg.evidence: Component ablations, SVD analyses, frequency-controlled token analyses, and causal singular-vector interventions across 26 language models spanning multiple architectural families and scales.
ETM5cVneOg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the broad empirical coverage across 26 models—including transparent reporting of three exception models—and the weight-level SVD framework connecting token triggers to MLP geometry.
ETM5cVneOg.main_concern: Reviewers note missing causal-specificity controls (such as downstream perplexity impact and non-MA direction controls), dimension and projection ambiguities in multi-layer equations, heterogeneous function-token definitions, and omitted prior super-weight MLP literature.

UDW8voNKmU.one_liner: Protects motion-unstable video-LLM visual tokens using Eulerian risk proxies while merging consistent tokens along estimated temporal trajectories.
UDW8voNKmU.problem: Training-free video-LLM token compression methods rely on feature similarity or importance while ignoring local motion instability, causing dynamic visual details to be lost when merging across frames.
UDW8voNKmU.method: Risk-Gated Lagrangian Token Compression (LTC) estimates inter-frame token displacements and matching confidence via Token Flow Estimation, then computes an Eulerian Risk Diagnosis score from local motion kinematic statistics and low-confidence signals. Risk-Gated Lagrangian Aggregation exempts high-risk tokens from merging, aggregates remaining feature-consistent tokens along motion trajectories, and selects top-importance tokens within a fixed budget without training.
UDW8voNKmU.key_idea: Estimate local inter-frame token flow and motion-instability risk to exempt high-risk tokens from trajectory-wise token merging under a fixed budget.
UDW8voNKmU.evidence: Evaluated training-free across three video-LLMs (including Qwen3-VL) and three video understanding benchmarks against compression baselines (FastVID, FlashVID, OTT-Vid) with component ablations.
UDW8voNKmU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing merge-risky dynamic tokens from safely aggregable temporal trajectories via Eulerian and Lagrangian motion cues is a clear, well-motivated perspective for video token compression.
UDW8voNKmU.main_concern: Reviewers note marginal accuracy gains (0.2–0.3 percentage points) over simpler selection variants that scarcely justify the pipeline's complexity, alongside missing head-to-head inference latency comparisons against competing compression baselines.

uhX41mYTVu.one_liner: Iteratively probes activations and causal output interventions with an LLM agent to jointly explain sparse autoencoder features.
uhX41mYTVu.problem: Automated sparse autoencoder interpretability methods rely on expensive full-corpus activation scans and characterize input triggers separately from output intervention effects without linking their functional relationship.
uhX41mYTVu.method: Dual-End Agentic Feature Interpretation (DAFI) equips an LLM agent with on-demand short-context token probing and causal activation interventions, iteratively refining input-side, output-side, and input-to-output functional explanations via component-specific score feedback. Reusable interpretation skills distilled from successful refinement trajectories are transferred to held-out features and unseen model-SAE pairs.
uhX41mYTVu.key_idea: Use an iterative agent with short-context activation probing, output interventions, and component-specific feedback to refine input, output, and functional SAE explanations.
uhX41mYTVu.evidence: Evaluated on GemmaScope SAEs, cross-model skill-transfer settings, blinded human evaluations, and AxBench downstream feature-selection tasks against SAGE, Token Change, and coding-agent baselines.
uhX41mYTVu.claimed_gains: On GemmaScope, DAFI improves Input score by 13.1 percentage points over SAGE and Output score by 38.9 points over Token Change, while distilled skills raise the held-out joint pass rate from 58.0% to 92.0% and find non-equivalent input-output semantics in 70.7% of reliably interpreted features.
uhX41mYTVu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the engineering efficiency of dual-endpoint agentic refinement, cross-model transfer of distilled skills, and empirical analysis of mismatches between input triggers and output effects.
uhX41mYTVu.main_concern: Reviewers note potential evaluation circularity because the agent optimizes the same automated metrics used for testing without clearly separated held-out evidence, alongside missing tool and functional ablations and unexplained discrepancies with prior Gemma SAE baselines.

4YH7vRE8JL.one_liner: Accelerates diffusion language models via intermediate-trajectory consistency distillation followed by accuracy-and-step-efficiency reinforcement learning.
4YH7vRE8JL.problem: Open-source diffusion large language models require many iterative unmasking steps to preserve generation quality, while imitation-only distillation does not enforce intermediate trajectory consistency or discover faster decoding paths.
4YH7vRE8JL.method: SwiftDLM applies a two-stage training pipeline to diffusion language models: Stage 1 performs consistency distillation across intermediate unmasking trajectory states to enable skip-step parallel decoding, and Stage 2 applies trajectory-level reinforcement learning with a joint accuracy and step-count reward to explore shorter, accurate decoding paths.
4YH7vRE8JL.key_idea: Combine skip-step consistency distillation along intermediate unmasking trajectories with reinforcement learning that jointly rewards task accuracy and fewer decoding steps.
4YH7vRE8JL.evidence: Evaluated on LLaDA and Dream diffusion language models across mathematical reasoning (including GSM8K) and code generation (including MBPP) benchmarks against dLLM acceleration baselines such as dParallel.
4YH7vRE8JL.claimed_gains: Applied to LLaDA, SwiftDLM achieves an 8.9x speedup with a 6 percentage point accuracy improvement on GSM8K and an 11.3x speedup on MBPP while maintaining competitive performance.
4YH7vRE8JL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining trajectory distillation with step-aware reinforcement learning delivers strong accuracy-latency improvements on LLaDA and Dream across math and coding benchmarks.
4YH7vRE8JL.main_concern: Reviewers point out omitted citations and comparisons to closely related trajectory-distillation and efficiency-aware dLLM RL methods (such as CDLM, TraceRL, DiFFPO, and dUltra), as well as domain-separate Stage 2 checkpoints and single-setting ablations.

5XWuJBGHss.one_liner: Enforces piecewise-flat linear boundary conditions analytically inside Ehrenpreis-Palamodov Gaussian process priors for constant-coefficient linear PDEs.
5XWuJBGHss.problem: Existing physics-informed Gaussian processes, neural operators, and PINNs typically satisfy either the governing linear PDE or the boundary conditions only approximately rather than enforcing both strictly in sample paths.
5XWuJBGHss.method: Boundary Ehrenpreis-Palamodov Gaussian Processes (B-EPGPs) start from the Ehrenpreis-Palamodov exponential-wave representation of solutions to linear constant-coefficient PDEs and analytically constrain basis functions (such as via reflection on piecewise-flat boundaries) to satisfy homogeneous linear boundary conditions. Conditioning on finite observation data learns free hyperparameters while ensuring every prior and posterior sample path has zero PDE and boundary residuals by construction.
5XWuJBGHss.key_idea: Analytically restrict Ehrenpreis-Palamodov exponential-wave basis functions on piecewise-flat boundaries so GP prior and posterior draws satisfy both PDE and boundary conditions.
5XWuJBGHss.evidence: Universal approximation proof (Theorem 1), constructive PDE examples (including rectangular and heat equations), and comparisons against GP, PINN, neural-operator, and numerical solver baselines.
5XWuJBGHss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and provides a clean mathematical construction whose GP sample paths satisfy both linear constant-coefficient PDEs and boundary conditions exactly.
5XWuJBGHss.main_concern: Reviewers view restricting EPGP basis functions via reflection as incremental, note missing comparisons with closely related boundary-respecting Hilbert-space GP priors (Solin & Kok 2019; Solin & Sarkka 2020), and request standardized benchmark tables and clearer theorem assumptions.

YzIzgMLqXV.one_liner: Learns compact Boolean gate networks using parameter-free connection routing, tree-free Boolean convolutions, and adaptive discretization.
YzIzgMLqXV.problem: Discrete combinatorial structure makes it difficult to train compact Boolean logic-gate networks without large connectivity parameterization overhead or severe discretization accuracy drops.
YzIzgMLqXV.method: The authors combine three mechanisms for training Boolean logic networks: a parameter-free strategy for learning inter-gate connections, a spatial-locality convolutional Boolean kernel using fewer gate operations, and an adaptive discretization schedule that converts continuously relaxed gates into discrete Boolean operations. Resulting networks compile directly to Verilog hardware descriptions.
YzIzgMLqXV.key_idea: Combine parameter-free gate-connection selection, compact Boolean convolutional kernels, and adaptive continuous-to-discrete gate rounding to shrink Boolean logic networks.
YzIzgMLqXV.evidence: Evaluated on standard vision benchmarks (including MNIST) and additional modalities with component ablations and Verilog circuit-size and latency estimates.
YzIzgMLqXV.claimed_gains: Achieves higher accuracy on vision benchmarks with up to 47x fewer Boolean operations than prior methods, and reaches 99.38% MNIST accuracy at a reported 6.48 ns FPGA latency with a 7x smaller Verilog file.
YzIzgMLqXV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers are sharply split (ratings 1, 4, 3), with supportive reviews noting strong accuracy-versus-gate-count improvements and connection learning while the critical review finds core algorithms underspecified.
YzIzgMLqXV.main_concern: Reviewers flag underspecified algorithmic descriptions of adaptive discretization and convolution, missing comparisons to recent sparse logic-gate networks, and FPGA latency numbers derived from a heuristic circuit-depth formula rather than physical hardware measurement.

VFeiMi6ZzR.one_liner: Combines a multi-quantile Mamba deterministic forecaster with conditional flow-matching residual ensembles for extreme precipitation nowcasting.
VFeiMi6ZzR.problem: Pixel-wise regression objectives blur heavy-tailed radar precipitation forecasts and suppress extreme rain, while diffusion-based residual generators require many costly sampling steps.
VFeiMi6ZzR.method: PrecMamba splits radar precipitation nowcasting into a Mamba-based spatiotemporal deterministic backbone trained with an asymmetric multi-quantile pinball loss to preserve high-intensity events, followed by a conditional flow-matching generator that samples sharp stochastic residuals in a few integration steps.
VFeiMi6ZzR.key_idea: Train a Mamba spatiotemporal backbone with multi-quantile pinball loss to preserve heavy-rain peaks and model residual uncertainty via conditional flow matching.
VFeiMi6ZzR.evidence: Evaluated on four radar precipitation nowcasting benchmarks (SEVIR, MeteoNet, Shanghai Radar, and CIKM) against deterministic and deterministic-generative baselines such as SimVP, DiffCast, and DuoCast.
VFeiMi6ZzR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing quantile-loss deterministic forecasting with residual flow matching is well structured and delivers consistent Critical Success Index gains across four radar benchmarks, especially at extreme thresholds.
VFeiMi6ZzR.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons to prior Mamba nowcasting work (STVMamba), unisolated contributions of the Mamba backbone (which trails SimVP standalone), single-sample evaluation without multi-seed variance or probabilistic ensemble metrics, and heterogeneous copied baseline numbers.

kU0EKgFyvF.one_liner: CueMuse combines visual rhythm extraction with text and editable timestamp conditioning for video-to-music generation.
kU0EKgFyvF.problem: Video-to-music systems offer limited editing control and generalize poorly across general video scenarios.
kU0EKgFyvF.method: CueMuse trains a conditional music backbone on the web-derived Universe-MV dataset, using V-Beater for 12-fps visual rhythm detection and optional text or edited rhythm timestamps.
kU0EKgFyvF.key_idea: Editable visual-rhythm timestamps provide a separate rhythmic control channel alongside video and text conditioning.
kU0EKgFyvF.evidence: Subjective and objective experiments assess music-video alignment, generation quality, and musicality, primarily on the self-constructed Universe-Bench.
kU0EKgFyvF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optional text and editable rhythm controls are practical and that experiments show competitive generation and alignment.
kU0EKgFyvF.main_concern: Reviewers most often state that V-Beater and the video-conditioning contributions are not isolated from the pretrained backbone or simple rhythm alternatives.

NDdBJHmxCa.one_liner: Issue-centric continual GraphRAG preserves weak evidence and issue identities across temporal discourse updates.
NDdBJHmxCa.problem: Topic-tracking methods cannot decide when fragmented evidence becomes an issue or whether later observations continue the same issue.
NDdBJHmxCa.method: The CEID framework separates discourse, evidence, and issue representations, retains weak signals with insufficient support, and updates persistent issue identities through continual GraphRAG.
NDdBJHmxCa.key_idea: Separate evidence and issue graphs defer unsupported signals while preserving identity as discourse changes.
NDdBJHmxCa.evidence: A controlled temporal benchmark derived from real public-service feedback evaluates issue formation, discourse grounding, identity preservation, and emergence latency against four baseline families.
NDdBJHmxCa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that continual emerging issue discovery is well motivated and that persistent graph state is useful for tracking weak signals.
NDdBJHmxCa.main_concern: Reviewers most often object that LLM-generated discourse and LLM-derived ground truth provide no independent validation on real longitudinal discourse.

mCm6MwKprF.one_liner: Embed-TTT optimizes task embeddings before backbone tuning to induce rule-aligned ARC representations.
mCm6MwKprF.problem: ARC-like task success can reflect shortcuts rather than inference of the intended transformation rule.
mCm6MwKprF.method: The two-step protocol first fine-tunes only a VARC task embedding, then freezes it and fine-tunes the backbone, separating rule representation from task execution.
mCm6MwKprF.key_idea: Backbone-frozen test-time optimization forces a small task embedding to capture rule structure before model adaptation.
mCm6MwKprF.evidence: Experiments cover ARC-AGI-1, ConceptARC, Mini-ARC, and two controlled known-rule datasets using retrieval, linear probes, and qualitative relation analyses.
mCm6MwKprF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the protocol is clear and supported by broad analyses of embedding structure and compositional properties.
mCm6MwKprF.main_concern: Reviewers most often question empirical generality because validation uses only VARC and does not test other backbones or embedding designs.

Qwz6FleWa5.one_liner: Trainable biophysical circuits manipulate dendritic routing and calcium conductance to study learned context dependence.
Qwz6FleWa5.problem: The effect of dendritic input organization on learned sensorimotor mappings and context use remains unclear.
Qwz6FleWa5.method: Recurrent circuits of biophysically detailed neurons receive sensory and contextual inputs through apical or basal routes, with weight-exchange and calcium-blockade interventions during training and execution.
Qwz6FleWa5.key_idea: Dendritic routing and training-time calcium conductance alter sensory weights that determine later dependence on context.
Qwz6FleWa5.evidence: Controlled sensorimotor tasks compare routing configurations, context withdrawal, sensory-weight exchanges, shared training, and acute or training-time conductance blockade.
Qwz6FleWa5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the perturbation design, especially weight exchange and calcium blockade, carefully investigates dendritic contributions to context use.
Qwz6FleWa5.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the computational mechanism unclear, with limited explanation of why routing and training history produce the observed differences.

5f7tLJjygV.one_liner: AgentSWE grades coding agents on held-out requirements for creating, editing, and optimizing agents.
5f7tLJjygV.problem: Existing benchmarks do not test whether coding agents deliver agents that faithfully satisfy a user's full natural-language requirement.
5f7tLJjygV.method: AgentSWE provides 25 commission-style tasks across three lifecycle stages, freezing submissions and grading hidden cases with requirement-derived rubrics and hard gates.
5f7tLJjygV.key_idea: Held-out requirement cases separate demonstrated behavior on illustrative examples from delivered agent behavior.
5f7tLJjygV.evidence: A range of coding agents, models, and harnesses is evaluated across creation, editing, and optimization, followed by failure-trajectory analysis.
5f7tLJjygV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that frozen submissions, hidden cases, and fixed runtime models provide a clean protocol for measuring requirement fulfillment.
5f7tLJjygV.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite thin evidence and uncertain solvability due to 25 tasks, six cases per task, and no reference implementation or human baseline.

u9tJQvDHx4.one_liner: Activation patching reveals irrelevant facts redirect transformer answers through attention query-key selection.
u9tJQvDHx4.problem: A true relation about the wrong entity can steer a transformer toward an incorrect suggested answer in two-step reasoning.
u9tJQvDHx4.method: The equal-function test varies a false witness while preserving all correct answers, and Q/K/V activation patching separates entity selection from answer retrieval.
u9tJQvDHx4.key_idea: Query–key attention selects the irrelevant entity, whose value vector supplies the incorrect suggested answer.
u9tJQvDHx4.evidence: Controlled random-function tasks train two-layer transformers across seeds and test prompt changes, causal interventions, and training dynamics.
u9tJQvDHx4.claimed_gains: Adding a false witness doubles predictions following the incorrect suggestion, from 27.4% to 54.8%.
u9tJQvDHx4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the equal-function control cleanly isolates the phenomenon and that Q/K/V patching gives a clear mechanistic account.
u9tJQvDHx4.main_concern: Reviewers most often question relevance to modern language models because experiments use small synthetic two-layer transformers without next-token pretraining.

BAGMWyIj3J.one_liner: Sibling Transfer audits source membership through likelihood changes on independently regenerated synthetic siblings.
BAGMWyIj3J.problem: Synthetic descendants can carry source information into fine-tuning even when original records and actual descendants remain hidden.
BAGMWyIj3J.method: Source-grounded QA probes measure calibrated likelihood changes on independently regenerated siblings, using base or multiple reference models to detect the Sibling Transfer Effect.
BAGMWyIj3J.key_idea: Member sources produce more favorable likelihood shifts on fresh sibling probes than nonmember sources after descendant fine-tuning.
BAGMWyIj3J.evidence: Experiments span eight model families on Enron and BillSum, generator mismatch, exact-match removal, dilution, repeated runs, and three non-QA synthetic forms.
BAGMWyIj3J.claimed_gains: Five-reference calibration achieves mean AUCs of 0.9240 and 0.9477 with matched generators and 0.8328 and 0.8504 under generator mismatch on Enron and BillSum.
BAGMWyIj3J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that source-level auditing addresses an important privacy problem and that exact-match removal and sibling-shuffling controls support the mechanism.
BAGMWyIj3J.main_concern: Reviewers most often question realism because training uses only one source-grounded synthetic transformation rather than mixed data or longer transformation chains.

DpdYBWQcrV.one_liner: CTBench uses zero-Bayes-error copy tasks to expose cross-channel retrieval failures in forecasters.
DpdYBWQcrV.problem: Aggregate errors on real forecasting benchmarks hide whether models retrieve and preserve delayed cross-channel dependencies.
DpdYBWQcrV.method: CTBench places the correct target in the input under pure-copy, daily-switching, and rotating-switching rules, then diagnoses failures with linear references, routing interventions, and normalization changes.
DpdYBWQcrV.key_idea: Known copy rules with zero Bayes error turn forecasting errors into interpretable retrieval and routing failures.
DpdYBWQcrV.evidence: Controlled comparisons include Ridge, persistence, Vanilla Transformer, iTransformer, oracle routing, Jacobian analyses, and layer-wise probes.
DpdYBWQcrV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exact solutions and simple references make errors interpretable and that routing and normalization analyses add mechanistic insight.
DpdYBWQcrV.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite narrow task coverage and sensitivity to shared training choices, with fixed delays and one main source-path pair.

zpXMAB7b1x.one_liner: SACQ combines structure-aware codebooks, action-sensitive bit allocation, and refinement for 1.5-bit VLAs.
zpXMAB7b1x.problem: Ultra-low-bit post-training quantization inherited from language models degrades VLA policies and ignores downstream action sensitivity.
zpXMAB7b1x.method: SACQ fits codebooks with role-specific quadratic metrics, allocates bits by final-action error, and refines indices, codebooks, and scales with second-order compensation and action calibration.
zpXMAB7b1x.key_idea: Downstream action error guides precision allocation and calibration instead of relying only on layer-wise weight reconstruction.
zpXMAB7b1x.evidence: GR00T N1.7 experiments cover four LIBERO suites and SimplER, with weight-only, activation-quantized, and low-precision-attention configurations.
zpXMAB7b1x.claimed_gains: SACQ achieves 93.85% average LIBERO success at 1.5 bits with 4.83× lower memory, and retains 93.55% success with INT8 activations and low-precision attention while running 1.51× faster than BF16.
zpXMAB7b1x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that action-sensitive quantization is well motivated and preserves near-BF16 success with substantial memory savings.
zpXMAB7b1x.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that ablations do not isolate structure-aware fitting because refinement contributes most of the preserved accuracy and baseline refinements are missing.

wJj72U5Qxo.one_liner: A hybrid plug-in and score-function gradient trains predict-then-optimize policies from partial feedback.
wJj72U5Qxo.problem: Decision-focused learning for contextual linear optimization usually assumes offline data with fully observed cost vectors.
wJj72U5Qxo.method: A stochastic policy samples cost predictions and solves downstream optimization, while an online nuisance model estimates latent costs and supplies a plug-in gradient mixed with an unbiased score-function gradient.
wJj72U5Qxo.key_idea: Differentiating the downstream optimizer at an online nuisance estimate turns partial feedback into decision-focused policy updates.
wJj72U5Qxo.evidence: The paper proves a policy-gradient norm bound and evaluates top-k selection, shortest path, combinatorial pricing, and energy scheduling under multiple feedback regimes.
wJj72U5Qxo.claimed_gains: The method proves an O(T^-1/2) bound on the average squared policy-gradient norm over T iterations.
wJj72U5Qxo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the online partial-feedback setting is useful and that four benchmarks and gradient ablations provide broad evidence.
wJj72U5Qxo.main_concern: Reviewers most often find no consistent benefit from mixing gradients because the plug-in-only variant often matches or beats the hybrid.

8wXIs8JFoD.one_liner: CMDS learns stochastic controls that coordinate frozen diffusion models into coherent structured generators.
8wXIs8JFoD.problem: Single generative models must learn both component distributions and interactions instead of reusing independently trained component generators.
8wXIs8JFoD.method: CMDS formulates coordination as stochastic optimal control, balancing assembly-level reward against deviations from pretrained reverse dynamics and amortizing the learned control across task instances.
8wXIs8JFoD.key_idea: A learned control steers frozen component reverse processes jointly without retraining the component diffusion models.
8wXIs8JFoD.evidence: Experiments cover an oracle target distribution, spatial constraints, source separation, maze navigation, articulated robot planning, and text-conditioned human motion.
8wXIs8JFoD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that coordinating frozen generators is practical and that experiments demonstrate the recipe across varied domains.
8wXIs8JFoD.main_concern: Reviewers most often find baseline comparisons incomplete and note that added reward-gradient guidance, rather than the base control, drives some gains.

7Idfb1oBwM.one_liner: PIRA computes per-query router biases to suppress risk-amplifying MoE experts with input-scaled strength.
7Idfb1oBwM.problem: MoE safety intervention must identify different risky experts and calibrate suppression separately for each input.
7Idfb1oBwM.method: PIRA uses safety-score gradients with respect to router logits to identify experts and an input-risk score to set a fixed negative router bias after one forward-backward probe.
7Idfb1oBwM.key_idea: Per-input router-logit gradients select risk-amplifying experts, while an input-risk estimate controls suppression strength without weight updates.
7Idfb1oBwM.evidence: Experiments span three MoE backbones, multiple attack families, helpfulness tests, held-out attacks, and suppression-versus-amplification ablations.
7Idfb1oBwM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that query-adaptive expert suppression is well matched to MoE routing and preserves relatively high benign answer rates.
7Idfb1oBwM.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite limited attack coverage, especially adaptive, multi-turn, multilingual, and broader-distribution evaluations.

vlb78MS8n5.one_liner: LCM routes complete domain terms to external memory and injects them at selected Transformer depths.
vlb78MS8n5.problem: Shared LLM parameters inefficiently store fragmented, long-tailed, evolving domain terminology alongside general reasoning.
vlb78MS8n5.method: LCM recognizes variable-length domain terms through deterministic longest-span routing and injects retrieved lexical representations through depth-specific interfaces without changing the tokenizer or backbone.
vlb78MS8n5.key_idea: Full-term lexical routing bypasses subtoken composition and supplies external domain memory through hierarchical conditional injection.
vlb78MS8n5.evidence: Experiments cover medicine, law, and chemistry on 0.5B–1.5B backbones, with Engram controls, RAG combinations, and interface and retrofitting ablations.
vlb78MS8n5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that external lexical adaptation is practical and supported by consistent multi-domain results and useful controls.
vlb78MS8n5.main_concern: Reviewers most often question general applicability because evaluation stops at 1.5B parameters and does not directly test the subtoken-fragmentation assumption.

NG6Pa93AjW.one_liner: Replaces direct cross-party feature alignment in label-scarce vertical federated learning with learnable heterogeneity-aware meta-prototypes.
NG6Pa93AjW.problem: Self-supervised vertical federated learning enforces rigid cross-participant alignment that causes representation collapse and high communication overhead.
NG6Pa93AjW.method: HAMPL introduces learnable meta-prototypes as intermediaries across two pre-training stages, enabling participants to share generalizable structure while preserving participant-specific feature semantics without frequent representation exchanges.
NG6Pa93AjW.key_idea: Uses learnable meta-prototypes as shared intermediaries so VFL participants learn common structure without rigid representation alignment.
NG6Pa93AjW.evidence: Evaluates under label scarcity and low aligned-sample overlap with ablations on aligned-sample ratio, privacy, and efficiency.
NG6Pa93AjW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the meta-prototype design well motivated for label-scarce VFL and appreciate the multi-perspective ablations.
NG6Pa93AjW.main_concern: Representation-collapse claims lack quantitative metrics, recent VFL baselines are missing, and prototype sensitivity/communication costs are under-analyzed.

gePRHcGIMt.one_liner: Probes whether LLMs transfer latent relational graphs across domains using programmatically generated four-way structural matching tasks.
gePRHcGIMt.problem: It remains unclear whether LLMs genuinely abstract relational structures from natural language and transfer them across entities and domains.
gePRHcGIMt.method: INSTILL constructs tasks from five cognitive-science structure families grounded into nine spatial, social, comparative, and temporal domains. Models must match a reference context to one of four candidates sharing its latent graph under congruent or incongruent semantics.
gePRHcGIMt.key_idea: Tests cross-domain structural abstraction by matching latent relational graphs embedded in semantically congruent or incongruent text scenarios.
gePRHcGIMt.evidence: Evaluates recent LLMs across varying structure sizes, families, and domain-congruency conditions with human audits.
gePRHcGIMt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled congruent/incongruent design and programmatic generation for probing cognitive structural transfer.
gePRHcGIMt.main_concern: Multiple-choice graph matching may be solved via local hub heuristics or explicit graph-matching prompts, and novelty over prior ReCogLab work appears incremental.

PukeDiG9L5.one_liner: Improves LZW-based dynamic token compression via decoupled I/O hyper-encoders, size-aware RoPE, digit protection, and multi-view evaluation.
PukeDiG9L5.problem: LZW dynamic-vocabulary token compression (zip2zip) degrades LLM perplexity and mathematical reasoning without modifying base weights.
PukeDiG9L5.method: zip2zip++ unties input and output dynamic embedding hyper-encoders, adjusts RoPE positions for multi-token spans, prevents LZW merges over digits, and evaluates likelihood across equivalent segmentations via multi-view decoding.
PukeDiG9L5.key_idea: Decouples input/output dynamic embeddings and adds span-aware RoPE and digit-merge protection to close LZW token-compression quality loss.
PukeDiG9L5.evidence: Evaluates perplexity and mathematical/code reasoning across four model scales with component ablations.
PukeDiG9L5.claimed_gains: Closes roughly half the quality gap between zip2zip and the uncompressed baseline across four models (exact numbers not stated in abstract).
PukeDiG9L5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the diagnostic analysis of embedding asymmetry, digit sensitivity, and multi-view segmentation evaluation.
PukeDiG9L5.main_concern: End-to-end decoding latency is unmeasured despite added hyper-encoder overhead, training drops high-compression windows unevenly, and HumanEval/IFEval drop at 14B.

tHa5utCpYa.one_liner: Audits eleven interactive-agent benchmarks using a Temporal Contract Specification to expose how think-time accounting alters scores.
tHa5utCpYa.problem: Interactive-agent benchmarks inconsistently handle what happens while an agent thinks, hiding whether world state advances, timers charge latency, or delays expire tasks.
tHa5utCpYa.method: The authors define the Temporal Contract Specification (TCS) along three axes (world progression, interval charging, time effects), audit eleven benchmark suites, and run controlled delay and closed-loop probes on MiniWoB++, RealtimeGym Freeway, and AndroidWorld.
tHa5utCpYa.key_idea: Formalize benchmark think-time semantics along three orthogonal axes and inject controlled latency swaps to measure how timer contracts shift agent outcomes.
tHa5utCpYa.evidence: Audits of eleven suites and controlled probes on MiniWoB++, RealtimeGym Freeway, and AndroidWorld support the findings.
tHa5utCpYa.claimed_gains: In MiniWoB++, swapping only timer accounting moves the official score by 0.185 at a two-second delay (95% CI [0.165, 0.200]).
tHa5utCpYa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that temporal fidelity is a neglected issue as agent reasoning latency grows and that TCS provides a clear, precise vocabulary.
tHa5utCpYa.main_concern: Reviewers note that probe outcomes largely follow from the documented decay/expiry formulas by construction and that the paper does not demonstrate real benchmark ranking reversals.

h2q445S12D.one_liner: Trains crystal flow models for few-step generation using a JVP-free semigroup consistency loss on flat product manifolds.
h2q445S12D.problem: Flow-matching crystal generators require 50-5000 NFEs, while existing few-step self-consistency methods need teachers or costly Jacobian-vector products (JVPs).
