h2q445S12D.method: Semigroup Riemannian Transport Flow (SRTF) combines a standard flow-matching boundary loss with a semigroup consistency loss requiring one large step to match two composed smaller steps using frozen forward evaluations.
h2q445S12D.key_idea: Enforce exact semigroup composition of finite-horizon velocities on flat product manifolds using ordinary forward passes of a frozen model copy without teachers or JVPs.
h2q445S12D.evidence: Evaluations on four crystal structure prediction (CSP) benchmarks at 2-5 sampling steps and theoretical analyses support the method.
h2q445S12D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reducing crystal generation sampling to 2-5 steps without teachers or JVPs addresses an important bottleneck with strong match rates.
h2q445S12D.main_concern: Reviewers note that the semigroup objective is a direct application of Riemannian MeanFlow, the linear step-size parameterization lacks quadratic ablations, and RMSE degrades (e.g., 0.141 vs. 0.057 on MP-20).

YqRKYoZMie.one_liner: Shows that changing only discrete posterior gradient estimators in DreamerV3 alters performance and acquired skills under intrinsic drives.
YqRKYoZMie.problem: The impact of discrete latent posterior gradient estimation choices on skill acquisition in intrinsically motivated world-model agents is poorly understood.
YqRKYoZMie.method: Holding reward computation, architecture, and forward sampling fixed in DreamerV3, the authors vary backward gradient estimators across categorical and intrinsic-reward modules and evaluate agent performance and subtask skill profiles.
YqRKYoZMie.key_idea: Isolate backward straight-through and Gumbel-Softmax gradient estimators across discrete latent world models under fixed forward dynamics and intrinsic drives.
YqRKYoZMie.evidence: Empirical evaluations across multiple intrinsic-drive methods (including homeostatic drive) and environments such as Crafter support the findings.
YqRKYoZMie.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating backward gradient estimation in world models yields clear, practically significant differences in downstream skills and performance.
YqRKYoZMie.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the paper only observes the phenomenon on a single backbone (DreamerV3) without explaining the underlying mechanism or separating representation learning from exploration feedback.

9yMYjHrOwM.one_liner: Uses prompt-selected sparse autoencoder features to build hallucination counterfactuals for inference-time contrastive decoding.
9yMYjHrOwM.problem: Contrastive decoding for hallucination mitigation typically contrasts coarse dense layers or attention heads rather than fine-grained semantic features.
9yMYjHrOwM.method: DeCoS identifies hallucination-correlated SAE latent features via prompt separation, constructs a strong-hallucination counterfactual and reference branch at each decoding step, and contrasts their next-token distributions over an adaptive plausible-token set.
9yMYjHrOwM.key_idea: Steer SAE latent features selected via truthful-versus-fake prompt separation to form a negative counterfactual branch for token-level contrastive decoding.
9yMYjHrOwM.evidence: Evaluations on multiple-choice, open-ended TruthfulQA, and chain-of-thought reasoning across seven instruction-tuned Gemma-2, Gemma-3, and Qwen3 models support the method.
9yMYjHrOwM.claimed_gains: All 28 pairwise margins over four competing decoders are positive with 16 nominally significant at the 5% level, though the 7 comparisons against the strongest per-model competitor are nonsignificant.
9yMYjHrOwM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using SAE features for counterfactual contrastive decoding is clear and achieves consistent empirical gains across models and reasoning benchmarks.
9yMYjHrOwM.main_concern: Reviewers warn that TruthfulQA is used for both feature extraction and open-ended evaluation (not formally disjoint), prompts confound abstention instructions, and margins over the strongest baseline are statistically nonsignificant.

6L00UwtO6w.one_liner: Generates domain-specific planning heuristics with LLMs and verifies their admissibility and grounding in Lean 4 via an agentic loop.
6L00UwtO6w.problem: LLM-generated planning heuristics achieve strong satisficing performance but lack admissibility guarantees needed for optimal planning.
6L00UwtO6w.method: LeanPlan runs an agentic loop (using GPT 5.6 Sol) with planner feedback to iteratively synthesize a domain-specific heuristic, its Lean 4 admissibility proof, and domain assumptions, paired with a machine-checked Lean 4 planner.
6L00UwtO6w.key_idea: Close an LLM synthesis loop with Lean 4 formal verification of goal awareness and consistency on reachable states to guarantee conditional heuristic admissibility.
6L00UwtO6w.evidence: Evaluations on ten International Planning Competition domains and three new domains with up to 57x object scaling against Scorpion support the system.
6L00UwtO6w.claimed_gains: LeanPlan generates verified heuristics and admissibility proofs for all 13 domains and solves more tasks overall than Scorpion on test tasks with up to 57 times as many objects as training tasks.
6L00UwtO6w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing LLM heuristic synthesis with Lean 4 admissibility verification is a principled way to ensure optimal planning.
6L00UwtO6w.main_concern: Reviewers note that the agentic loop was run only once per domain (leaving reliability and variance untested) and question novelty claims over prior Lean-verified A* work.

8evM24Fxu7.one_liner: Models backdoor poison counts and label-noise fractions as a unified cost equation trading off pattern build cost against counter-examples.
8evM24Fxu7.problem: Backdoors require an almost constant count of poisoned examples whereas class flipping requires roughly half the class, lacking a unified explanation.
8evM24Fxu7.method: The authors propose a two-term cost model summing a pattern build cost and a weighted counter-example cost from correctly labeled examples carrying the pattern, deriving four testable predictions on threshold linearity and parity.
8evM24Fxu7.key_idea: Express rule-formation thresholds as a linear combination of a constant pattern build cost and a weighted count of contradicting clean counter-examples.
8evM24Fxu7.evidence: Synthetic patch experiments on CIFAR-10-derived datasets testing all four predictions and parity regimes support the model.
8evM24Fxu7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find unifying data poisoning counts and label-noise fractions via a counter-example cost model an interesting framing.
8evM24Fxu7.main_concern: Reviewers criticize confusing writing and terminology, limited CIFAR-10-only validation, and unclear theoretical contribution beyond prior spurious-feature and capacity-based poisoning work.

P12PcfQgLR.one_liner: Regresses out nonlinear effects of observed common causes before applying linear one-sample root-cause discovery.
P12PcfQgLR.problem: Linear one-sample root-cause discovery misidentifies root causes when observed common causes exert nonlinear or interaction effects on variables.
P12PcfQgLR.method: CSP-RCD is a two-stage procedure that first transforms variables via flexible regression on observed common causes to remove their propagated contributions, then runs existing one-sample RCD algorithms on the residuals. The authors characterize valid additive transformations and prove preservation of the causal coefficient matrix and sparse intervention signal.
P12PcfQgLR.key_idea: Regressing observed variables on common causes before running linear one-sample RCD removes nonlinear confounding while preserving the causal matrix and sparse intervention.
P12PcfQgLR.evidence: Theoretical consistency proofs and characterization of additive transformations are paired with empirical evaluations including RNA-sequencing and cloud-service style tests.
P12PcfQgLR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and addresses nonlinear common-cause confounding without separately estimating the structural matrix or nonlinearities.
P12PcfQgLR.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about limited novelty over standard residualization, fixed-dimension asymptotic theory, and sensitivity to conditional mean estimation errors.

jU4JnWGPVP.one_liner: Weights multi-view graph domain adaptation per view and class pair using cross-domain class centroid distance discrepancies.
jU4JnWGPVP.problem: Multi-view graph domain adaptation methods align views globally while ignoring class-level structural shifts, leaving classes misaligned across domains.
jU4JnWGPVP.method: The authors define Cross-Domain Aggregated Class Distance (CD-ACD) using per-view class centroids to measure inter-class structural shifts between source and target graphs. Class Centroid-Guided Alignment (CCGA) uses CD-ACD to weight view and class-pair alignment during training.
jU4JnWGPVP.key_idea: Weighting multi-view graph alignment by cross-domain inter-class centroid distance discrepancies (CD-ACD) targets class-level structural shifts.
jU4JnWGPVP.evidence: Evaluates 12 transfer tasks on multi-view graph benchmarks including ACM and MAG.
jU4JnWGPVP.claimed_gains: not stated in abstract (reviews note average accuracy/macro-F1 gains of 8.25/9.75 points on ACM and 3.88/6.49 on MAG over SAGA).
jU4JnWGPVP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing class-level structural shifts in multi-view graph domain adaptation is well-motivated and yields consistent gains on ACM and MAG.
jU4JnWGPVP.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the bidirectional InfoNCE objective in Eq. (8) lacks explicit positive/negative class masks and that CD-ACD conflates cross-domain alignment with inter-class separation.

JQwie0bKBb.one_liner: Combines cached finite-difference velocity acceleration with discrepancy-guided step shrinkage for training-free flow-matching sampling.
JQwie0bKBb.problem: Fixed-timestep numerical solvers for flow-matching models suffer from inference trajectory drift at low step counts, evaluating the velocity field at shifted states.
JQwie0bKBb.method: The authors propose a training-free adaptive sampler that computes an Euler update and a finite-difference acceleration update from the current and cached previous velocity using one network evaluation per step, shrinking the timestep when their magnitude and angular disagreement is large.
JQwie0bKBb.key_idea: Using one cached velocity to form a finite-difference acceleration update and shrinking steps on Euler-acceleration discrepancy reduces drift at one NFE per step.
JQwie0bKBb.evidence: Experiments across several flow-matching model families (including RectFlow and SD3.5) and metrics, plus full-vector trajectory diagnostics and bootstrap analysis.
JQwie0bKBb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free, uses one NFE per step, and shows strong gains on low-NFE RectFlow sampling.
JQwie0bKBb.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty over existing multistep ODE solvers, note the lack of stability/order analysis, and observe that gains diminish on larger models like SD3.5.

YHO92Majz8.one_liner: Adapts sender KV caches to receiver contexts without training via KVTrans using RoPE alignment, KV rescaling, and system-key modulation.
YHO92Majz8.problem: Direct reuse of sender-generated KV caches across multi-agent LLM contexts degrades quality due to mismatched instructions, histories, and token positions.
YHO92Majz8.method: The authors introduce KVTrans, a training-free framework for same-model agents that applies rotary position alignment, receiver-referenced key/value norm rescaling, and dynamic attention amplification (DAA) of receiver-instruction keys during decoding.
YHO92Majz8.key_idea: Combining RoPE alignment, receiver-referenced KV rescaling, and dynamic modulation of receiver system-instruction keys adapts foreign KV caches without retraining.
YHO92Majz8.evidence: Experiments across four models on MMLU debate and WebSailor on BrowseComp-EN and BrowseComp-ZH, plus prefill timing measurements.
YHO92Majz8.claimed_gains: On MMLU debate, KVTrans improves macro-averaged accuracy from 59.61% (direct reuse) to 65.44% (versus 64.88% for text) while cutting receiver prefill tokens by 59.14% and prefill time by 57.04%; on BrowseComp-EN/ZH it uses 53.9%/62.3% of text prefill tokens.
YHO92Majz8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multi-agent KV-cache reuse is a practical efficiency bottleneck and appreciate the lightweight training-free design and careful prefill/end-to-end cost accounting.
YHO92Majz8.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the omission of closely related training-free baselines (KVCOMM, CacheBlend, RelayCaching) and the lack of a Text+DAA control to separate cache recovery from generic attention steering.

XcfzmWxvXK.one_liner: Gives deterministic relative approximation schemes for concave expectational functionals on product distributions and proves NP-complete positivity on in-degree-2 Bayes nets.
XcfzmWxvXK.problem: Additive approximations fail to provide meaningful relative guarantees when estimating exponentially small distribution overlaps or Bayes error.
XcfzmWxvXK.method: The authors design deterministic FPTAS algorithms for nonnegative concave expectational functionals on pairs of product distributions and binary-variable Bayesian networks sharing a graph with at most one parent per variable, alongside an NP-completeness proof for in-degree-2 Bayes nets.
XcfzmWxvXK.key_idea: Uses an evaluation oracle and a positive rational lower bound on f(1) to deterministically compute multiplicative approximations of concave likelihood-ratio expectations.
XcfzmWxvXK.evidence: Theoretical proofs establish polynomial-time relative approximation bounds and NP-complete positivity hardness.
XcfzmWxvXK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the FPTAS provides rigorous multiplicative guarantees across a broad class of concave functionals where additive bounds fail.
XcfzmWxvXK.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental algorithmic novelty over prior sparsification work, a large structural gap between product-distribution tractability and hardness, and unclear ML motivation or readability.

ypVb4jfd2V.one_liner: Adds generator-side L2 consistency regularization between intermediate and final outputs under separate per-scale adversarial supervision in transformer GANs.
ypVb4jfd2V.problem: Multi-scale adversarial supervision optimizes each intermediate generator resolution independently, causing spatial and semantic drift relative to the final output.
ypVb4jfd2V.method: CAT (Cross-scale Aligned Transformer) retains separate per-scale discriminators for direct realism feedback while adding a generator-side consistency loss aligning intermediate outputs with the final image. They show joint multi-scale discriminators enforce consistency at the cost of severe quality degradation.
ypVb4jfd2V.key_idea: Combines per-scale adversarial supervision with a generator-side L2 consistency loss aligning intermediate stage outputs to the final output.
ypVb4jfd2V.evidence: Evaluated on ImageNet-256 (B/M/H models, 20-60 epochs), FFHQ, and preliminary pixel-space experiments with consistency and ablation analyses.
ypVb4jfd2V.claimed_gains: Improves 40-epoch CAT-H/2 FID-50K on ImageNet-256 from 4.35 to 1.76 and reaches 1.56 FID-50K in 60 epochs at 1 NFE.
ypVb4jfd2V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the strong 1-NFE ImageNet-256 FID results at 60 epochs and the simplicity of the consistency loss.
ypVb4jfd2V.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains come from stabilization rather than alignment (since unregularized H/2 worsens over M/2), note limited novelty over deep supervision, and find motivation unclear for 1-step generation.

uZHoAOpdn9.one_liner: Detects Trojaned test inputs online across architectures by flagging anomalous sparse autoencoder concept activations.
uZHoAOpdn9.problem: Existing backdoor defenses are typically architecture-specific or operate offline on poisoned training sets rather than flagging individual test inputs online.
uZHoAOpdn9.method: SPARSE attaches a read-only sparse autoencoder to an intermediate model layer, fits a lightweight anomaly detector on clean-data reconstruction statistics, and flags test inputs whose concept activations deviate from clean distributions.
uZHoAOpdn9.key_idea: Attaches a read-only sparse autoencoder side-car trained on clean data to detect backdoor triggers via anomalous internal concept activations.
uZHoAOpdn9.evidence: Evaluations across CNNs, encoder-only LMs (BERT), and generative LLMs under multiple backdoor attacks and SAE variants.
uZHoAOpdn9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified, read-only, clean-data detection framework working across vision and language modalities with transparent failure reporting.
uZHoAOpdn9.main_concern: Statistical aggregation claims lack overall clean FPR/AUROC metrics, and LLM evaluations rely on dated baselines and generated-token statistics.

ItfAw5sasJ.one_liner: Synthesizes stateful executable environments, task-reachable prompt injection paths, and programmatic verifiers for agent security evaluation and alignment.
ItfAw5sasJ.problem: Existing indirect prompt injection benchmarks reuse a small set of fixed environments or rely on non-reproducible LLM tool simulation.
ItfAw5sasJ.method: ToolHazard generates Python-implemented stateful environments and tasks, discovers task-reachable paths from attacker-writable state to agent observations, and builds programmatic outcome verifiers to construct ToolHazard-Bench and alignment training data.
ItfAw5sasJ.key_idea: Synthesizes stateful executable environments and identifies write-to-read task-reachable injection paths paired with deterministic final-state verifiers.
ItfAw5sasJ.evidence: Evaluations across seven models and six attack strategies on ToolHazard-Bench, plus alignment experiments on ToolHazard-Bench and AgentDojo.
ItfAw5sasJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the executable, stateful environments with deterministic verifiers for reproducible security evaluation and RL reward generation.
ItfAw5sasJ.main_concern: The synthesis pipeline heavily reuses EnvScaler without clear differentiation, and alignment comparisons lack external data-generation baselines and full generation cost accounting.

Lah3nHPxAf.one_liner: Guides budgeted LLM discovery with an interpretable design rubric, UCB selection, and a prospective 5%-error-reduction gate for new dimensions.
Lah3nHPxAf.problem: LLM-driven scientific discovery under tight evaluation budgets needs structured representations and experiment selection without overfitting past observations.
Lah3nHPxAf.method: RIGOR represents candidates on an interpretable rubric shared by hypothesis generation and an LLM outcome predictor, selects experiments via UCB, and activates newly proposed rubric dimensions only if they cut error by >=5% on the next five observed outcomes.
Lah3nHPxAf.key_idea: Shares an interpretable design rubric between hypothesis generation and UCB outcome prediction, gating new dimensions on >=5% prospective error reduction.
Lah3nHPxAf.evidence: Evaluated on four scientific-design tasks and four MLS-Bench tasks with Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 over 24-evaluation budgets (three runs each).
Lah3nHPxAf.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest mean final best score in 11 of 16 model-task settings under a 24-evaluation budget.
Lah3nHPxAf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the prospective outcome-gated rubric refinement as a well-motivated safeguard against overfitting historical discovery traces.
Lah3nHPxAf.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations isolating dynamic rubric refinement, UCB selection, and rubric representation vs. full text on downstream discovery performance.

iSppOCNr5c.one_liner: Amortizes Wasserstein gradient flows of KDE-defined f-divergences and quadratic distances into single-pass neural generators.
iSppOCNr5c.problem: One-step generative models lack a unified variational formulation linking state-space geometry, kernel choices, and directly estimable divergence energies.
iSppOCNr5c.method: Gradient Flow Drifting (GFD) derives clean-particle Wasserstein gradient fields for KDE-smoothed f-divergences and quadratic distances (using Gaussian and von Mises-Fisher kernels) and trains single-step generators via sample-based field estimation and stop-gradient regression.
iSppOCNr5c.key_idea: Computes clean-particle Wasserstein gradients of KDE-smoothed divergence energies with adjoint smoothing and amortizes them via stop-gradient regression.
iSppOCNr5c.evidence: Derived first variations, dissipation, and identification results; evaluated on synthetic, spherical, DNA sequence, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet-256 generation.
iSppOCNr5c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear variational derivation distinguishing clean-distribution gradients from KDE score differences and the critic-free multi-divergence support.
iSppOCNr5c.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over clean-measure KDE-KL and MMD flows, estimator stability with 64 references, and mixed empirical results (worse ImageNet FID than Drifting/W-Flow).

eZYeqPZlFr.one_liner: Identifies a linear random-choice mode direction and separate distribution-shaping direction in LLMs to steer sampling calibration.
eZYeqPZlFr.problem: LLMs exhibit strong output biases when asked to choose randomly, and it is unclear whether they internally represent random choice as a distinct, controllable mode.
eZYeqPZlFr.method: Using linear probes, sparse autoencoders, and causal interventions across 12 domains, the authors separate a domain-general random-choice mode direction from a distribution-shaping direction. They also apply LoReFT interventions motivated by low-dimensional LoRA activation changes.
eZYeqPZlFr.key_idea: Decomposes LLM random-choice behavior into a linear mode-switch direction and a separate distribution-shaping direction, enabling training-free steering and low-rank LoReFT calibration.
eZYeqPZlFr.evidence: Evaluated across twelve domains and five model families (Gemma-2, Gemma-3, Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, Qwen3), with causal interventions on Gemma-2-9B and Llama-3.1-8B.
eZYeqPZlFr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the careful probing controls against lexical confounds and the functional distinction between recognizing a random-choice request and shaping the output distribution.
eZYeqPZlFr.main_concern: Reviewers flag an inconsistent evaluation interface in Table 2—where LoRA/LoReFT are scored on restricted valid-answer marginals while prompting baselines use free generation—and note poor free-generation results.

v76Mas4WFK.one_liner: Separates embodied spatiotemporal memory into raw evidence and extensible tools built offline by a coding agent.
v76Mas4WFK.problem: Embodied agents may store relevant historical observations yet lack the registered tools needed to process them for new spatiotemporal queries.
v76Mas4WFK.method: ReSight separates raw keyframes from derived fields and uses an Explore-Distill-Mount (EDM) loop where a coding agent inspects exploration records to synthesize reusable memory builders, query tools, and skills for a bounded execution agent.
v76Mas4WFK.key_idea: Decouples stored observation keyframes from derived fields and uses a coding agent to distill exploration solutions into reusable execution tools.
v76Mas4WFK.evidence: Evaluations on three public benchmarks including FindingDory held-out episodes with frozen capabilities.
v76Mas4WFK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating raw evidence from derived representations and the strong held-out reuse gains on FindingDory.
v76Mas4WFK.main_concern: Experiments test a single EDM cycle rather than continual cumulative tool growth, and ablations do not isolate EDM from direct tool synthesis under matched evidence access.

k3vtooA1ve.one_liner: Coordinates online imputation-candidate weighting and LoRA branch selection using arriving financial forecast losses.
k3vtooA1ve.problem: Missing historical observations and shifting statistics degrade financial forecasting with pretrained time-series foundation models, where imputation accuracy does not match forecasting utility.
k3vtooA1ve.method: COIN generates forecasts from eight candidate completions, weights them online by downstream forecast losses to form frozen and LoRA-adapted mixtures, and uses a second layer to select a forecast or residual correction. LoRA is fit once per scenario while rolling updates adjust only weights, residual states, and scores.
k3vtooA1ve.key_idea: Scores candidate imputations by arriving downstream forecast losses and selects between frozen and LoRA-adapted mixtures in a two-layer online hierarchy.
k3vtooA1ve.evidence: Evaluated across four time-series foundation models and 11 financial data sources, including development and 22 held-out series.
k3vtooA1ve.claimed_gains: Reduces mean scaled absolute error by 2.87%-3.67% on the development set, achieves 1.124 points lower mean relative MAE on 22 held-out series (Holm p = 0.068), and reduces rolling latency by 38.9% via pruning.
k3vtooA1ve.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing reconstruction quality from downstream forecasting utility via online forecast feedback is well motivated and practical.
k3vtooA1ve.main_concern: Reviewers view the framework as a complex combination of existing techniques with decoupled layers, modest gains, and insufficient justification over simpler aggregation baselines.

I9kkaT5o7B.one_liner: Unifies four slide image generation and editing tasks using a 13M-record data engine and a 9B diffusion model.
I9kkaT5o7B.problem: Existing image generators lack slide-native supervision and diagnostic evaluation for combined text rendering, layout, and editing on presentation canvases.
I9kkaT5o7B.method: The authors build a data engine (13M continual-pretraining and 1.9M SFT records), curate the 1,527-instance VisSlideBench, and post-train FLUX.2-klein-base-9B across four slide tasks with parameter fusion.
I9kkaT5o7B.key_idea: Post-trains a 9B image generation backbone on large-scale slide-native pretraining and four task-specific SFT branches combined via parameter fusion.
I9kkaT5o7B.evidence: Evaluated on VisSlideBench (1,527 instances), human preference rankings, external BizGenEval, and SlidesGen-Bench.
I9kkaT5o7B.claimed_gains: InfoVis scores 7.94 overall on VisSlideBench against 7.99 for Nano-Banana-2, adding 1.6 points over the FLUX.2-klein-base-9B backbone (6.30 to 7.94).
I9kkaT5o7B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the complete data-to-benchmark pipeline, strong empirical gains over open-source baselines, and commitment to releasing code and data.
I9kkaT5o7B.main_concern: Reviewers view the academic novelty as limited engineering work, note the fusion ablation confounds parameter fusion with extra four-task data, and question calling image-level edits slide editing.

zRJCi0y6Em.one_liner: Distinguishes permissible numerical drift from training faults across hardware backends using contract-grounded rules and targeted replay.
zRJCi0y6Em.problem: Migrating LLM training across hardware accelerators introduces legitimate finite-precision drift that can mask or be confused with actual implementation faults.
zRJCi0y6Em.method: AlignDiag builds a contract-grounded evidence library of noise, permitted drift, and injected faults, selects role-aware detection rules, localizes divergence, and verifies root causes via targeted replay.
zRJCi0y6Em.key_idea: Combines a contract-grounded provenance library with role-aware divergence rules and targeted replay to separate hardware numerical drift from faults.
zRJCi0y6Em.evidence: Evaluated on 5,861 comparison pairs across 844 controlled groups, plus Qwen3-0.6B localization and H200/Ascend cross-vendor experiments.
zRJCi0y6Em.claimed_gains: AlignDiag achieves 98.61% accuracy (91.90% balanced accuracy) distinguishing drift from faults across 844 controlled groups.
zRJCi0y6Em.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-hardware numerical fault diagnosis is a practical problem and appreciate the carefully calibrated evaluation protocol.
zRJCi0y6Em.main_concern: Reviewers note limited evidence from realistic migration workloads (using small Qwen3-0.6B, 2-step localization, and no newly discovered real bugs) and unclear connection to specific number formats and training correctness.

ZdXOvLFQic.one_liner: Enables heterogeneous LLM latent communication by expressing messages as weighted vocabulary tokens with vocabulary alignment and decoupled training.
ZdXOvLFQic.problem: Existing latent communication methods either require identical backbones, retrain when swapping receivers, or collapse into task-agnostic messages.
ZdXOvLFQic.method: InfoLat represents latent messages as sequences of vocabulary tokens with continuous weights so they are independent of backbone hidden dimensions. It combines latent label construction, vocabulary alignment, and decoupled sender-receiver training so one sender can broadcast to multiple heterogeneous receivers without retraining the sender.
ZdXOvLFQic.key_idea: Representing latent messages as continuously weighted vocabulary-token sequences with decoupled sender-receiver training for heterogeneous LLM collaboration.
ZdXOvLFQic.evidence: Evaluated on math benchmarks and ALFWorld, including message-shuffling diagnostics and compatibility heatmaps.
ZdXOvLFQic.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the message-shuffling test reveals collapse in prior latent-communication methods and that vocabulary-weighted messages offer a clean backbone-agnostic interface.
ZdXOvLFQic.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the two-model system barely beats or underperforms the standalone sender/receiver, and shuffling drops accuracy to 1.4%, indicating the receiver merely decodes sender CoT rather than collaborating.

EhvRgyoKgC.one_liner: Diagnoses whether LLM uncertainty stems from ambiguity or missing knowledge using single-generation denoising trajectories in diffusion language models.
EhvRgyoKgC.problem: Autoregressive LLMs require multiple generations to distinguish ambiguity from missing knowledge, whereas diffusion LLMs expose token distributions at every denoising step in one pass.
EhvRgyoKgC.method: The authors build SOUL, a benchmark of 16,224 prompts across seven corpora and an authored set labeled by uncertainty source. They extract statistical summary signals from single-generation denoising trajectories across four diffusion LLMs to classify uncertainty sources and compare against tokenizer-matched autoregressive models.
EhvRgyoKgC.key_idea: Using summary statistics of single-generation token-distribution trajectories across denoising steps in diffusion LLMs to classify uncertainty sources.
EhvRgyoKgC.evidence: Evaluated across four diffusion LLMs and tokenizer-matched autoregressive baselines on the 16,224-prompt SOUL benchmark.
EhvRgyoKgC.claimed_gains: Constructs SOUL with 16,224 prompts; trajectory signals outperform tokenizer-matched autoregressive baselines by 0.08–0.22 F1 on task underspecification.
EhvRgyoKgC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using single-pass diffusion denoising trajectories to identify uncertainty sources is a novel question supported by the SOUL benchmark and time-axis ablations.
EhvRgyoKgC.main_concern: Reviewers note that headline classification scores are confounded by corpus provenance and answer length, and direct comparisons against prior uncertainty-source identification methods are missing.

K0FEiK0U0H.one_liner: Proves policy-gradient wrong-direction risk is unidentifiable from low-order moments and builds a finite-sample reliability certifier.
K0FEiK0U0H.problem: Finite-batch policy-gradient updates can point against the true gradient, yet it is unclear whether mean, variance, and standard trajectory summaries determine that risk.
K0FEiK0U0H.method: The authors construct bounded sequential MDPs with identical expected-return, gradient, second-moment functions, and arbitrary prescribed trajectory summaries whose wrong-direction batch probabilities differ arbitrarily. They further characterize remaining ambiguity under fixed likelihood information and propose a finite-sample certification method requiring no knowledge of the true gradient direction.
K0FEiK0U0H.key_idea: Constructs moment-matched MDP pairs with divergent wrong-direction update probabilities and certifies future batch reliability from independent pilot data without knowing the true gradient.
K0FEiK0U0H.evidence: Non-identification theorems, sharp ambiguity characterizations, and experiments in ordinary control and rare-event settings.
K0FEiK0U0H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the rigorous theoretical non-identification results extending beyond classical mean-variance limits to full policy-gradient moment functions and sequential REINFORCE MDPs.
K0FEiK0U0H.main_concern: Reviewers note that exact non-identification should be separated from conservative Chebyshev-style bounds, the certification method needs heavy pilot data and can be vacuous, strong failures appear mostly in synthetic rare-event setups, and the writing is dense.

Bk8XXFzlcV.one_liner: Calibrates partially trusted biological prior graphs and trains a mediator-guided graph transformer with subgraph faithfulness constraints.
Bk8XXFzlcV.problem: Genetic perturbation predictors treat noisy, incomplete biological priors as fixed ground truth and rely on post-hoc saliency rather than explicit mechanistic mediators.
Bk8XXFzlcV.method: PerturbDigger performs context-specific structural calibration on a partially trusted biological prior graph using control cells. It then predicts perturbation responses via a biologically-guided graph transformer that propagates through explicit transcription-factor and pathway mediators regularized by counterfactual subgraph faithfulness constraints.
Bk8XXFzlcV.key_idea: Calibrates noisy prior regulatory graphs to cellular context and constrains a mediator-guided graph transformer with subgraph faithfulness regularization.
Bk8XXFzlcV.evidence: Genetic perturbation prediction and unseen-perturbation experiments with counterfactual faithfulness, stability, specificity, and literature case-study evaluations.
Bk8XXFzlcV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate treating biological priors as partially trusted and context-calibrated, using explicit TF/pathway mediators for intrinsic interpretability, and strong predictive accuracy.
Bk8XXFzlcV.main_concern: Reviewers argue that biological validation is partly circular against the input priors without wet-lab confirmation or a prior-only explanation baseline, and that baseline calibration fairness and statistical significance are underspecified.

nYwpIMfmvD.one_liner: Weights causal-versus-non-causal subgraph contrast by full-graph loss to mitigate cue discordance in graph OOD generalization.
nYwpIMfmvD.problem: Non-causal graph subgraphs can generalize across samples and emit predictive cues that directly conflict with causal subgraphs, causing OOD misclassifications.
nYwpIMfmvD.method: The authors define cue discordance and establish the Discordance-Conditioned Causal Contrast (D3C) criterion showing relative risk separation between causal and non-causal subgraphs. They propose DCS, which uses full-graph classification loss as a proxy for latent discordance strength to adaptively enforce a larger predictive margin for candidate causal subgraphs.
nYwpIMfmvD.key_idea: Uses full-graph classification risk as an observable proxy for cue discordance to adaptively weight the predictive contrast between candidate causal and complementary subgraphs.
nYwpIMfmvD.evidence: Theoretical D3C risk-separation analysis and graph OOD experiments including controlled discordance-ratio sweeps on Motif and CMNIST.
nYwpIMfmvD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clear problem formulation of cue discordance, the simple environment-free training objective, and the controlled empirical correlation between discordance ratio and accuracy.
nYwpIMfmvD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether full-graph loss isolates cue discordance from general sample difficulty, whether training sets actually contain sufficient discordant samples, and whether the objective guarantees causal identification.

g2SwJTAEgO.one_liner: Fits a signed source-to-target transfer map from fine-tuning runs to select helpful instruction-tuning task mixtures.
g2SwJTAEgO.problem: Instruction-tuning heuristics assume adding tasks never hurts or that task transfer is symmetric, failing when source tasks interfere asymmetrically under a fixed budget.
g2SwJTAEgO.method: The authors introduce the transfer map, a signed estimate of how much each source task helps or hurts a held-out target task drawn from the same corpus. Fitted across fine-tuning runs, the map predicts unseen mixture accuracy and selects scale-transferable mixtures that drop interfering tasks.
g2SwJTAEgO.key_idea: Estimates a signed directed source-target transfer matrix from fine-tuning runs to predict unseen mixture performance and prune negatively interfering tasks across model scales.
g2SwJTAEgO.evidence: Hundreds of fine-tuning runs on Qwen3 and Mistral models (0.6B–32B) with prospective evaluations recorded before runs on held-out reasoning targets.
g2SwJTAEgO.claimed_gains: Prospective transfer-map predictions have less than half the error of a mixture-agnostic baseline on unseen mixtures, and map-selected mixtures raise accuracy on reasoning targets by up to 14 percentage points.
g2SwJTAEgO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear motivation, crisp asymmetric-transfer findings, multi-scale transfer across two model families, and prospective evaluation protocol.
g2SwJTAEgO.main_concern: Reviewers question reliance on automated embedding-similarity scoring against GPT-5-mini references without human validation, non-target accuracy drops (-2.40 pp), and unclear incremental gain over simpler selection baselines.

ixiOWyKx03.one_liner: Jointly routes queries across model-defense pairs using risk gating and introduces the S^2-Bench safety-cost benchmark.
ixiOWyKx03.problem: Decoupling multi-LLM routing from fixed safety defenses wastes compute and degrades benign quality while under-protecting against complex adversarial attacks.
ixiOWyKx03.method: The authors create S^2-Bench with 1.4 million labeled outcomes across 10 models, 16 attack settings, and 16 composite defenses. They propose SafeRouter, which applies a risk gate to route low-risk queries for quality and high-risk queries to the lowest-cost predicted-safe model-defense configuration.
ixiOWyKx03.key_idea: Extends multi-LLM routing to joint model-defense pairs via a query risk gate that prioritizes quality for benign traffic and minimum-cost predicted-safe defenses for risky queries.
ixiOWyKx03.evidence: S^2-Bench dataset (1.4M outcomes across 10 models, 16 attacks, 16 defenses) and held-out attack evaluations of SafeRouter.
ixiOWyKx03.claimed_gains: On held-out attack methods, SafeRouter achieves a 0.35% attack success rate.
ixiOWyKx03.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly optimizing model routing and defense selection is well-motivated and that S^2-Bench enables systematic safety-cost analysis.
ixiOWyKx03.main_concern: Reviewers highlight the lack of adaptive attacks targeting the router/risk gate and note that benign test queries are easily separable from jailbreak probes, leaving over-refusal on benign-looking adversarial-style prompts untested.

h3fforGrGa.one_liner: Learns train-time continuous weight scaling and binary gates via auxiliary networks folded offline into pruned dense LLMs.
h3fforGrGa.problem: Fixed-architecture LLMs contain substantial parameter and compute redundancy, while train-time structural pruning often requires auxiliary inference modules or premature hard pruning.
h3fforGrGa.method: GliaLLM introduces Astrocyte Net (AS-Net) and Microglia Net (MG-Net) to learn layer- and projection-specific continuous scaling factors and binary gates from linear-layer weights via three-stage alternating optimization. After training, these signals are folded offline into the backbone to export a static, hardware-compatible pruned dense subnetwork.
h3fforGrGa.key_idea: Alternates LLM weight updates with auxiliary scaling and binary-gating networks whose modulation signals are folded offline into a static pruned dense subnetwork.
h3fforGrGa.evidence: Pretraining/pruning experiments on a Llama-style-1.1B baseline and multiple model sizes across six benchmarks, plus RTX 3090 memory, TTFT, and latency measurements.
h3fforGrGa.claimed_gains: Relative to the pretrained Llama-style-1.1B baseline, GliaLLM achieves a 23.1% parameter reduction ratio with a 0.006 decrease in aggregate acc_norm across six benchmarks.
h3fforGrGa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that auxiliary networks are completely removed offline to produce standard dense subnetworks with measured memory and prefill improvements.
h3fforGrGa.main_concern: Reviewers cite incomplete baseline pruning ratios and training/compute budgets (GliaLLM uses 19.4% more GPU hours), confounded ablations that shift compression ratios, and heavy biological framing over combinational components.

sDFXLFETs0.one_liner: Restores low-SNR automatic modulation recognition features via a confidence-routed adapter that shifts degraded embeddings toward clean class prototypes.
sDFXLFETs0.problem: Severe noise in low-SNR automatic modulation recognition causes models to collapse predictions onto a few dominant classes through shortcut learning.
sDFXLFETs0.method: LOFT builds clean semantic class prototypes from high-SNR features and trains a lightweight plug-and-play transport adapter on a frozen backbone to predict single-step feature displacements toward those anchors under an optimal-transport-motivated alignment loss. Confidence-aware routing activates correction selectively at inference without requiring SNR labels.
sDFXLFETs0.key_idea: Trains a frozen-backbone residual adapter to displace low-SNR features toward high-SNR class prototypes in one step, gated at inference by confidence-aware routing.
sDFXLFETs0.evidence: Evaluated across six AMR backbones on two RadioML benchmark datasets with latent-space visualizations and training-dynamics analysis.
sDFXLFETs0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing low-SNR AMR failures as shortcut-induced feature collapse is insightful and that the frozen-backbone adapter is lightweight and consistently improves accuracy across six backbones.
sDFXLFETs0.main_concern: All three reviewers note that the optimal transport claim is overstated because the method reduces to class-mean prototype residual regression without solving a Monge map or comparing against OT/adaptation baselines.

CsiSWr5xeC.one_liner: Formalizes pre-onset VLM hallucination forecasting with the PreHallu trajectory dataset and RiskTrace continuous decoding-history early-warning monitors.
CsiSWr5xeC.problem: Existing VLM hallucination detectors either score risk before generation starts or flag errors only after hallucinated tokens appear, missing pre-onset warning signals during still-supported generation.
CsiSWr5xeC.method: The authors define Pre-Onset Hallucination Forecasting and release PreHallu (~85K trajectories and >180K continuations from supported prefixes) to study hallucination onset. They introduce RiskTrace, which combines current multimodal evidence with observed decoding history to continuously emit response-level early warnings.
CsiSWr5xeC.key_idea: Monitors still-supported VLM decoding prefixes by fusing current multimodal features with decoding history to forecast upcoming hallucinations before the first erroneous token.
CsiSWr5xeC.evidence: Evaluated on InstructBLIP, LLaVA-NeXT, and Qwen3-VL using PreHallu (~85K trajectories, >180K continuations) under matched response-level false-alarm rates and leakage audits.
CsiSWr5xeC.claimed_gains: On InstructBLIP with the same frozen scorer, dynamic monitoring raises response-level AUROC from 75.43% to 83.58%.
CsiSWr5xeC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that formalizing pre-onset hallucination forecasting with response-level false-alarm controls and releasing PreHallu are well-defined and practically relevant.
CsiSWr5xeC.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that RiskTrace actually uses three incompatible backbone-specific pipelines (including online rollouts for LLaVA), shows zero median lead time on Qwen3-VL, and does not clearly justify advantages over simpler dynamic or post-hoc detectors.

ho1jSsu7j9.one_liner: Detects multi-view anomalies using hierarchical view- and sample-level prototypes to condition dual-masked diffusion reconstruction and adaptive score fusion.
ho1jSsu7j9.problem: Multi-view anomaly detection methods relying on dense patch-level cross-view interactions introduce redundant, spatially inconsistent features across viewpoints.
ho1jSsu7j9.method: HPMD-AD extracts input-dependent view-level prototypes and aggregates them into sample-level prototypes without explicit spatial alignment to condition diffusion-based normal feature reconstruction. Dual prototype and feature masking encourages cross-view reasoning and prevents identity shortcuts, while prototype-prior adaptive fusion combines view scores using disagreement and reliability.
ho1jSsu7j9.key_idea: Conditions dual-masked diffusion feature reconstruction on hierarchical input-dependent view- and sample-level prototypes without spatial alignment, paired with prototype-reliability score fusion.
ho1jSsu7j9.evidence: Evaluated on Real-IAD and Real-IAD Variety benchmarks across object-level, image-level, and pixel-level metrics with component ablations.
ho1jSsu7j9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that alignment-free hierarchical prototypes provide strong detection and localization performance on Real-IAD and Real-IAD Variety.
ho1jSsu7j9.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate hierarchical prototypes against flat or dense cross-view conditioning, comparisons with closely related INP-Former are missing, and unmasked input-derived view prototypes risk propagating defects.

b8pWQcfAyG.one_liner: Decomposes masked diffusion LM parallel-decoding dependence scores into true mutual information plus a positive self-marginalization defect.
b8pWQcfAyG.problem: Training-free parallel samplers for masked diffusion language models interpret their token-dependence score as mutual information, assuming all masking conditionals arise from a single joint distribution.
b8pWQcfAyG.method: The authors prove an exact identity showing the parallel-decoding score equals the mutual information of the model's sequential sampler plus a non-negative self-marginalization defect Δ measuring how much predictions shift after conditioning on another token's expected value. They design bias-characterized estimators to measure Δ across models and audit EB-Sampler decodes.
b8pWQcfAyG.key_idea: Decomposes MDLM parallel-decoding scores into sequential-sampler mutual information plus a non-negative self-marginalization defect quantifying inconsistency across masking patterns.
b8pWQcfAyG.evidence: Theoretical identity and bias-bounded estimators evaluated on four MDLMs (110M to 8B parameters, including LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B) and EB-Sampler decodes on GSM8K and HumanEval.
b8pWQcfAyG.claimed_gains: Along EB-Sampler decodes on GSM8K and HumanEval, the self-marginalization defect accounts for about half of the local parallel-step cost on LLaDA-8B and over a third on Dream-7B.
b8pWQcfAyG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing the hidden single-joint assumption and decomposing parallel-decoding scores into mutual information plus a self-marginalization defect is an insightful theoretical finding.
b8pWQcfAyG.main_concern: Reviewers criticize poor readability with dense, undefined jargon and note that the analysis yields no improved sampler, with proposed score-based decoding interventions performing neutrally or worse than EB-Sampler.

LUZ4W1KVHH.one_liner: Evaluates agentic CPU performance-critical code generation via PACE using Effective Calibrated Attainment relative to calibrated hardware resource references.
LUZ4W1KVHH.problem: Evaluating agent-generated code by speedup over ad-hoc reference implementations depends heavily on reference quality and obscures how close the code is to hardware performance limits.
LUZ4W1KVHH.method: PACE evaluates bounded coding-agent runs on performance-critical CPU workloads using Effective Calibrated Attainment (ECA), a metric comparing runtime against calibrated computing-resource references rather than arbitrary software baselines. It incorporates hidden input shapes, wrong-code controls, and repeated timing checks across x86-64 and AArch64.
LUZ4W1KVHH.key_idea: Scores agent-generated CPU code via Effective Calibrated Attainment (ECA), measuring proximity to hardware-calibrated resource references alongside strict correctness controls.
LUZ4W1KVHH.evidence: 3,000 runs across five models on x86-64 and AArch64 plus a 135-run x86-64 pilot across nine conditions with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
LUZ4W1KVHH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that measuring attainment toward hardware-calibrated references on diverse CPU workloads with hidden tests and correctness controls is a well-engineered evaluation idea.
LUZ4W1KVHH.main_concern: Reviewers question whether ECA truly removes software-reference dependence or represents an achievable lower bound, and note limited novelty over existing hardware-aware GPU kernel benchmarks like SOL-ExecBench.

PnN3AXO9Og.one_liner: Trains multimodal fake-image detectors with controlled relational-gaze rationales on identity-preserving eye-edited pairs.
PnN3AXO9Og.problem: It is unclear how the semantic content of supervision rationales shapes the cues learned by multimodal AI-generated image detectors.
PnN3AXO9Og.method: The authors build Custom Gaze (23,415 identity-preserving real/fake pairs differing only in an inpainted eye band) and fine-tune FakeVLM with fixed five-block rationales whose semantic content varies between relational gaze consistency and local eye artifacts. They evaluate detection transfer across person-centric benchmarks, held-out inpainters, and a vision-only Effort detector.
PnN3AXO9Og.key_idea: Supervises a VLM forensics detector on eye-edited real/fake pairs with fixed-structure rationales isolating relational gaze versus local artifact descriptions.
PnN3AXO9Og.evidence: Experiments on Custom Gaze, three person-centric evaluation sets (including COCOAI Person), three held-out inpainters, and both FakeVLM and Effort backbones across three seeds.
PnN3AXO9Og.claimed_gains: Rationales describing the eye-region edit raise the detector's decision on COCOAI Person over decision-only supervision by 0.70 (relational gaze) and 0.55 (local eye artifact).
PnN3AXO9Og.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled paired dataset construction, fixed-structure rationale comparison, out-of-distribution tests, and thorough statistical reporting.
PnN3AXO9Og.main_concern: Reviewers point out that rationales are drawn from label-deterministic templates lacking image-specific evidence, and that held-out inpainted eyes leave unclear whether the model learns gaze semantics or inpainting artifacts.

pGpgGywqhL.one_liner: Instantiates user-conditioned mobile app states to evaluate GUI agents and trains them with cross-user interaction rewards.
pGpgGywqhL.problem: Mobile GUI agents operating in personalized interfaces exhibit poorly understood reliability drops across different users' histories and content.
pGpgGywqhL.method: PAIR constructs controlled user-conditioned application states that hold task instructions and app structure fixed while varying user profiles. RePAIR then trains mobile GUI agents with reinforcement learning using personalization-aware interaction rewards derived from cross-user differences in subgoal outcomes.
pGpgGywqhL.key_idea: Generates user-conditioned app states for controlled cross-user testing and optimizes GUI agents with RL rewards contrasting subgoal outcomes across users.
pGpgGywqhL.evidence: Evaluated six mobile GUI agents across user-conditioned environments and trained RePAIR on unseen-user splits relative to an SFT parent model.
pGpgGywqhL.claimed_gains: Agents drop 6.98 to 15.4 pp in subgoal achievement in user-conditioned UIs (8.77 to 22.0 pp for personal targets), while RePAIR improves user-conditioned SAR (+6.90 pp), all-success (+8.33 pp), and overall Task SR (+8.92 pp) over its SFT parent on unseen users.
pGpgGywqhL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-user reliability in personalized mobile UIs is a timely, practical axis and that PAIR's controlled common-target setup and trajectory analyses are useful.
pGpgGywqhL.main_concern: Reviewers raise that RePAIR lacks a matched RL baseline (such as single-user GRPO) to isolate cross-user rewards from generic RL, and that training tasks were selected using baseline outcomes on evaluation users alongside unresolved benchmark task flags.

enYLrnOIol.one_liner: Retrieves query-relevant normal reference images via global-and-patch similarity and scores patch anomalies across multi-level features without training.
enYLrnOIol.problem: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection methods sample normal references randomly even when abundant normal data is available, ignoring how reference relevance to a query impacts accuracy.
enYLrnOIol.method: Built on a frozen foundation visual encoder, the training-free framework retrieves a small set of query-relevant normal images using global and patch-level similarity. It then scores query patches by jointly measuring normal-feature matching and explainability under normal reference variations, aggregating evidence across multiple feature layers.
enYLrnOIol.key_idea: Retrieves query-relevant normal references via two-stage global and patch similarity before scoring multi-level patch deviations against reference variation.
enYLrnOIol.evidence: Evaluated in multi-class and single-class settings on industrial benchmarks (including MVTec-AD and VisA) and plugged into existing few-shot detectors like AnomalyDINO and SubspaceAD.
enYLrnOIol.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find query-relevant reference selection a practical, clearly presented problem and appreciate that the training-free retrieval module also improves existing few-shot detectors.
enYLrnOIol.main_concern: Reviewers flag backbone confounding (defaulting to DINOv3-B/16 against DINOv2-based baselines), close similarity to prior retrieval-based method RAD, and potential sensitivity of query-driven retrieval to large anomalies.

xKSek6dEkn.one_liner: Penalizes latent world models when locally searched counterfactual actions achieve lower prediction error than factual actions.
xKSek6dEkn.problem: Low forward-prediction error in latent world models does not ensure reliable planning because nearby incorrect actions can receive lower predicted goal cost than the factual action.
xKSek6dEkn.method: Action-Consequence Alignment (ACA) augments forward latent prediction with a loss penalizing any prediction-error advantage of locally searched counterfactual actions over the factual action, requiring no extra architecture or training-time environment interaction. The same mismatch signal also guides targeted local data collection for self-improvement.
xKSek6dEkn.key_idea: Adds a contrastive training penalty whenever locally searched alternative actions yield lower latent prediction error than the factual action, and uses it to guide data collection.
xKSek6dEkn.evidence: Evaluated across LeWM and SMWM backbones on four simulated planning environments, comparing ACA training and ACA-guided data collection against standard prediction and random local sampling.
xKSek6dEkn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ACA identifies a concrete prediction-planning mismatch and offers a simple, component-free alignment objective that consistently improves simulated planning performance.
xKSek6dEkn.main_concern: Reviewers question the assumption that factual actions uniquely minimize prediction error (which can fail under stochasticity or equivalent actions), note limited positioning against prior planning-oriented representation literature (e.g., DeepMDP), and point out that counterfactual accuracy is not directly evaluated.

vOrjKtGDRq.one_liner: Projects privileged solution-conditioned teacher distributions onto the unguided student's local support and iteratively refines verified reasoning trajectories.
vOrjKtGDRq.problem: Self-improvement using reference-solution-conditioned teachers produces trajectories that are unreachable or shortcut-leaking for the unprivileged student, stalling post-RL reasoning gains.
vOrjKtGDRq.method: Self-Steered Reasoner (SSR) applies student support projection to restrict a privileged teacher's directional guidance strictly to reasoning actions locally reachable under the unguided student, then verifies sampled trajectories. An iterative refinement loop supplies diagnostic guidance from current failures to improve sampling efficiency.
vOrjKtGDRq.key_idea: Projects privileged teacher logits onto the unguided student's locally reachable action support and iteratively refines verified reasoning rollouts via diagnostic steers.
vOrjKtGDRq.evidence: Evaluated on hard reasoning problems where extensive RL yields pass@64 = 0, with controlled ablations on projection leakage and multi-round refinement budgets.
vOrjKtGDRq.claimed_gains: Recovers correct and learnable trajectories for 74.6% of problems with pass@64 = 0 after extensive RL.
vOrjKtGDRq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the distinction between privileged correctness and student reachability, praising the well-motivated support projection and controlled generation-side leakage ablations.
vOrjKtGDRq.main_concern: Reviewers note the central claim that projected trajectories yield better downstream training is not isolated via matched fine-tuning against raw-guided trajectories, and that diagnostic steers still rely on full reference solutions.

xojclOzNhK.one_liner: Maintains a persistent non-parametric belief state of environment propositions, statuses, and interaction evidence for continual-learning LLM agents.
xojclOzNhK.problem: Non-parametric continual-learning agents typically store raw histories or compressed solutions without explicitly tracking the evolving evidential status of incomplete environment-level beliefs across tasks.
xojclOzNhK.method: Evolving Belief Memory (EBM) pairs task-directed proposition proposal and evidence-based validation with a persistent memory storing each environment proposition alongside its current belief status and supporting interaction evidence. Accumulated beliefs can be updated across tasks and replayed to fresh memoryless solvers.
xojclOzNhK.key_idea: Tracks environment-level propositions with explicit belief statuses and supporting interaction evidence updated via task-directed proposal and validation.
xojclOzNhK.evidence: Evaluated on adapted continual Database and Poker environments across three LLM backbones, including persistent-state replay and frozen-checkpoint ablations.
xojclOzNhK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find explicit, revisable belief tracking a well-motivated view of continual agent memory and appreciate the Database gains and persistent-state replay experiments.
xojclOzNhK.main_concern: Reviewers point out that EBM uses substantially more tokens than baselines (up to ~4.4x on Database and ~9x on Poker) without compute-matched comparisons, and ablations do not isolate explicit belief-status tracking from plain structured notes.

GuWmlr4NXA.one_liner: Bounds red-teaming policy ranking shifts across hidden-behavior implementations using a reference-intervention twin and stopped change-of-measure analysis.
GuWmlr4NXA.problem: Adaptive red-teaming policies that rank highest on one implementation of a hidden behavior (e.g., prompt-injected) can underperform on another (e.g., LoRA-trained) even with fixed triggers and budgets.
GuWmlr4NXA.method: The authors introduce a reference-intervention twin that keeps on-trigger responses while replacing off-trigger responses with a fixed reference, isolating implementation-dependent feedback. A change-of-measure bound stopped at the triggering query yields target-rate intervals and conditional ranking certificates, while counterexamples separate trigger localization from recognized discovery.
GuWmlr4NXA.key_idea: Replaces off-trigger responses with a fixed reference twin and applies a stopped change-of-measure bound to certify red-teaming policy rankings under implementation shift.
GuWmlr4NXA.evidence: Theoretical bounds and counterexamples paired with red-teaming experiments comparing two policies (Beam-Scalar and LLM-RT) on Qwen3-8B and Gemma-3-12B-IT across prompt-based and single-adapter LoRA implementations.
GuWmlr4NXA.claimed_gains: Selecting between two policies on the reference rather than a prompt-based implementation improves recognized discovery on a held-out trained implementation by +11.82 percentage points on Qwen3-8B and +6.54 percentage points on Gemma-3-12B-IT.
GuWmlr4NXA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses an important red-teaming evaluation gap and clearly distinguishes trigger localization from recognized discovery through the reference intervention.
GuWmlr4NXA.main_concern: Reviewers note the empirical validation is narrow (only two policies and one trained adapter per model on simple keyword/topic rules) and does not establish the information-budget bounds needed for conditional certification in the LLM experiments.

5I0NPzT7lk.one_liner: Queries sparse human annotations at entropy-peaked action boundaries and propagates them via directional boundary overwrite for test-time TAS adaptation.
5I0NPzT7lk.problem: Temporal action segmentation models degrade under deployment shifts, yet extending active test-time adaptation to long procedural videos is hindered by temporal span and boundary ambiguity.
5I0NPzT7lk.method: Based on an analysis showing that model hesitation under temporal smoothing creates informative entropy peaks at action boundaries, the framework queries sparse human feedback at key temporal anchors. It then converts local feedback into frame-level adaptation labels using agnostic or semantic directional boundary overwrite.
5I0NPzT7lk.key_idea: Selects query frames via smoothing-induced boundary entropy peaks and converts sparse annotations into adaptation labels through directional boundary overwrite.
5I0NPzT7lk.evidence: Evaluated on three temporal action segmentation benchmarks (including Breakfast) across two backbones (MS-TCN and ASFormer).
5I0NPzT7lk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree extending active test-time adaptation to temporal action segmentation is practical and that boundary-centric querying with directional overwrite is an intuitive way to cut annotation cost.
5I0NPzT7lk.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over existing active TTA/TAS methods, lack of explicit controlled temporal distribution-shift evaluations, simplified two-class theoretical assumptions, and missing component ablations.

lwtx6mANAL.one_liner: Separates latent subsystem propagation from variable-level dynamics via a soft engineering prior for two-stage Granger-causal root cause localization.
lwtx6mANAL.problem: Flat variable-level root cause analysis in industrial multivariate time series conflates subsystem-wide disturbance propagation with local variable interactions.
lwtx6mANAL.method: HiRCA uses a soft engineering prior on subsystem membership to learn latent subsystem states and temporal dependencies, while decomposing variable prediction into self-history, target-excluded shared subsystem context, and cross-variable interactions. At diagnosis time, it aggregates calibrated innovation scores to screen candidate subsystems before ranking variables.
lwtx6mANAL.key_idea: Decomposes multivariate forecasting into latent subsystem states, target-excluded subsystem context, and cross-variable effects using a soft engineering prior for coarse-to-fine RCA.
lwtx6mANAL.evidence: Evaluated on two synthetic hierarchical benchmarks and four real-world industrial datasets for graph recovery, variable localization, and joint time-variable ranking.
lwtx6mANAL.claimed_gains: Achieves Avg@10 scores above 0.90 on two synthetic benchmarks and ranks in the top three in nearly all real-world evaluations, with 16 top-two variable ranking and 17 top-two time-variable ranking results across four datasets.
lwtx6mANAL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find exploiting industrial subsystem structure via a three-branch decomposition with target-excluded context well motivated and broadly evaluated across synthetic and real datasets.
lwtx6mANAL.main_concern: Reviewers stress that ablations only test two-stage vs. direct ranking on the same trained model rather than ablating the hierarchy, subsystem context, or engineering prior against a flat predictor, alongside graph-score/gate mismatches and missing real-data setup details.

zJjespYJGe.one_liner: Probes tool-result misbinding in stateful LLM agents via controlled cross-task replay benchmarks and runtime contextual-binding checks.
zJjespYJGe.problem: Genuine, unmodified tool results persisted across caches or shared runtime state can be replayed into incompatible contexts, causing tool-using agents to take unsafe actions.
zJjespYJGe.method: The authors introduce ReplayBench, which evaluates tool-result misbinding across 19 agent scenarios, 4 failure properties (attribution, freshness, duplication, ordering), and 3 replay mechanisms using independent final-state checkers. Stage-wise localization pinpoints errors in model-side action generation and motivates runtime contextual-validity mechanisms.
zJjespYJGe.key_idea: Replays authentic tool outputs across mismatched execution contexts in stateful workflows to measure model-side misbinding and evaluate runtime validity checks.
zJjespYJGe.evidence: Evaluated across eight LLMs, four agent frameworks, and 19 sandboxed stateful scenarios in ReplayBench, plus stage-wise analysis and runtime defense experiments.
zJjespYJGe.claimed_gains: Finds a mean Final-State Error Rate of 0.687 under cross-task replay across evaluated models and frameworks, and reports runtime validity mechanisms eliminate final-state errors in the evaluated settings.
zJjespYJGe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value highlighting non-malicious tool-result misbinding as a distinct agent safety axis and appreciate ReplayBench's stage-wise attribution and state-checker evaluation.
zJjespYJGe.main_concern: Reviewers question whether permissive prompt wording in the target instruction confounds misbinding with instruction compliance, note that the practical attacker threat model is unclear, and observe that stronger models like Claude-Opus-5 already show very low error rates (1.9%).

4DSWFZTwM9.one_liner: Fits a global linear model and per-query neighborhood residual linear model guided by a tabular foundation model's predictions and representations.
4DSWFZTwM9.problem: Tabular in-context learning foundation models achieve strong accuracy but lack inherently interpretable feature contributions, while post-hoc explainers do not govern the actual prediction.
4DSWFZTwM9.method: TICL^3 fits a shared linear model to a tabular foundation model's predictions, then for each test query retrieves similar training rows in the foundation model's representation space and fits a local linear model to the residuals. The summed coefficients form an explicit query-specific linear predictor whose weights directly determine feature contributions.
4DSWFZTwM9.key_idea: Combines a foundation-model-distilled global linear model with a query-specific local linear residual model fitted over representation-space neighbors.
4DSWFZTwM9.evidence: Evaluated across 386 tabular classification benchmark-dataset pairs (using TabICLv2 as backbone) for predictive accuracy, runtime, and feature-attribution metrics.
4DSWFZTwM9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple integration of global and local linear prediction using tabular foundation model representations and the broad predictive evaluation.
4DSWFZTwM9.main_concern: Reviewers argue TICL^3 behaves very similarly to post-hoc LIME (which matches or exceeds its feature-selection metrics), is both less accurate and slower than the matched TabICLv2 backbone, and does not explain internal ICL reasoning.

8zGHx9G906.one_liner: Decouples K and V cache compression using SimHash-clustered positional-function token merging and cluster-conditioned channel pruning.
8zGHx9G906.problem: Existing KV-cache compression methods ignore RoPE-induced attention discrepancies among semantically similar tokens and compress tokens, channels, keys, and values uniformly.
8zGHx9G906.method: PACT-KV separates K-side and V-side compression via logical token index maps. For keys, it defines positional-function similarity combining semantics and attention responses to merge tokens within SimHash clusters, paired with cluster-conditioned channel pruning that exploits consistent intra-cluster channel-energy patterns.
8zGHx9G906.key_idea: Applies SimHash-clustered K-side token merging via positional-function similarity and cluster-conditioned channel pruning decoupled from V-side compression.
8zGHx9G906.evidence: Evaluated across three LLMs under equivalent KV-cache budgets against token/channel eviction baselines, with runtime and prefill overhead measurements.
8zGHx9G906.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation that RoPE breaks semantic-only token mergeability is valuable and that the K/V-decoupled token-channel framework is technically sensible.
8zGHx9G906.main_concern: Reviewers note substantial prefill/TTFT overhead without clear end-to-end amortization analysis, heuristic merge-bias and hyperparameter choices lacking justification or ablation, and missing efficiency comparisons against SnapKV and combined baselines.

YPEIKoowoQ.one_liner: Aligns high-frequency DCT patch features and applies low-pass frequency gradient regularization to improve adversarial transferability to closed-source MLLMs.
YPEIKoowoQ.problem: Transfer-based targeted adversarial attacks against closed-source MLLMs suffer from spatial-domain feature redundancy and surrogate-specific high-frequency gradient noise.
YPEIKoowoQ.method: FRA-Attack optimizes perturbations on open-source surrogate encoders using two frequency-domain components: a high-pass DCT feature-alignment objective over patch tokens to focus on shared semantic cues, and a model-agnostic low-pass frequency gradient regularizer based on geometric frequency coordinates to filter surrogate-specific artifacts.
YPEIKoowoQ.key_idea: Combines high-pass DCT alignment on patch features with coordinate-based low-pass frequency filtering of surrogate gradients for transferable MLLM attacks.
YPEIKoowoQ.evidence: Evaluated across 15 flagship MLLMs from 7 vendors with component ablations, cross-surrogate transfers, and multiple judge models.
YPEIKoowoQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad evaluation across 15 MLLMs from multiple vendors and the consistent empirical gains over strong baselines like M-Attack-V2.
YPEIKoowoQ.main_concern: Reviewers question the core assumption that 1D high-frequency DCT components of flattened patch sequences capture cross-model intrinsic visual focus, and note limited novelty over prior frequency-domain attacks.

dTNXuZy6dL.one_liner: Adds a direction-calibrated reader and noise-conditioned tangent writer to manage multiple persistent residual states in Diffusion Transformers.
dTNXuZy6dL.problem: Diffusion Transformer improvements focus on backbones and objectives while leaving the residual pathway across layers largely fixed.
dTNXuZy6dL.method: Building on Gated Residual, the authors introduce a direction-calibrated reader that preserves adaptive gate directions while matching the magnitude of an ungated normalized average, and a noise-conditioned tangent writer that modulates only the update component orthogonal to each stored state. Both operate with a single forward pass of each attention and MLP sublayer.
dTNXuZy6dL.key_idea: Reads multiple residual states via magnitude-calibrated gating and writes updates by noise-conditioned modulation of the component orthogonal to each stored state.
dTNXuZy6dL.evidence: Evaluated across eight pixel- and latent-space diffusion settings (including SiT-XL/2, PixelDiT, JiT, LightningDiT, and REPA) with readout/write ablations and overhead reporting.
dTNXuZy6dL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the localized plug-in residual design, systematic readout/write ablations, and consistent guided-FID improvements across pixel- and latent-space diffusion backbones.
dTNXuZy6dL.main_concern: Reviewers note that most of the controlled gain comes from adopting Gated Residual rather than the two proposed components (whose incremental FID gains are small and reported without error bars), and that longer-training comparisons against top REPA/REG results are lacking.

VCkt8k0kx6.one_liner: Combines series-prior electrochemical history attention with memory-anchored SOH training for causal online battery state-of-health prediction.
VCkt8k0kx6.problem: Online battery SOH forecasting is hindered by indirect cycle-level measurements of latent aging and incomplete or unreliable historical SOH during autoregressive deployment.
VCkt8k0kx6.method: EDR-BAT extracts multi-modal electrochemical health features from raw cycling data and uses a learned series-level identity prior to attend over recent electrochemical history. To mitigate online drift, it maintains an SOH memory branch trained with memory-anchored exposure to measured, incomplete, or predicted SOH histories.
VCkt8k0kx6.key_idea: Queries recent electrochemical feature history using a learned series-identity prior and stabilizes causal SOH prediction with memory-anchored autoregressive training.
VCkt8k0kx6.evidence: Evaluated on five battery aging datasets using leave-one-cell-out cross-validation across 22 cells and five random seeds.
VCkt8k0kx6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the deployment-aware causal online SOH formulation addresses a real mismatch between training and inference, backed by multi-dataset leave-one-cell-out results.
VCkt8k0kx6.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the ablations do not isolate the learned series prior and bilinear fusion from a simpler history encoder with scheduled sampling, and that comparisons omit closely related recent electrochemical-attention SOH methods.

c1ZGUNE89R.one_liner: Modulates per-token SFT updates via compatibility-adaptive relaxed policy projections and information-aware projection strengths.
c1ZGUNE89R.problem: Standard supervised fine-tuning applies uniform deterministic imitation to every reference token, risking overfitting and ignoring compatibility with the model's current policy.
c1ZGUNE89R.method: The authors cast fine-tuning as token-level policy projection minimizing KL shift and introduce Modulated Fine-Tuning (MFT), which pairs a compatibility-adaptive relaxed projection target with an information-aware projection strength. This consolidates compatible, informative tokens while applying conservative updates to strongly conflicting targets.
c1ZGUNE89R.key_idea: Constructs minimum-KL relaxed per-token projection targets weighted by information-aware strength to attenuate updates on tokens conflicting with the current policy.
c1ZGUNE89R.evidence: Evaluated on mathematical reasoning, general domain, code generation, and medical tasks against SFT and DFT baselines.
c1ZGUNE89R.claimed_gains: Improves average performance over SFT by +6.96 on mathematical reasoning and +10.8 on general domain tasks.
c1ZGUNE89R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean policy-projection perspective on SFT, the simple implementation of MFT, and solid gains over vanilla SFT across multiple domains.
c1ZGUNE89R.main_concern: Reviewers note marginal gains over strong baselines like DFT, missing comparisons with closely related token-weighting methods (InfoSFT, EAFT), equivalence to detached token-weighted SFT, and unverified assumptions about attenuating conflicting but correct knowledge.

jYLlpt0DOn.one_liner: Splits LLMs into a frozen KV-cache writer and an isolated reader to test whether operation spans store routing addresses and payload values.
jYLlpt0DOn.problem: Prior entity-tracking studies characterize what language models use at query time, leaving unclear what information a forward pass actually writes into operation-span KV caches.
jYLlpt0DOn.method: The authors freeze the base model as a writer whose operation-span KV cache is computed without gradients, then train a LoRA reader in isolation that sees only instructions and operation tokens (hiding state descriptions). Activation transplants and masking interventions test whether the unmodified cache holds routing records and payload values.
jYLlpt0DOn.key_idea: Trains an isolated LoRA reader over a frozen base model's operation-span KV cache with hidden state descriptions to probe pre-existing routing and payload records.
jYLlpt0DOn.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic boxes entity-tracking task using Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B with operation-span transplants, masking, and layer-localization interventions.
jYLlpt0DOn.claimed_gains: On the synthetic boxes task, a base reader recovers at most 0.07 of queried bindings compared to 0.75-1.00 after isolation training, localized to layers 12-15 in Llama-3.1-8B and 14-17 in Mistral-7B.
jYLlpt0DOn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean frozen-writer/isolated-reader experimental separation and causal transplant controls for investigating KV-cache information storage.
jYLlpt0DOn.main_concern: Reviewers argue that training a ~13.6M-parameter LoRA reader cannot distinguish an explicitly stored payload representation from a newly learned decoder over distributed cache traces, especially given collapse on out-of-range values.

oclt7rbbYi.one_liner: Poisons web-agent graph memory with coordinated text-image evidence using trigger-conditioned retrieval and OCR/perturbation post-retrieval induction.
oclt7rbbYi.problem: External multimodal memory in long-horizon web agents creates a persistent attack surface where injected entries can be repeatedly recalled to hijack future tasks.
oclt7rbbYi.method: MemoryMischief is a two-stage multimodal memory-poisoning framework targeting graph-structured external memory. Stage one optimizes trigger-conditioned retrieval so malicious text-image entries are recalled with high probability; stage two uses adversarial visual perturbations and stealthy OCR injection to override the user's objective post-retrieval.
oclt7rbbYi.key_idea: Combines trigger-conditioned multimodal memory retrieval with post-retrieval adversarial perturbations and stealthy OCR injection to persistently hijack web-agent goals.
oclt7rbbYi.evidence: Evaluated across multiple web-agent frameworks, VLM backbones (including GPT-5-family agents), and sandboxed tasks with stage-wise retrieval/action ablations.
oclt7rbbYi.claimed_gains: Reaches up to 99.15% end-to-end attack success on GPT-5-family web agents with minimal impact on benign performance.
oclt7rbbYi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree multimodal memory poisoning is a timely web-agent security threat and commend the clear two-stage decomposition, executable sandbox checks, and multimodal ablations.
oclt7rbbYi.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch with the claimed black-box memory-only threat model—since trigger optimization accesses retriever image/memory embeddings and requires webpage trigger injection—and question the unclear role of graph structure.
