DrNkPCfMKR.one_liner: Chains non-thinking SFT expert creation, thinking-mode on-policy distillation into a fresh student, and non-thinking RL for domain adaptation.
DrNkPCfMKR.problem: Direct supervised fine-tuning on black-box teacher demonstrations degrades general capabilities, and subsequent RL fails to reliably restore the domain-vs-general trade-off.
DrNkPCfMKR.method: BWB-KD follows an off-on-off three-stage schedule: non-thinking SFT first trains a white-box domain expert from black-box demonstrations; thinking-mode on-policy distillation uses that frozen expert to supervise a base-initialized student on student-generated reasoning rollouts; finally, non-thinking RL optimizes outcome performance.
DrNkPCfMKR.key_idea: Separates demonstration ingestion into a temporary SFT expert, transfers it via thinking-mode on-policy distillation into a base student, and finishes with non-thinking RL.
DrNkPCfMKR.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3.6-27B across three biomedical tasks (BioASQ, MedCaseReasoning, MedXpert) and general-capability benchmarks with stage-order and mode ablations.
DrNkPCfMKR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical idea of converting black-box demonstrations into a white-box OPD teacher to preserve general non-thinking capabilities, along with thorough stage and mode ablations.
DrNkPCfMKR.main_concern: Reviewers flag that one model (GPT-5.4) acts as demonstrator, RL reward, and test judge on two tasks, headline retention gains appear only in non-thinking OFF mode without compute-matched baselines, and margins over FKL+GRPO/Base+DAPO are small on a single backbone.

NHSEeACa16.one_liner: Repurposes pretrained JEPA latent transition predictors into visuomotor policies using dual action-query and future-latent prediction routes.
NHSEeACa16.problem: It is unclear whether pretrained JEPA latent transition predictors—beyond visual encoders—can be repurposed directly into robot policies without pixel rollouts or search.
NHSEeACa16.method: LTM-Policy adapts a pretrained JEPA latent transition model via two routes: a policy route with learnable action queries to emit robot actions, and a world route that retains action-conditioned future-latent prediction during training. At deployment, actions are generated directly without pixel reconstruction, video rollout, or MPC.
NHSEeACa16.key_idea: Adapts a pretrained JEPA transition predictor into a direct visuomotor policy using learnable action queries jointly trained with an auxiliary future-latent prediction route.
NHSEeACa16.evidence: Evaluated across all four LIBERO suites, LIBERO-Plus perturbations, low-data regimes, and three real-robot tasks, with pretrained-vs-random and objective ablations.
NHSEeACa16.claimed_gains: Retaining future-latent prediction during adaptation adds a 5.4-point benefit, and LTM-Policy achieves 97.4% average success across the four LIBERO suites.
NHSEeACa16.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the focused question of transferring pretrained JEPA transition weights well motivated, clearly scoped, and supported by strong LIBERO gains and initialization ablations.
NHSEeACa16.main_concern: Reviewers note limited conceptual novelty beyond world-action models, missing ablations separating policy-future vs. world-future losses and a direct V-JEPA-to-policy BC baseline, plus unbaselined real-robot trials and mixed conditioning comparisons.

NdAhQXMNNM.one_liner: Soft-Label Tensor Learning performs continual multi-view clustering from retained soft labels using membership transfer and Low-Bias Refined regularization.
NdAhQXMNNM.problem: Continual multi-view clustering must transfer historical knowledge and maintain stable cluster structures when new views arrive without retaining raw features of past views.
NdAhQXMNNM.method: The method uses a probability membership module to relate current and historical soft labels for cross-session transfer, and a tensor correction learning module that stacks current soft labels, historical soft labels, and the consistency structure into a third-order tensor regularized by a Low-Bias Refined norm.
NdAhQXMNNM.key_idea: Transfers historical clustering knowledge solely via soft labels and regularizes a third-order tensor of current, historical, and consistency soft labels with a Low-Bias Refined norm.
NdAhQXMNNM.evidence: Evaluated across seven benchmark datasets with runtime/memory measurements, spectral regularizer comparisons, and two view-order settings.
NdAhQXMNNM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that retaining only compact soft clustering states instead of raw historical features is a practical continual multi-view clustering setting with broad empirical coverage.
NdAhQXMNNM.main_concern: Multiple reviewers found mathematical errors and inconsistencies in the optimization derivations, update rules (Eqs. 19-20, 26, 29), simplex constraints, and convergence proof.

4D97u6PnpC.one_liner: SLDBench v2 expands scaling-law discovery to 127 scenarios and adds an active replay setting where agents purchase priced experiments.
4D97u6PnpC.problem: Passive scaling-law benchmarks give agents all experimental outcomes upfront, failing to test whether agents can actively choose which costly experiments to run for extrapolation.
4D97u6PnpC.method: SLDBench v2 expands the corpus from 8 to 127 scenarios (selecting 30 hard scenarios with reference power-law R^2 <= 0.8 representing >=1.09e23 FLOPs) and introduces active scaling-law discovery via a replay ledger where agents buy recorded experiments at their compute cost and update their fitted laws for hidden extrapolation targets.
4D97u6PnpC.key_idea: Couples scaling-law discovery with a reproducible replay ledger where agents actively purchase priced historical experiments and extrapolate to hidden targets.
4D97u6PnpC.evidence: Evaluates 7 frontier agent systems across passive and active settings on the 30 challenging scenarios.
4D97u6PnpC.claimed_gains: Across 7 frontier agent systems, median R^2 drops from 0.72-0.75 (passive) to 0.24-0.56 (active) and prediction error rises 1.5-4.7x, while agents spend only 9-44% of the full-pool cost.
4D97u6PnpC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that active, cost-aware scaling-law discovery is a timely problem and that the signed-ledger replay design is low-cost and reproducible.
4D97u6PnpC.main_concern: Reviewers flag high variance across only three seeds without error bars or random baselines, prompt-induced confounding (instructing agents to minimize FLOPs while not scoring cost), and missing comparisons to SL^2 and SLDAgent.

MGgFK0tLk0.one_liner: Bi-granularity weighted asynchronous federated learning reconstructs unavailable straggler models by reassembling neural blocks from available clients using statistical fingerprints.
MGgFK0tLk0.problem: Asynchronous federated learning methods that discard or downweight straggler updates underutilize client data and slow convergence under severe system heterogeneity.
MGgFK0tLk0.method: Instead of dropping stragglers, the server reconstructs a pseudo local model for each unavailable straggler by reassembling neural blocks selected from available client models guided by the straggler's statistical fingerprints, then aggregates received and reconstructed models with claimed model-level and block-level weighting.
MGgFK0tLk0.key_idea: Reconstructs unavailable straggler models by reassembling neural blocks from available clients matched via statistical fingerprints before global aggregation.
MGgFK0tLk0.evidence: Evaluated across multiple datasets, straggler regimes, client populations, baselines, and ablations.
MGgFK0tLk0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find reconstructing stand-in straggler models via block reassembly an interesting angle for asynchronous federated learning and note broad experimental coverage.
MGgFK0tLk0.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over prior model-reassembly FL (pFedHR, pFedClub), note that Eq. (2) uses uniform averaging rather than explicit bi-granularity weighting, and point out missing server-side efficiency measurements and pseudo-model fidelity checks.

6vvzb6nMSe.one_liner: HiKGR learns relation-, entity-, and subgraph-level invariant semantics across generated structural environments via bi-level optimization for inductive KG reasoning.
6vvzb6nMSe.problem: GNN-based inductive knowledge graph reasoning entangles task-relevant semantics with training-environment spurious correlations, hurting extrapolation to unseen entities.
6vvzb6nMSe.method: HiKGR uses a trainable multi-environment generator to simulate diverse structural variations, extracts invariant semantic factors at hierarchical relation, entity, and subgraph levels, and applies bi-level optimization to jointly promote cross-environment invariance and environment diversity.
6vvzb6nMSe.key_idea: Generates structurally varied graph environments and applies bi-level optimization to enforce cross-environment semantic invariance at relation, entity, and subgraph levels.
6vvzb6nMSe.evidence: Theoretical analysis of spurious associations and generalization, plus experiments and ablations on real-world inductive knowledge graph benchmarks.
6vvzb6nMSe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing spurious structural correlations in inductive KG reasoning is important and that the hierarchical multi-environment formulation is coherent and empirically supported by ablations.
6vvzb6nMSe.main_concern: Reviewers note a gap between the theoretical mutual-information objective and the implemented surrogate losses, limited scope (entity-inductive only, ignoring unseen relations), and insufficient distinction from standard graph augmentation and consistency regularization.

kQBJhVXASx.one_liner: Klineage walks expert GPU kernels backward via validation-gated deoptimization to extract precondition-aware optimization skills for downstream LLM agents.
kQBJhVXASx.problem: LLM agents generating GPU kernels struggle to know when an optimization is valid because its required code state and dependencies remain implicit in expert code.
kQBJhVXASx.method: Klineage simplifies expert kernels step by step under compile/correctness/profile gates and reverses each accepted deoptimization step into a reusable skill card recording intent, code scope, validity conditions, effects, and avoided failures. Downstream LLMs retrieve and materialize these skills on new code under the same validation gate.
kQBJhVXASx.key_idea: Walks expert kernels backward through validated simplifications and reverses each step into a precondition-tagged skill card for gated forward synthesis.
kQBJhVXASx.evidence: Evaluated on five expert workloads across two NVIDIA GPU architectures and extended to Ascend NPUs under fixed optimization budgets, plus a baseline audit.
kQBJhVXASx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that backward deoptimization of expert kernels to recover applicability preconditions is a creative, well-motivated idea and praise the rigorous baseline audit.
kQBJhVXASx.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing ablations isolating backward deoptimization, explicit preconditions, and SkillCards from other system differences, plus insufficient detail on the end-to-end pipeline.

ULdKoyAEvq.one_liner: NA-VAE aligns noise-conditioned autoencoder latents with pretrained vision foundation models via a lightweight spatially biased head without diffusion loss.
ULdKoyAEvq.problem: REPA-E improves autoencoder diffusability via end-to-end diffusion training but requires labeled class-conditional setups, whereas direct REPA on clean latents oversmooths them.
ULdKoyAEvq.method: After ablating REPA-E to show representation alignment rather than diffusion loss drives diffusability, the authors propose Noise-Aligned Autoencoder (NA-VAE), which adds noise to latents and aligns them to pretrained VFMs through a lightweight head with spatial inductive bias in under four lines of code without labels or end-to-end diffusion training.
ULdKoyAEvq.key_idea: Aligns noise-corrupted VAE latents to pretrained VFM features via a lightweight spatially biased head, eliminating end-to-end diffusion loss and class labels.
ULdKoyAEvq.evidence: Component-wise REPA-E ablations and tokenizer/diffusion evaluations across three VAE families (SD-VAE, IN-VAE, VA-VAE), alignment heads, noise schedules, and generator sizes.
ULdKoyAEvq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean component isolation of REPA-E and the simplicity and broad ablations of NA-VAE across three tokenizer families.
ULdKoyAEvq.main_concern: Reviewers identify major novelty overlap with uncited Send-VAE (and prior noise-injection/spatial-bias works like DeTok and i-REPA) and note that FID gains diminish after 80 epochs, especially with CFG.
